## Pass 18 — Medical and outpost collision map, with outreach-only expansion

This pass applies current integration evidence to the outreach plan. The mobile route is not a new medical authority, clinic building system, patient list, or diagnostic layer.

### Field 01 expansion — reuse the medical owners that already exist

The integrated ledger records medical legibility and disease lifecycle work under Plan 60, canonical disease data, and an existing clinical-stage authority. The shelter EMP/medical power plan is complete and routes treatment pauses and clinic-power requirements through PowerGridSystem, WaterTreatmentSystem, MedicalPipelineCoordinator, and quarantine behavior. Plan 160’s ColonySystem already includes a field-clinic building blueprint. Plan 24 medical ward staffing and other clinical work are recorded as sealed in the supplied active instructions.

These integrations change the premise. “Mobile outreach” should mean arranging a visit to an existing receiving service, carrying an authorized message, coordinating with an existing outpost field-clinic site, or collecting a source request. It should not mean adding a second patient record, disease protocol, triage scale, clinic stock, or surgery flow. If current ExpeditionSystem cannot dispatch to a relevant site, report that as a specific missing route seam; do not implement health logic in a new route panel.

### Field 02 expansion — boundaries between outreach and care

The route owner confirms whether a party can travel. ColonySystem confirms the existence and state of an outpost building. The current medical authority controls any diagnosis, procedure, and treatment result. Inventory owns all supplies. The communication owner reports message delivery. A patient/health record is written only by its existing owner. A group visit or welfare check may remain purely narrative if that is all a supported route can record.

A service request can point to a site but cannot certify the site’s staffing, power, or procedural readiness. Before the player promises care, query the owner that controls that exact fact. If the field clinic exists but the power, roster, or medical preconditions are not met, the outreach objective can still deliver a message or explain the delay; it cannot pretend to provide treatment.

### Field 03 expansion — outreach sites by existing owner

| Site class | Existing integration to reuse | Possible outreach purpose | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shelter clinic room | MedicalWardSystem and clinic power path | Bring a request to the current medical service | No parallel appointment or patient store |
| Colony field clinic | ColonySystem field-clinic blueprint and medical owners | Confirm service location and ask what requests it can receive | Blueprint presence is not proof of staffing or operation |
| Quarantine location | Existing DiseaseQuarantineCoordinator/power owner | Carry a permitted message or coordinate a return | Do not relax quarantine via outreach narrative |
| Expedition rendezvous | ExpeditionSystem and current map/travel owners | Meet a party or deliver a note | Arrival comes from expedition/travel receipt |
| Radio contact point | Existing communication/radio owner | Ask whether a remote visit can be replaced by a message | Queued message is not delivered |
| Public meeting room | Current site/event owner | Deliver general service information | Group attendance is not individual consent |
| Inventory store | Canonical Inventory owner | Review a requested supply transfer | Stock estimate is not a reservation |
| Shelter archive | ShelterArchiveSystem | Review a permitted historical service note | History projection is not a new patient chart |

### Field 04 expansion — crossover storylines grounded in current systems

**The field clinic that is present but not ready.** A colony blueprint names a field clinic post, and residents assume it is operational. The player checks ColonySystem/site state and then the existing roster, power, and medical readiness seams. If readiness is unconfirmed, the story allows the player to relay a request to the shelter clinic, send an update, or defer. It exposes the difference between a building definition and a functioning service.

**The route and the receiving room.** An expedition returns with a request to see a medical worker. The travel owner reports that the party arrived at the outpost. The receiving medical owner decides what service can occur. One branch results in a supported appointment; another discovers that the clinic room is unpowered or lacks an accepted assignment; a third ends with the request withdrawn. The story does not create a new field-triage path.

**A disease note with an old date.** A community worker finds an old disease information sheet and asks whether it still applies. The player checks its source/revision through the existing medical-text or disease catalog. The outreach team may deliver current educational information if the content consumer exists, but it cannot derive a diagnosis from dialogue. A callback explains that clinical questions go to the medical authority.

### Field 05 expansion — content tasks that exercise integrated systems

- Check whether a ColonySystem field-clinic site exists before naming it as available.
- Ask the current site owner whether the receiving room can be entered.
- Check the roster owner for an accepted clinical assignment.
- Check the clinic room’s current power result before promising a procedure.
- Carry a request to the existing MedicalPipelineCoordinator path without changing treatment rules.
- Deliver a medical text only if its current catalog/host route is available.
- Record that a recipient declined a visit without changing patient state.
- Send a follow-up through the current radio/communication owner.
- Use ShelterArchiveSystem only for its permitted institutional history sources.
- Return supplies through canonical Inventory.
- Tell a sender that the outpost has a building blueprint but no readiness confirmation.
- Close an outdated referral after the request source withdraws it.

### Field 06 expansion — integrated-plan and partial-plan collision notes

Plan 60 already integrates disease information and medical lifecycle; Plan 24 medical staffing and ward readiness are sealed in the user-supplied active queue; Plan 160 owns colony outposts and the field-clinic building definition; the EMP/medical power package has wired clinic power to medical scheduling and treatment. Existing clinical tools include MedicalPipelineCoordinator, MedicalWardSystem, MedicalReservationLedger, PatientRecordIntegrityValidator, MedicalRecordLog, and disease catalogs. Use those owners as evidence and seams. A new UI should surface their accepted commands, not duplicate their responsibilities.

Before promotion, check current partial integration logs for medical referral or clinic consumers. If one exists, send content to that owner. If a previous plan remains partially integrated, document its exact unfinished acceptance; do not claim this package seals it until the owner accepts a specific route and visible outcome.

### Field 07 expansion — outreach navigation across medical surfaces

The outreach board can open a current clinic/service detail by reference, but should not clone its procedure state. A player action may route to the established medical panel and return to the selected stop. Private clinical content stays inside the medical surface and its current privacy boundaries. The outreach summary shows only visit logistics and approved follow-up.

### Field 08 expansion — clinical scope in clear language

Examples: “The outpost has a field-clinic building definition; current staffing is not confirmed.” “The clinic is without power, so scheduled procedures are paused by the medical owner.” “The team carried the request; no treatment was recorded.” “The disease sheet is outdated; no diagnosis was made during this visit.” “The message is queued and the receiving service has not confirmed it.” These lines tell the player exactly what the outreach layer did and did not do.

### Field 09 expansion — performance through the existing service surface

Do not query every patient or disease profile to render a route card. Read a bounded service readiness summary only where the existing owner supports it. A visit detail loads its specific current medical result on demand. Use the current UI lifecycle and data consumers. Performance review observes route queries, service-detail opening, and history rendering under a long expedition list; it does not benchmark a hypothetical mobile patient database.

### Field 10 expansion — corrected promotion gate

The first outreach release can be a route and communication content pack that visits an existing field clinic, confirms its status, and delivers or withdraws a request. It is accepted only after current expedition, colony, medical, inventory, communication, and save owners are named. A new mobile treatment mechanic requires a separate, signed architecture decision. Without that, the plan remains an orchestration/content proposal and must not add medical authority.

## Pass 19 — Outreach service contracts, referral journeys, and player-visible receipts

This pass specifies a candidate slice as service requests, site visits, and confirmed handoffs. It is centered on mobile outreach coordination. Treatment, patient identity, diagnosis, stock, staffing, power, and colony construction remain with established owners. It does not claim a new mobile-clinic simulation is missing.

### Field 01 supplement — a route is a service promise

Before committing the team, the player sees the stop, request source, known information, receiving service, travel estimate from the current expedition owner, and what the team cannot promise. A route may matter even when nobody is treated: it can verify an existing clinic, carry a request, retrieve an accepted result, or explain that service is unavailable.

The loop has five visible beats: review requests; choose reachable stops; prepare a handoff using existing equipment; travel and speak with people who consent; then return or communicate what the receiving owner accepted. Each beat exposes a real command or is marked narrative-only. There is no invisible “care delivered” increment.

### Field 02 supplement — command and result contract

Candidate operations are review request, plan stop, depart, record visit outcome, submit or withdraw referral, request status, and close route. These are design terms; implementation must use current expedition, communication, quest, and medical APIs. Each operation returns the owner's reference and an accepted, rejected, pending, or unavailable result with a safe refusal explanation.

Invariants:

- Planning a stop does not reserve a patient, bed, treatment, or supply.
- Departure is not arrival; travel results belong to the expedition owner.
- A visit can be declined, interrupted, or limited to observation.
- Carrying a referral is not submitting it.
- Submission is not acceptance; acceptance is not completed treatment.
- A status request can remain pending without changing a medical record.
- Closing a route cannot close a referral still active with the medical owner.

If a current API cannot represent a step, remove it from the first slice rather than emulate it locally.

### Field 03 supplement — service-stop content set

**Ridge Relay Stop.** A radio operator asks for a clinic power check. The player carries the message, resolves the outpost via ColonySystem, and requests readiness through current medical/power owners. A blueprint does not prove staffing, power, stock, or availability. Outcomes are confirmed, not ready, or unknown.

**South Track Shelter.** A resident asks whether a family member can travel for follow-up. The player explains uncertainty, requests the current travel result, or withdraws the trip. A referral is offered only through the medical owner and its privacy rules. The person may decline to share details.

**Flood Gauge Camp.** A worker reports illness but has no diagnosis. The visit records a concern as a communication or quest fact. Diagnosis remains clinical. Without a qualified event, the response is to route a request or explain the limitation.

**Old Weigh Station.** A clinic has not confirmed an earlier message. The player checks transmission status, repeats a request only if the communication owner supports it, or tells the sender delivery is unknown. Repetition cannot duplicate a referral or visit.

Every stop has a canonical location, trigger, visit window, evidence, supported commands, consent text, owner responses, failure route, expiry, and callback. Data is only playable where a current owner can present and resolve it.

### Field 04 supplement — linked referral stories

**The Long Walk Home** follows a survivor who wants to return after an interrupted trip. The player carries an approved request, accompanies them if travel supports it, or helps them contact a relative. Branches depend on actual route and communication results. An unsuccessful trip is not a medical failure.

**The Names We Share** centers consent. One character wants a condition private; a neighbor wants it shared. The player can share approved logistics, ask the clinical owner what can be disclosed, or decline to carry details. There is no reward for disclosure. Later callbacks reflect the promise, while records stay with their privacy owner.

**The Empty Cabinet** follows a clinic worker's unreliable paper supply list. The player compares it with canonical inventory or reports that no verified count exists. A missing key and misdated label create investigation beats; neither creates duplicate stock. A transfer callback depends on an accepted Inventory result.

Each arc has a short operational objective, two valid branches, and room for refusal or deferral. An authored positive ending is not required.

### Field 05 supplement — visit cards and route sequence

A planner lists destinations accepted by current location and expedition systems. Suggested order may use current travel estimates if that API exists; outreach cannot make a separate distance or danger calculation. The player can choose another order and can leave a request unserved with a reason.

A visit card has visit ID, request reference, location ID, priority source, expiry, known travel estimate, consent state where relevant, supported actions, return path, and narrative beat. Avoid patient names or diagnoses unless privacy rules explicitly allow them. Use opaque owner references where possible.

The route sequence supports all stops visited, some deferred, interrupted, and no longer relevant. A delay does not complete a referral. Interruption returns control to the travel owner and presents the actual cause. Any active medical workflow stays active with its owner.

### Field 06 supplement — current owner matrix

| Fact | Authority to verify | Outreach role |
|---|---|---|
| Condition, referral, treatment, privacy | MedicalPipelineCoordinator and current medical/ward owners | Display permitted summaries; do not infer |
| Outpost and building | ColonySystem and catalog | Resolve destination and readiness |
| Travel and return | Expedition/travel owner | Request or display current result |
| Item transfer | Canonical Inventory | Report accepted transfer |
| Power | PowerGrid and medical-power integration | Display resulting medical status |
| Disease facts | Disease catalog and medical coordinator | No parallel patient state |
| Objective and callback | Existing quest/campaign owner | Bind to real events |
| Message delivery | Existing communication owner | Use its defined statuses |

This is a review aid, not authority to modify those systems. Inspect current APIs, host routes, save owners, and claims. An active ledger claim takes precedence over this draft.

### Field 07 supplement — one stop, three outcomes

For a blueprint-defined field clinic, the initial text is: “Clinic building listed. Current service readiness has not been checked.” After inspection, the relevant owner returns one of three outcomes.

- Confirmed ready: name only the factors the owner actually confirmed.
- Not ready: show the supported blocker and a valid next request if available.
- Status unavailable: explain that data is missing, stale, or the query failed; let the player retry or choose another stop.

All cards show when status was checked and whether it can change. Text and symbols supplement color. Back returns to the selected stop. An error does not replace a previous valid result with optimism.

### Field 08 supplement — consent and interruption

Dialogue distinguishes asking, declining, and withdrawing consent. A character can stop a conversation without losing unrelated services. Before submission, the player sees what will be sent and to whom. If privacy controls are not exposed to this route, the branch stays non-clinical until the gap is assigned.

Interruption cases include departure before arrival, local refusal, route closure, missing equipment, unavailable receiver, and stale request. Each tells the player what happened, what did not happen, and the next available action. Interruption cannot consume an unapproved item or close another owner's workflow. Critical limitations use text plus a symbol.

### Field 09 supplement — route history cost

Long campaigns accumulate requests. The board uses a bounded summary or page, not a scan of every patient, disease, and message each frame. Details load on selection. Historical visits reference canonical results instead of duplicating them.

Benchmark sparse and repeated routes, stale requests, long history, panel reopen, and restore. Measure actual list and detail calls before adding a cache. A derived cache invalidates when its owner reports change and is never a save authority.

### Field 10 supplement — integration slice and stop conditions

The smallest credible release receives one request, travels to one known outpost through the existing expedition owner, requests clinic readiness, then returns a confirmed or limited result. It does not promise treatment. It proceeds only if each handoff exists and the readiness query protects private data.

If movement cannot carry the reference, author follow-up inside the existing quest owner. If readiness cannot be queried, report unknown and seek an architecture decision; do not add shadow readiness. If privacy cannot be preserved, remove the referral branch. Acceptance needs one accepted and one refused or pending result, with persistence handled by the existing owners.
## Pass 20 — Service-request deck, route outcomes, and referral content matrix

This pass converts outreach into a set of repeatable case shapes and authored cases. It adds no treatment system. The player has meaningful choices through route planning, communication, consent, evidence, and handoff, while every clinical result stays with the current medical owner.

### Field 01 supplement — decisions before departure

A mobile operation begins at a known service base or existing campaign location, never from a free-floating new vehicle state. Before departure, the player reviews the requesting source, current clinic readiness, available route information, the minimum gear already owned by the game, and the latest status of any active referral. The player chooses which request to prioritize and which to defer, with an explanation of who waits. If the team cannot be modeled by a current roster/expedition owner, the proposed trip remains narrative content.

### Field 02 supplement — reusable request types

The content schema should distinguish four request types: status check, message delivery, referral handoff, and follow-up confirmation. A type states what evidence can close it. Status check requires a current owner response. Delivery requires a message owner result. Referral handoff requires explicit submission/acceptance semantics from the medical owner. Follow-up confirmation requires an owner event or a visit that can be recorded by the current quest owner.

Every request has a stable source reference, urgency explanation, expiry condition, privacy class, allowed stop, and known failure modes. No urgency value is introduced without an owner that already uses it. If requests are data-driven, integrity validation checks every reference and verifies that each request type has a consumer.

### Field 03 supplement — ten case cards

1. **Battery Check:** a clinic requests a power status. The player carries the query to its owner and returns confirmed, unavailable, or no longer current.
2. **Return Address:** a patient asks for a message to a relative. The player can deliver only the approved text and receives a communication-owner result.
3. **Missed Visit:** a prior team did not arrive. The player checks the expedition result before offering a new visit; the old trip is not erased.
4. **Cold Cabinet:** a worker suspects a supply storage problem. The player reports an observation, not a clinical conclusion, and asks the accepted service owner for status.
5. **Quiet Request:** an individual wants a private follow-up. The player asks consent and can leave without collecting detail.
6. **Shared Road:** two groups request the same route day. The player compares current travel and expedition options, then reports which request was deferred.
7. **No Signature:** a receiving service cannot accept a handoff without a supported confirmation. The player can return, recontact, or close as unaccepted.
8. **Second Account:** two visitors describe a concern differently. The player records provenance and asks a qualified owner; dialogue does not settle diagnosis.
9. **The Empty Cart:** supplies believed to be on a route are not present. Canonical inventory resolves the discrepancy; no free replacement is generated.
10. **Late Reply:** a message arrives after the route ends. The communication owner determines delivery timing; the campaign displays a callback only when the result is current.

Each card needs briefing, source, supported action, refusal, privacy, callback, and objective closeout. The title alone does not count toward content volume.

### Field 04 supplement — case clusters with divergent play

**Power and Promise:** Battery Check, No Signature, and Late Reply test whether the player communicates only confirmed service availability. The team can finish the route without powering any new facility. Its satisfying outcome is an accurate answer and a documented limitation.

**The Road We Share:** Shared Road and Missed Visit put two requests in conflict. A late arrival can preserve one commitment and defer another. The scenario's branch changes who receives the next message; no hidden satisfaction or health score is calculated.

**Private Words:** Quiet Request, Return Address, and Second Account explore consent. The player can ask, carry approved wording, or decline to share anything. These scenes have distinct voices and outcomes without making disclosure a reward.

**Stock in Transit:** Cold Cabinet and Empty Cart ask the player to separate suspicion from verified stock. The story can expose a bookkeeping error, but only the inventory or clinic owner can correct its state.

### Field 05 supplement — referral lifecycle illustrations

**Proposed:** the player can review the source and ask what may be shared. No medical record changes.
**Carried:** the team travels with an approved request reference. Travel can be interrupted and the reference stays pending.
**Submitted:** the receiving owner has accepted the handoff for review. This is not treatment.
**Accepted, declined, or unavailable:** the medical owner returns a result; the outreach layer shows only permitted summary.
**Follow-up requested:** a new task has a valid owner and date/window if supported.
**Closed:** the request is closed only by its owner or by an explicit withdrawal allowed by its contract.

Every transition is idempotent across save/restore. If the live medical contract uses different terms, use the real terms rather than preserving this draft vocabulary. The journey is not complete until one refusal and one stale/withdrawn path have authored language.

### Field 06 supplement — crossing with current integration work

Plan 24's ward staffing and Plan 60's disease lifecycle are integrated. EMP/medical power integration routes clinic service through current power and medical scheduling. Plan 160 creates colony/outpost context and includes a field-clinic blueprint, which does not assert readiness. Outreach can unblock a missing content handoff only after it names the existing event and destination panel.

Before a claim, inspect each active plan for partial integration around referral presentation, clinic readiness, and route callbacks. If a current plan owns any seam, contribute the content packet to that owner or defer. This plan does not revise medical schema or promote a field clinic from decorative blueprint to operational clinic.

### Field 07 supplement — route planner details

The planner exposes a request list, selected-stop detail, route review, and departure confirmation. A destination is selectable only if canonical location and travel owner support it. A preview lists estimate source and age. If no estimate exists, say “route not checked.” Departure confirmation lists selected requests and any known expiry, but it does not reserve them unless an existing owner explicitly supports reservation.

After arrival, the visit view shows consent, allowed actions, and open requests. The player can mark not seen, declined, observed, referred, or follow-up needed only where the current quest/medical contract supports that result. Every status has an explanation. Returning from detail preserves route selection.

### Field 08 supplement — protection against false reassurance

The interface avoids “clinic open,” “medicine available,” or “patient stable” unless the corresponding owner confirms that exact fact. “Building exists,” “last checked on day X,” “message delivered,” and “referral accepted” remain distinct. If a result is old, its timestamp stays visible. A red warning is never the only indication of risk, and a green icon cannot imply treatment succeeded.

Dialogue acknowledges uncertainty without becoming vague: “The power owner confirmed the clinic circuit is available. Staff readiness has not been checked.” “The request reached the service; no treatment result was returned.” These phrases are localization-ready and can be reused across route cards.

### Field 09 supplement — load and replay scenarios

Performance and replay review uses actual operations: route list with many requests, repeated stop history, one active referral, one withdrawn referral, and repeated open/close. Query counts are bounded and detail is loaded on demand. A route order should remain stable after restore. If travel estimates use seeded behavior, they come from the existing deterministic owner. Presentation-only query timestamps are not gameplay state.

### Field 10 supplement — first acceptance run

A pilot run starts with four requests. The player checks current readiness, prioritizes one trip, declines to transmit a private detail, reaches one outpost, receives a “status unknown” answer for a second site, and returns with one accepted communication result. The debrief names completed, pending, declined, and unavailable work separately. The run is successful only if no diagnosis, transfer, or treatment is claimed without an owner result.
## Pass 21 — End-to-end route: A Day of Open Doors

This worked route demonstrates mobile outreach as coordination around existing services. It is not an ambulance simulation and contains no new patient, vehicle, treatment, staffing, or inventory authority.

### Field 01 supplement — shift premise

At the start of a route window, the player has four requests: check clinic readiness at an outpost, carry an approved message, revisit a missed stop, and verify whether an old referral is still active. The route planner shows which requests have a known recipient, which require consent, and which are stale. The player may choose only destinations that the current expedition owner recognizes.

The experience is about deciding what can be promised during one trip. The team can complete a message delivery and still return without treatment. If the game cannot represent a team through an existing roster or expedition owner, the sequence is an authored quest with no separate crew simulation.

### Field 02 supplement — route day

**Before departure.** The player reviews owner-provided requests. The outpost blueprint is visible, but readiness is “not checked.” The approved message contains no clinical details. The old referral is still pending according to the medical owner. The missed visit has a recorded travel result; the player cannot rewrite it.

**Stop one: South Track.** The resident declines to discuss private information but accepts a neutral message. The player confirms the exact message before sending it. Communication returns delivered or pending; the route card reflects that result.

**Stop two: Clinic outpost.** The player requests readiness. The medical/power owners return “not ready,” “ready,” or “unknown.” If not ready, the player can submit an allowed service request or carry a factual update. A blueprint alone is never treated as an open clinic.

**Stop three: Ridge Shelter.** The player checks whether the previous visit request remains relevant. The source may have withdrawn it. The outreach route closes its own visit only after a current result; the original medical referral remains under its owner.

**Return.** The player reports completed message delivery, clinic status, an unchanged pending referral, and one request withdrawn. There is no composite “care score.”

### Field 03 supplement — choice/outcome table

| Player choice | Valid result | Invalid claim to avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Carry only approved message | Communication owner reports delivery | Do not claim clinical follow-up occurred |
| Ask for current readiness | Medical/power owner returns status | Do not infer staffing from a building blueprint |
| Revisit a stale request | Source owner confirms active/withdrawn | Do not close a medical referral locally |
| Defer one destination | Request remains pending with reason | Do not mark it completed at end of day |
| Cancel before departure | No trip or item use if owner accepts cancellation | Do not charge resources from a preview |
| Return early | Expedition owner records the interruption | Do not invent a treatment failure |

### Field 04 supplement — three character beats

**Mara, the messenger.** Mara wants her brother to receive a practical update, but not a description of her condition. The player carries only her approved words. If delivery fails, the debrief says so without exposing the private detail.

**Oren, the caretaker.** Oren believes a clinic is ready because the building exists. The player can acknowledge that belief and request a service check. The later callback names the exact confirmation that arrived and the questions that remain.

**Sella, the returning visitor.** Sella asks whether the old referral can be canceled. The player checks with the medical owner. If withdrawal is unsupported, the answer is that outreach cannot cancel it, and a route is offered to the correct surface. No hidden invalidation occurs.

These beats are written with distinct cadence and local vocabulary. They do not turn into generic “patient success” scenes regardless of result.

### Field 05 supplement — side quests along the route

- **An Address in Ink:** verify a message recipient and update a location reference through its owner.
- **Lamp on Loan:** return a lamp through canonical inventory; if the item is missing, record the actual refusal.
- **The Missed Door:** ask why the previous stop did not happen; use travel evidence before attributing blame.
- **A Folded List:** help a worker sort service requests by source and expiry without copying private medical facts.
- **The Extra Seat:** ask whether a passenger can travel only if the current travel/team owner supports the request.
- **A Note Left Open:** return a message when the receiver cannot be found; keep it pending and choose a later supported handoff.

Optional tasks alter the route's narrative or who receives a message, not medical treatment state. Each has a repeatability rule and a result producer.

### Field 06 supplement — route evidence log

For each stop, retain only the reference, time/window if current campaign time provides it, owner result, and approved narrative summary. Do not duplicate the medical payload. The host presents a route result after the owner emits it. Save ownership is assigned by the active campaign/quest owner for route progress and by medical/communication owners for their facts.

The integrator must establish that an interrupted trip can return without losing references, that a restored route does not resend a message, and that a changed consent decision cancels only the not-yet-submitted action. If existing APIs cannot distinguish preview from commit, the route cannot add its own unverified guarantee.

### Field 07 supplement — screen sequence

1. Request inbox, grouped by source and freshness.
2. Stop selection with route status provided by the current travel owner.
3. Departure confirmation listing the chosen requests and approved message text.
4. Visit screen with consent and supported action controls.
5. Handoff receipt with accepted, pending, declined, withdrawn, or unknown status as defined by owners.
6. Return summary with direct links to the medical and communication surfaces.

The screen sequence preserves controller back, focus return, and disposal. A stale-data banner stays visible when the player opens a request. A network/communication error is not transformed into delivered.

### Field 08 supplement — role-aware copy

Use “visit,” “message,” “request,” “referral,” and “treatment” precisely. A visit can be completed without a referral. A referral can be accepted without a treatment result. Avoid “served” as a blanket status. The player can review the message text aloud and remove any unapproved clinical detail before sending.

A character may consent to carrying a message while declining a visit. Consent for one operation does not imply consent for another. The route list never reveals a private reason to other characters unless the player sends it through an approved owner.

### Field 09 supplement — repeated route reliability

Open and close every screen several times, refresh a request, interrupt travel, save, reload, and confirm that subscriptions and route references remain singular. Run the same seeded route twice if the approved route mechanics include random travel; compare canonical owner results. Repeated content events must not reapply an accepted referral or duplicate a delivered message.

### Field 10 supplement — acceptance summary

This route is eligible for integration when its destination, travel command, message delivery, service readiness query, and quest callback are proven. It succeeds with one delivered message and one unresolved service status, provided the debrief says exactly that. It is rejected if a player sees treatment claimed, a private detail exposed, a referral closed by outreach, or a duplicate message after restore.
## Pass 22 — Referral privacy matrix, request expiry, and outcome language

This pass gives content authors a consistent way to distinguish outreach logistics from clinical state. It focuses on information boundaries and request lifecycle rather than adding new treatment behavior.

### Field 01 supplement — information carried by the team

A route can carry a message, public service query, private referral reference, or non-sensitive supply request. Each category has its own allowed audience and expiry. A message body is visible to the player before transmission. A private referral may use only the opaque reference and fields that the medical owner permits. A supply query refers to canonical inventory or stock owner data; it is not a local count.

The player should see why a request can be carried and what it cannot contain. If a recipient cannot be identified or consent is not recorded under the current contract, the request remains at its source. The team must not collect sensitive data simply because a route screen has space for another text box.

### Field 02 supplement — expiry and supersession

A request can expire because the source withdraws it, the visit window passes, a newer request replaces it, or the destination is no longer relevant. Expiry is decided by the request's owner and is displayed with source/time. A route planner may hide expired work from its active list while preserving the history reference. It cannot mark the clinical referral canceled unless the medical owner accepts cancellation.

Supersession differs from deletion. The old request remains in the audit trail if its owner retains it; the new request references it. A repeated message is sent only when the communication owner confirms the first was not delivered and the source still authorizes retry. Save/reload cannot create a second submission.

### Field 03 supplement — outcome language matrix

| Owner result | Permitted wording | Wording to avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Message queued | “Message queued for delivery.” | “Recipient informed.” |
| Message delivered | “Message delivered.” | “Request resolved.” |
| Referral submitted | “Referral submitted for review.” | “Treatment arranged.” |
| Referral accepted | “Service accepted the referral.” | “Patient treated.” |
| Service status unknown | “No current readiness result.” | “Clinic closed.” |
| Visit declined | “The person declined this visit.” | “Unable to comply.” |
| Route interrupted | Use travel owner's exact reason | “Medical mission failed.” |
| Item transfer accepted | Name transferred item and owner | “Clinic stocked.” |

Localized variants retain those distinctions. A character can react emotionally, but the status receipt remains precise.

### Field 04 supplement — privacy-aware story beats

**One Sentence Only:** the resident approves a short logistical note but refuses to share a diagnosis. The player previews the note and can change the recipient or cancel. The callback depends on actual message delivery.

**The Wrong Envelope:** a sealed message is addressed to a person who has moved. The player can ask the communication owner for a safe return or retain it until the source is found. Opening the envelope is never a required objective.

**The Shared Waiting Room:** another survivor asks why a person is at the clinic. The player can explain only public service information, redirect to the receiving service, or decline to answer. The game does not reveal a private condition through ambient dialogue.

**A Name to Remove:** a patient asks that their name be removed from a non-clinical note. The outreach story routes this request to the proper record owner; it does not erase a medical record directly.

### Field 05 supplement — expiry-aware content cards

Every request card includes source, destination, category, consent/authorization state if supported, expiry cause, retry rule, and result owner. The content author writes an expired branch that avoids guilt language and gives an available next step. Time-limited requests show their window before departure. The player does not discover after arrival that the content silently expired.

### Field 06 supplement — audit and current owner boundary

MedicalPipelineCoordinator, MedicalWardSystem, and related medical record owners remain responsible for clinical data. Plan 60 disease lifecycle, Plan 24 ward staffing, Plan 160 outpost building definitions, and the accepted medical/power integration remain dependencies to verify. This plan is not authority to change privacy contracts or referral state. If the current API cannot express the requested privacy behavior, remove the branch or seek an architecture decision.

### Field 07 supplement — private and public route views

The route board shows the minimum operational summary. A private detail opens through the existing medical surface with its existing access checks. Closing it returns the player to the same route selection. The public route summary does not keep a cached diagnosis. When the current owner refuses a query, the UI explains that the result is unavailable without exposing why.

### Field 08 supplement — communication safeguards

Before message send, the player sees sender, receiver, exact approved content, and delivery uncertainty. A private referral summary cannot be copied into a public notice. If a correction is needed, the original message stays in history and the communication owner records a correction. No global “consent accepted” flag is created by a one-time conversation unless the current medical system uses that exact contract.

### Field 09 supplement — restore and duplicate review

Review interruptions at every point: before departure, en route, at stop, after submission, after delivery, and before return. Save/restore resumes the real owner references and does not replay send, transfer, or referral actions. If a data update removes a request ID, migration must use the current owner policy and present a recoverable content error.

### Field 10 supplement — adoption rule

This matrix can be adopted as writing guidance even if no new route mechanics are approved. A production referral route requires exact API, consent, expiry, and save evidence. If any of those are unverified, keep the content as a quest conversation without exposing private clinical data or advertising an operational outreach system.
## Pass 23 — Canon reconciliation and the caretaker-hut outreach circuit

Current data already includes a field clinic room, the field-clinic colony blueprint, and the starting supplies profile origin_field_clinic. The player-facing cohort setup passes a selected starting-supplies profile into campaign creation. Mobile outreach must therefore add route-based service content and operational handoffs around these existing assets, not another field-clinic type, origin selector, patient store, or treatment system.

The Works, identified in data as faction_rebuilders, already has a caretaker’s hut clinic, an autoclave, a still, and a floodplain water problem. Existing faction-war content also contains a field-hospital-overflow arc and several water/route stories. Those are collision boundaries. This packet uses the caretaker-hut setting only after content-owner review, and does not recreate Bitter Water, Cistern Toll, Broken Route, or Field Hospital Overflow.

### Field 01 supplement — a route with an existing destination

The player receives an invitation to check the caretaker-hut clinic’s readiness before a limited visit window. The visit uses a known canonical location and current expedition/travel owner. The clinic is not converted into a mobile vehicle; the mobile element is the player’s ability to coordinate a visit, carry an approved message, request a readiness result, and return with the answer.

The first route card explicitly distinguishes the Rebuilders’ narrative claim that the hut serves as the sector clinic from current mechanical readiness. It does not assert that the building is a colony field-clinic blueprint, that it has power, or that it can accept treatment. The player can ask for a current result, deliver a non-clinical message, or decide the trip is not yet justified.

### Field 02 supplement — existing start profiles and service readiness

The existing origin_field_clinic profile is a starting-supply configuration whose description says the treatment room was evacuated in a hurry while medical stock survived and pantry/repair/water reserves did not. It is not a route mission and does not by itself create a staffed external clinic. The origin_waterworks_failure profile is likewise a starting stock profile, not proof of a medical referral workflow.

Before binding this plan to either origin, verify whether the selected profile ID is exposed to the quest owner after campaign creation. Do not infer origin from current item quantities: a player can spend or acquire those items and make the inference false. If the profile identity is not available to an existing quest trigger, author the outreach arc as a normal campaign quest or request a narrow data/event seam from the owner.

A readiness receipt can mention only facts the current medical/power/colony owner returns. “Clinic exists” is a location/blueprint fact. “Clinic can receive a patient” requires a separate readiness result. “Treatment began” requires the medical owner to say that treatment began.

### Field 03 supplement — story arc: Minutes from the Hut

**Disturbance.** A short message arrives with a request for a clean instrument cycle and an overdue return of one ledger. The message does not say a patient is in danger. Its delivery status comes from CommunicationsSystem if the existing message route supports this message type.

**Discovery.** At the destination, the caretaker shows two work lists with different dates. The player can compare them, ask whether the autoclave completed its last cycle, and check whether water status can be confirmed by the current owner. No mechanic is added for sterilization quality or water purity.

**Complication.** A visitor wants a private follow-up but the route request was written on a public sheet. The player may carry a generic message, ask the visitor to authorize a referral through the clinical owner, or decline to move the private detail. These branches do not change treatment.

**Decision.** The player chooses between returning with an accurate pending notice, requesting a supported service, or staying to gather more information if the campaign/travel owners permit. The caretaker’s service remains open or closed only according to current readiness; dialogue cannot toggle it.

**Delayed consequence.** The returned notice changes how the next requester uses the route. If a prior message was delivered, the recipient may have an answer. If not, the player sees a delivery failure or uncertainty rather than a scripted success.

### Field 04 supplement — role and voice matrix

| Role | Surface identity | Contradiction under pressure | Gameplay hook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Caretaker | Keeps the hut’s operating list | Refuses to sign a result they did not witness | Readiness query and archive provenance |
| Traveling registrar | Carries request references between sites | Has memorized names but distrusts copied lists | Communication and identity check |
| Night sterilizer | Maintains a paper cycle log | Will not call a cycle valid without water evidence | Medical/service owner query |
| Patient relative | Asks for a route update | Does not want the condition repeated | Consent-limited message |
| Colony quartermaster | Counts delivered crates | Treats a blueprint as if it were a service | Colony/Inventory status correction |

These are proposed roles. Before creating survivor or NPC IDs, search canonical character, survivor, faction, quest, and dialogue data. The medic is not a new named specialist by default, and the caretaker is not a second clinic authority.

### Field 05 supplement — outreach side-quest bank

1. **A Cycle Not Witnessed:** compare the paper log date with an owner-provided service result; close as verified or unknown.
2. **Message Without a Condition:** deliver an approved logistics request without patient details.
3. **The Return Ledger:** carry the ledger back through canonical inventory only if it is an actual item; otherwise record a source-linked document handoff.
4. **A Name Spoken Once:** ask consent before carrying a name to a second location; no consent means no transfer.
5. **Water Status, Not Water Rumor:** request the current water-owner result and report only the returned status.
6. **The Hut Is Not the Blueprint:** explain that the Rebuilders’ clinic narrative and a colony building definition are different facts.
7. **The Visit Withdrawn:** check whether the original source still requests travel; medical referral closure remains with its owner.
8. **One Seat Left:** ask the existing travel/roster owner about passenger capacity; never add a mobile-team seat counter.
9. **Two Stops, One Window:** choose an order among accepted destinations using current travel data.
10. **Receipt of Delivery:** confirm whether the communication or inventory owner accepted the handoff.
11. **The Wrong Date:** preserve both records until a source owner reconciles them.
12. **No Result at Dusk:** return with a truthful unavailable status instead of inventing a negative diagnosis.

Each quest is a genuine player action or a supported conversation branch. A list of calls and labels alone does not count as a route feature.

### Field 06 supplement — current-owner map

MedicalPipelineCoordinator, MedicalWardSystem, MedicalReservationLedger, patient record integrity, and Plan 60 disease lifecycle remain clinical authorities. Plan 24 staffing and the EMP/medical power integration remain operational dependencies. ColonySystem and Plan 160 own colony/outpost and field-clinic construction; its supply line is not a medical referral. CommunicationsSystem and Plan 157 own network messages. Expedition owns travel and return. Canonical Inventory owns any carried item. Existing quest systems own request/objective progression.

The data consumer and host route for each owner must be verified before promotion. If the medical system lacks a privacy-safe referral API, remove that branch. If route progression cannot keep an opaque referral reference, use a content-only message arc instead of storing a patient copy.

### Field 07 supplement — status card examples

- “Caretaker-hut clinic is named in faction records. Current service readiness has not been checked.”
- “Message delivered to the caretaker. No clinical request was included.”
- “Referral submitted to the medical service for review. Treatment has not been confirmed.”
- “The traveler withdrew this visit request. The medical referral remains open.”
- “No current readiness result is available. You can return or ask the source to check again.”

These lines give a direct next action, avoid false reassurance, and preserve clinical privacy.

### Field 08 supplement — choice and consent presentation

Before transmitting, show the exact message, recipient, and content scope. Consent to travel does not imply consent to reveal a condition. Consent to transmit a message does not imply consent to open a sealed record. A character can refuse an interview without losing access to the clinic. The player can take a neutral action that preserves route access without disclosing medical information.

Every state has a text and icon equivalent. The route is keyboard/controller reachable and returns focus to the selected request after visiting a medical detail panel. A failed lookup does not overwrite the last valid status.

### Field 09 supplement — loop, load, and persistence

The first slice queries only the selected request and destination. It does not load every patient record or disease profile. Active references are stored by the existing quest/campaign and clinical owners; historical summaries refer back to those owners. Repeated route open/close cannot double-send messages. Saving after departure and restoring before arrival must not create a second trip or duplicate request.

If a later feature adds several simultaneous requests, use a bounded list and existing indexes. Measure actual query time and allocation before adding cache; the route panel must not become a patient database.

### Field 10 supplement — updated scope classification

This is an EXTENSION of the existing start-profile, medical, communications, expedition, colony, and quest owners if their APIs expose the needed facts. It is not a NEW clinic system. A new mobile treatment authority is explicitly out of scope unless a signed architecture decision assigns it. The initial deliverable can be a questline using one real destination, one delivered logistics message, one readiness check or truthful unavailable result, and a later callback.

## Pass 24 — Field packet for a consent-led outreach circuit

The concrete expansion proposed here is a sequence of care requests carried to and from existing locations, not a vehicle simulation. The player coordinates who can travel, what existing supplies can be carried, what the recipient consents to, and which current medical owner can answer a request. A route becomes playable only if the current expedition/travel owner can take a party to a canonical destination and return a result. A clinic becomes operational only if its current room, staff, power, stock, and medical owners say so. The existing `room_clinic`, `col_bldg_field_clinic`, and `origin_field_clinic` are useful references, but none alone proves that a remote treatment circuit is wired.

The Field Clinic Withdrawal origin is especially important because its authorial premise is uneven: medical stock survived while food, repair, and water did not. That is a reason for an explicit capacity check, not a free starting clinic. Any profile-specific content must be conditional on a stable profile ID reaching the chosen quest owner; no inventory inference is permitted after play begins. The Rebuilders’ caretaker-hut clinic is a possible narrative anchor, but its canonical location ID is unresolved in the current evidence. No route, journey, or `locationId` is ready for authored data until the map/content owner resolves that identity.

### Field 01 supplement — the service loop in measurable terms

An outreach episode is accepted only when it completes a chain of real owner calls: form a request; confirm consent; check existing capacity; reserve or carry a canonical item if the current travel/inventory owner supports it; visit a known place if the travel owner supports it; return an owner result; and tell the requester what was or was not done. If one link has no API, the episode can show an honest referral or a pending response, but it cannot be described as a completed treatment.

| Loop stage | Minimum player-facing fact | Authority that must answer | What the plan must not cache |
|---|---|---|---|
| request | Who asked and what they agreed to share | Existing quest/dialogue route | A shadow medical record |
| capacity | Whether support is available now | Current room, staffing, inventory, and power owners | A local treatment capacity counter |
| route | Whether a trip can be scheduled | Existing travel/expedition owner | A second route graph |
| dispatch | Whether the party and carried items were accepted | Existing party/inventory owners | A parallel ambulance inventory |
| arrival | Whether the destination is reachable | Canonical location/travel owner | A cached “visited” boolean |
| service result | What an existing health/disease owner reports | That health or disease owner | A new diagnosis or treatment state |
| callback | What can truthfully be reported | Quest/narrative owner plus source receipt | A shadow patient status |

“Service result” may be “could not assess,” “no stock,” “recipient declined,” or “source unavailable.” These are not failure states for the player to optimize away. They allow the arc to finish without falsifying the world or silently consuming supplies.

### Field 02 supplement — request types and explicit boundaries

The first circuit uses only requests that current systems can answer: a request for an existing item to be delivered; a request to confirm a known clinic is staffed; a request to relay a message to an existing owner; or a request to return an existing record to its source. Treatment selection, diagnoses, triage ordering, patient transport, and medical outcome prediction are excluded until source inspection identifies the current owner and its public contract.

Each authored request contains a requestor reference, recipient reference, canonical location reference, reason in plain language, consent scope, earliest/latest useful day if an existing clock can express it, accepted owner command, evidence source, and no-service fallback. It must not include a mutable `patientHealth`, `treatmentProgress`, `triageRank`, or `clinicStock` field owned elsewhere. A consent record can be a one-time choice in a quest branch if the current quest owner can persist that choice; do not add an independent consent ledger.

### Field 03 supplement — privacy and consent interaction contract

The player asks permission before sending identifying health details through an open channel. The patient/requester is told what is being shared and with whom. Consent can be narrow: “tell the clinic only that supplies are needed,” “send the full note to the named clinician,” or “do not transmit.” These are authored dialogue choices, not a hidden legal subsystem. Where no current channel supports protected delivery, the only honest options are a limited non-identifying message or no transmission.

Consent is revisited if the recipient, content, or channel changes. Declining to disclose cannot reduce morale or reputation by default. An emergency exception must not be invented as an invisible rule; if the game needs one, it requires explicit design authority and a clear player-facing explanation. A paper note left at a public board is treated as public, and the UX says so before the player confirms it.

### Field 04 supplement — contact and service card workbook

The following are candidate interactions; they do not name new patients or claim new medical mechanics. New characters should be selected from the live roster and narrative continuity index only after checking which survivor arcs are already assigned. For unknown people, keep the authoring slot role-based until that review is complete.

| Candidate card | Need expressed in scene | Player action | Confirming owner/result | Completion without treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A closed treatment room | Room availability is unclear | Ask the existing room owner | Room reports open/closed/unknown | Report the status accurately |
| A request for clean dressings | One listed item is requested | Check canonical stock, then dispatch if supported | Inventory and travel result | Explain that no item left storage |
| A message with too much detail | A public relay includes private information | Edit scope or cancel | Channel confirms dispatch or cancellation | Preserve privacy and close |
| A return visit postponed | Recipient does not want visitors today | Respect the refusal | Quest records the chosen branch | Close as declined by recipient |
| A supply receipt without patient name | Delivery proof lacks identity | Attach only an existing receipt | Inventory owner confirms transfer | Keep recipient anonymous |
| A second-hand symptom report | Source has no direct observation | Request a direct source or leave unverified | Existing dialogue/event source | Record uncertainty |
| A missing clinic key | Access is not established | Ask current access/location owner | Access confirmed or denied | Do not enter or mark service complete |
| A power interruption | Clinic readiness cannot be inferred | Check existing power owner | Power result at the destination | Defer service, report cause only if confirmed |
| A request for a return note | The source needs a response | Choose public or private channel | Communications/print owner if available | Hold the note if no channel exists |
| A medicine count conflict | Two counts disagree | Reconcile against inventory owner | Canonical count/result | Retain mismatch as a report |
| A missed appointment | The party did not arrive | Ask whether rescheduling is possible | Current travel/quest owner | Close without inventing a penalty |
| A clinician unavailable | An expected staff member is absent | Check staffing owner | Current staffing result | Refer or return later |

This card set creates route and communication variety while keeping health decisions under existing owners. The first implementation slice chooses no more cards than it can fully wire end to end.

### Field 05 supplement — three non-duplicative story spines

**The Note That Stayed Folded** follows a request that contains more private detail than the recipient authorized. The player chooses a narrower message, waits for direct consent, or declines to transmit. Its mechanical result is only the current communications owner’s accepted delivery or a recorded local choice. It is not another signal-repair story.

**The Room Was Ready on Paper** begins with a room listed as a clinic while a caller cannot confirm staffing or power. The player compares the room record with current owners and communicates uncertainty. The story ends with a truthful availability notice, not a guaranteed clinic opening. It must not repeat a current “hospital overflow,” water-contamination, or disease-outbreak chain.

**A Parcel With No Name** is a supply custody story. A sealed package is offered for delivery, but the receiving party asks that no personal details be retained. The player checks the canonical item and existing dispatch route. Branches cover accepted delivery, refused parcel, lost route, and no current carrier. The arc resolves on custody and consent, not an invented treatment result.

The stories share a restrained tone but have different verbs: redact, verify readiness, and preserve custody. A continuity check compares names, places, asks, and outcomes with current faction chains, NPC arcs, disease content, and partial-plan material before any title is promoted.

### Field 06 supplement — optional task inventory and truthful evidence

1. Ask the recipient what may be included in the message.
2. Compare the request against the canonical inventory once, at the moment of dispatch.
3. Identify whether the claimed sender directly saw the situation.
4. Confirm an existing room state with its owner rather than infer it from a room label.
5. Return a receipt to the requester without revealing the patient’s identity.
6. Ask for permission before leaving a note in a shared place.
7. Tell the traveling party that a destination is unresolved and defer dispatch.
8. Deliver a no-stock response through a supported channel.
9. Retrieve a return message from its actual communications source.
10. Correct a stale address through CartographySystem only if that system owns the place fact.
11. Preserve an unreadable note in the existing archive only if archive intake supports it.
12. Cancel an outdated request without implying that care was delivered.

Every objective has proof: an accepted item transfer, a route completion event, a room/staff status response, a published message receipt, or a saved player choice in the current quest owner. Dialogue alone is not proof for a gameplay outcome.

### Field 07 supplement — faction and place guardrails

The Works’ caretaker-hut clinic and the 200-resident water-shortage context can give a care story human scale, but only after the exact site reference and chronology are reconciled. The faction lore does not give this plan permission to relocate the clinic, make it a new hub, or assign Adaeze a medical role. Existing Rebuilders plot chains around Bitter Water, Cistern Toll, Field Hospital Overflow, exchange disputes, and route issues are exclusion candidates; query the full chain index and integrated narrative plans before approving a title or branch.

The destination registry is the authority for place identity. If it has no caretaker-hut entry, use a verified location with a different canon premise or hold the story. Never mint a location ID in an expansion plan and then write content as if it were live.

### Field 08 supplement — outreach UI and service status language

The interaction flow is request → consent → readiness → route → dispatch → result → callback. The route and dispatch screens show party, canonical items, known destination, likely return path, and action cost only when the relevant owner supplies those facts. The result screen preserves three separate concepts: whether the trip happened, whether a message arrived, and whether a medical owner reports an outcome.

Screen-reader labels and visible text name the recipient and channel before a disclosure choice. Keyboard/controller navigation can reach “do not share,” “cancel trip,” and “return” without traversing a long narrative transcript. Pending results have an explicit check-again action only if the host has an event or query; there is no rapid timer-driven polling. Service rows use words and icons in addition to color. On closing the panel, event subscriptions are released and focus returns to the originating quest or party row.

### Field 09 supplement — throughput, risk, and performance limits

The experience can communicate capacity by calling current owners when a request is previewed, but it should not recompute every potential patient's demand on each frame. A circuit plan displays only its finite authored requests and current results. If the user opens a detail row, retrieve that owner’s current state once; refresh only on its state-changed signal or a deliberate player action. The narrative system is not asked to predict treatment success or build an unbounded queue.

If a later approved feature needs persistent outreach reservations, route legs, or waiting recipients, estimate maximum active entries and define stale reservation recovery with the existing save owner before adding state. The replay packet includes: no trip, accepted trip, interrupted trip, no stock, recipient refusal, conflicting source, and save/restore while a request is pending. Deterministic behavior comes from explicit owner inputs and stable content ordering; the story does not draw random patient outcomes.

### Field 10 supplement — first vertical slice and exit criteria

The first slice can be: one canonical origin or generic start; one destination resolved by the map owner; one request whose consent text is explicit; one existing item or message transfer; one travel/readiness result; one branch for refusal or unavailable service; and one callback. Do not make the field-clinic supply origin mandatory until its ID persists to the correct quest owner. Do not use the caretaker hut until location resolution and collision review are complete.

Acceptance requires the content author to attach exact source file and stable ID for every person, item, room, place, route, and message; list the current owner for each change; demonstrate that the UI reads rather than duplicates state; and show a player-observable result after reopening the panel. If the existing systems cannot answer “did the trip happen?” or “was the item transferred?”, the slice is blocked at design level and cannot be presented as a functional clinic expansion.

## Pass 25 — Care circuit schedule, visit variants, and continuity envelope

This pass turns the outreach premise into a paced set of encounters. It still does not simulate a mobile hospital. A “visit” is one supported interaction at a known place, with the participant’s permission and an owner-confirmed result. The player should feel a pattern of care and responsibility across a circuit, but the runtime should not gain a second patient list, appointment calendar, or triage queue from the narrative plan.

### Field 01 supplement — a short circuit with recovery time

The initial experience is designed around four possible stops, at most two of which are mandatory in a normal playthrough. A stop can be skipped for lack of stock, a refused visit, an unavailable route, or a player choice. Skipping should alter the final report, not permanently lock the campaign. If current day and travel owners expose no reliable ETA, the narrative uses “later” only as a chapter boundary and does not calculate an invented travel duration.

| Stop | Reason to go | New information | Player decides | If skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Origin room | Confirm what the clinic can honestly offer | Room and stock may disagree | Inspect, ask, or close | State remains unknown |
| Roadside contact | Obtain direct consent for a request | Second-hand version may be stale | Meet, send limited message, or defer | No patient status inferred |
| Remote destination | Return an existing supply or answer | Route may not accept dispatch | Continue, cancel, or return | Item stays where owner says |
| Home callback | Tell the requester what happened | Delivery may differ from care outcome | Public, private, or no reply | Arc closes with no claim |

The order is authored, not a new itinerary manager. If the current quest/travel owner cannot represent one of the stops, collapse it into a message/record scene or remove it. Do not add simulated movement just to make the sequence appear longer.

### Field 02 supplement — three request classes, one service envelope

Requests fall into **information**, **supplies**, and **readiness**. Information asks who can verify an event. Supplies asks whether a canonical item can be transferred. Readiness asks whether a current room/staff/power owner reports availability. These distinctions are meaningful even if each request ends with “not confirmed.”

The service envelope explicitly excludes assessment/treatment actions that the current health, disease, or ward owner does not expose to the chosen host. If a medical owner exposes a supported command later, its contract supplies the possible actions and returned result. The player cannot click a narrative choice that writes a symptom, dose, disease stage, recovery flag, health percentage, or ward admission into another subsystem.

### Field 03 supplement — capacity is a returned fact, not a computed score

The preview may summarize owner replies as “room is open,” “staffing not confirmed,” and “stock not available.” It must not turn those separate values into an invented capacity score such as “clinic ready 72%.” The player can decide whether to travel based on the visible facts. A future cross-owner readiness result requires an integrator to choose which owner composes it and how conflicting answers resolve.

When values change after the player confirms dispatch, the confirmation screen must not silently use stale data. The host either rechecks the relevant owner before issuing the command or reports that the operation is unavailable. It must never consume an item and then reject travel without a recovery path unless the inventory/travel contract expressly supports that transaction.

### Field 04 supplement — encounter cards for a second tranche

These cards add relationship and continuity choices without creating diagnoses or patient records. The same character does not appear in an existing arc unless a current roster/continuity audit confirms that the new scene fits their chronology.

| Candidate scene | Human question | Player’s meaningful option | Observable close |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Caller Wants No Name | Can help be requested anonymously? | Send a limited request or stop | Channel accepts or refuses the message |
| One Chair Stays Empty | Who is allowed in the room? | Respect a declined visit or request a later meeting | Recipient choice is recorded |
| The Page With a Torn Edge | Can an incomplete note be trusted? | Seek source or preserve as unverified | Archive/message source result |
| Two Lists of Dressings | Which count is current? | Check canonical inventory or leave mismatch | Inventory result, no local count |
| The Door Is Not a Promise | Does a clinic label mean service is available? | Ask current room/staff owner | Availability response only |
| Return Before Dusk | Is there a supported return trip now? | Depart, wait, or cancel | Travel owner result |
| No Message Was Sent | Did the channel accept the note? | Retry only if safe and supported | Actual delivery result |
| The Recipient Changed Their Mind | Does earlier consent still apply? | Confirm again or stop | New choice supersedes old disclosure intent |
| A Borrowed Coat | Who owns the item after the visit? | Return through inventory or keep by agreement | Transfer receipt |
| The Quiet Follow-up | Can the player close without more questions? | Leave a minimal callback | Quest owner closes with limited detail |
| An Unmarked Package | Is the sender known? | Refuse, inspect under an existing owner, or hold | Custody status only |
| The Wrong Address | Is the place reference canonical? | Correct through map owner or return | Accepted correction or unresolved place |

The scenes are authored content hypotheses until exact IDs and routes are reviewed. None may expose private content on a broad public notice because a writer wants the player to learn a clue.

### Field 05 supplement — longer story: “The Hand That Kept the List”

The central character is chosen from an existing survivor record only after all current personal arcs are checked. The character has been asked to keep appointment notes but is not the owner of the clinic schedule. Their conflict is that a copied list has become more authoritative in conversation than the clinic’s current state. The player must find out whether any person actually authorized the list to circulate.

In the opening, a requestor offers a full roster. The player may refuse the whole list, ask for one non-identifying supply request, or ask the list holder to speak directly to the clinic. In the middle, one matching owner response agrees with only part of the list. The player may correct the copy, mark it as a report, or preserve it without distribution. In the close, the list holder asks whether the correction means the earlier visitors were turned away. The correct answer depends on the owner’s source: if no historic visit record exists, the player says that they cannot confirm what happened. The human ending is not a medical recovery; it is the return of control over the person’s information.

Branches converge on an owner-confirmed communication result or a clear no-message closure. The arc should not grant an abstract trust point or modify treatment outcomes. If the existing narrative quest format cannot represent its needed choices, this is a story brief for a supported quest owner, not a reason to add a new branching engine.

### Field 06 supplement — side objectives grouped by actual authority

**Inventory and custody:** check one requested item; decline to move another; return a borrowed container; reconcile a receipt; preserve a disputed count; cancel a dispatch after the recipient changes their mind.

**Communications:** select a private channel; redact a name; verify delivery; hold a message with no current route; correct the sender attribution; return only a status summary.

**Place and travel:** resolve a canonical destination; cancel at an inaccessible gate; request a supported return; identify a stale place label; tell a traveler that arrival was never confirmed.

**Clinic readiness:** ask the room owner; check a staffing response; report missing power only through its current owner; distinguish a supply shortage from a staffing gap; tell the requester that no current result is available.

Each side task uses one authority group at a time. A cross-system objective is admitted only if both owner results have stable public references and the player can see which requirement remains unfinished.

### Field 07 supplement — no coercive failure and no false urgency

Care arcs are not timed by default. The urgency comes from a person waiting for an answer, not a countdown that punishes the player for reading dialogue. If a true event deadline exists, it must be supplied by an existing owner and displayed in plain language. The player gets a known consequence before confirming the route.

Refusal is a real branch, not a hidden morality penalty. A character may be disappointed, but any morale effect must come from a current owner with an authored result. The player can withdraw consent before transmission if the existing communications command supports cancellation. Once a public message is accepted, the UI must not imply that it can be retracted unless the owner supports that action.

### Field 08 supplement — sequence, focus, and disclosure details

The first screen gives a short request summary, not the entire medical backstory. The second screen clearly names what information leaves the player’s control. A review row shows the recipient and channel. The final screen reports the actual send/delivery result. A “share nothing” action stays visible and focusable even if it is not the recommended choice.

Voice and sound are optional; no diagnosis, consent, or urgency distinction is carried by audio alone. The same result is available to keyboard and controller users. Opening a medical profile does not subscribe the player to all health state changes; close releases its listener. When the current owner changes a fact, the screen marks the value as updated and the source, rather than replaying an alarming animation.

### Field 09 supplement — persistence contract for pending care

If the existing quest owner saves the arc, its state should be no more than the chosen branch, current stage, accepted objective deliveries, and stable owner references already included in its contract. Medical state, consent history, appointment schedule, route ETA, and patient location remain outside that save object unless their actual owner already supplies them. A loaded arc must not re-send a message or consume a supply a second time.

If the current owner cannot store a disclosure choice, keep that interaction within one non-persistent message action or request a signed contract before claiming the choice survives a save. This is especially important when an arc’s branch determines who learns private information. Never encode sensitive player-facing text in a debug log or hidden serialized copy.

### Field 10 supplement — tranche sizing and review checkpoint

Tranche one comprises one profile-agnostic request, one resolved site, two main-story scenes, four optional encounter cards, one actual delivery or message action, and a no-service ending. Tranche two adds a second route only if the first route uses no local mirror state, has focused functional coverage under the owning package, and passes content/continuity review. The complete candidate card set above is a backlog, not a commitment to ship every scene.

The reviewer records the observed result for accepted dispatch, item missing, route unavailable, recipient refusal, consent narrowed, communication undelivered, no room/staff response, and save/load during a pending stage. A demo that only shows a new panel is insufficient. A demo that mutates health from dialogue without going through the current health owner is a failed integration even if the prose reads well.

## Pass 26 — Medical-owner map and outcome card set

This pass makes the medical boundary concrete. Outreach is coordination and narrative over existing owners, not a second clinical simulation. Room, stock, staffing, health/disease, ward, and communication facts are usable only when their current owners expose a supported query or command to the chosen route. A missing API is not filled with a panel-owned diagnosis, patient roster, treatment queue, or readiness score.

### Field 01 supplement — owner inspection matrix

| Fact/action | Owner to inspect | May display | May change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Individual health | Current health owner | Exact exposed status | Nothing directly; supported command only |
| Disease lifecycle/exposure | Disease/health owner | Owner-provided state | Nothing unless accepted action exists |
