| Ward placement/staffing | Ward and staffing owners | Current result and source | Existing owner command, if exposed |
| Clinic room | Shelter room/building owner | Current room facts | Existing room operation only |
| Medical item quantity | Canonical inventory | Returned item and count | Existing transfer action only |
| Party travel/arrival | Current expedition/travel owner | Accepted/completed result | Existing dispatch action only |
| Referral/message | Communications/quest owner | Draft/sent/delivered as available | Existing send/cancel command |
| Faction response | Faction/quest owner | Source and participant response | Existing branch only |

This is an inspection agenda, not proof that each API exists. The integrator marks every row VERIFIED, MISSING, or DIFFERENT SCOPE. A missing row is omitted or escalated through its owner; it cannot become local mutable state.

### Field 02 supplement — bounded care request

A request is a bounded question addressed to an owner: request source, desired response, recipient/consent, optional canonical item/location, valid channel, source certainty, and closure language. It contains no clinical state. “Can the known room accept a delivery?” may be answerable by room and inventory owners. “Is this person medically stable?” belongs to a health owner and is omitted if no query exists.

Before dispatch, state whether the action is reversible, which owner confirms success, and what happens if the player leaves or loads a save. A delivery preview names recipient and quantity. A message preview shows content and audience. An irreversible accepted command is explained before confirmation. If the owner cannot cancel an accepted action, the UI must not imply it can.

### Field 03 supplement — outcome vocabulary

| Owner result | Wording | Actual meaning |
|---|---|---|
| accepted | “The request is on the route.” | Owner accepted; trip not completed |
| delivered | “The receiving owner confirmed the parcel.” | Inventory transfer completed |
| arrived | “The party reached the listed place.” | Travel owner confirmed arrival |
| not accepted | “No one accepted the request.” | No effect occurred |
| no stock | “The owner found no transferable item.” | Inventory unchanged |
| declined | “The visit was declined.” | No service or disclosure |
| conflicting | “The two accounts still differ.” | No fact was promoted |
| no response | “No confirmation has arrived.” | Pending only if owner says so |
| unavailable | “This route cannot be confirmed now.” | No local state change |
| need changed | “The current owner reports the request changed.” | Another owner changed state |

Words such as “recovered,” “treated,” “stable,” “infected,” and “cleared” appear only when a current health/disease owner returns that fact. A story can conclude on a communication result without claiming medical improvement.

### Field 04 supplement — roster and destination checks

Before writing a named encounter, check the survivor ID, residence, existing personal quest, faction, voice, chronology, and route. Confirm that the location ID exists and that current travel can reach it. The caretaker-hut address remains unresolved until canonical map data proves it. Unverified people and places stay role placeholders and do not enter runtime data.

The Rebuilders’ lore supports a community-clinic setting, but the plan cannot retell existing contaminated-water, hospital-overflow, tally, exchange, or clinic/outbreak plots. A new contact’s need must differ in player action and result. “Deliver the same medicine to another NPC” is not a new mechanic. Check faction events, NPC arcs, disease content, and integrated plan indexes before naming a story.

### Field 05 supplement — three episode packets

**The Return Bag:** a party brings back a marked container; its sender wants to know only whether it arrived. Present the canonical transfer receipt, return it through inventory if supported, or report that the route did not confirm delivery. This is custody after a trip, not treatment. Do not reveal who received the parcel.

**A Quiet Referral:** a resident prefers a named person over a public board. Ask whether that person consents to relay a request, select a minimal message, and wait for the actual communications result. A branch lets the resident withdraw before send. The outcome is whether a trusted channel carried the request, not whether the underlying need disappeared.

**The Room With Two Owners:** one record calls a room a clinic while the current staffing owner reports no responsible clinician. Return the discrepancy to building/ward owners and tell the requester that room function and readiness are different facts. Do not invent a lease, dispute, or staffing assignment.

### Field 06 supplement — additional playable request cards

| Request | Proof | Safe close |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm delivery acceptance | Inventory/travel callback | Preserve unknown custody |
| Remove name from public copy | Communication draft/result | No send before review |
| Ask whether visit is welcome | Recipient branch | Decline closes cleanly |
| Return unneeded item | Inventory transfer | Keep it if rejected |
| Carry unsigned note | Existing source reference | Label unsigned |
| Ask room owner about entry | Room/access result | No entry without response |
| Correct destination identity | Cartography result | No dispatch if unresolved |
| Request second witness | Existing person/event route | Preserve first report |
| Cancel pending dispatch | Travel owner | Explain if irreversible |
| Report unavailable channel | Communications result | Leave no phantom message |
| Return blank form | Inventory/archive if supported | No hidden copy |
| Mark request superseded | Quest/health result | No duplicate request |
| Send limited readiness question | Room/staff reply | No diagnosis shared |
| Ask for item list only | Inventory owner | No identity disclosed |
| Correct copied date | Archive/communications owner | Retain old date/source |
| Decline to guess urgency | No added state | Explain unknown urgency |

Each gameplay card needs a unique owner interaction. A flavor scene with no state change is tagged as flavor, not a task.

### Field 07 supplement — continuity and character consequence

Remember choices only through the selected current owner. `NarrativeQuestlineSystem` may suit a personal arc only if a free survivor slot exists and the item-objective/binary-branch grammar fits. It is not a campaign-wide queue. `QuestlineSystem` is usable only in its verified game mode and only with a playable definition; this plan does not assume its JSON supports delivery objectives.

Character consequences can appear in dialogue and owner-confirmed callbacks. A character may express disappointment, but no relationship meter changes unless its current owner accepts the action. An apology is not a trust score, and a quest resolution is not a medical result.

### Field 08 supplement — patient-safe workflow

Show the request reason, source, permitted disclosure, and owner action. The medical detail view is read-only unless a current health owner exposes a command. “Ask first,” “share less,” and “cancel” have equal visual weight to “send.” The result names the owner and time. If state changes while open, mark it refreshed. Do not auto-open or steal focus. Warnings correspond to real owner state and include text; sound is supplementary and captioned.

### Field 09 supplement — capacity and save budget

The first slice adds no treatment or route reservation and at most one active narrative request. Reuse a current quest cap if one exists. A larger patient queue needs owner review; it is not added because outreach sounds organizational. Performance checks cover the largest supported quest list, callback volume, listener cleanup, and save/restore with one request. Dialogue loads on demand; no panel-open operation scans health state for every survivor.

### Field 10 supplement — tranche evidence

The first release has one profile-agnostic request, one resolved site, two main scenes, one real delivery or message operation, one refusal, and one unresolved-source path. A Field Clinic Withdrawal variant is optional only if the stable profile ID reaches the selected owner. Dismissing before dispatch preserves all starting items.

The handoff lists owner methods, events, save section, loader/schema, IDs, and callback. Focused verification covers repeated dispatch, duplicate receipt, missing item, changed consent, route failure, no response, and save during pending. Until verified, this remains a proposal and does not claim that a mobile clinic feature exists.

## Pass 27 — Referral edge cases and information-handling outcomes

This packet tightens the boundary between care coordination and medical state. It gives writers and UI designers consistent behavior for interruptions, changing consent, missing sources, and old saves. The chosen owner remains responsible for every real transfer, medical fact, trip, or message.

### Field 01 supplement — consent timeline

Consent is scoped to one named recipient, one content payload, and one channel. A prior “yes” to a private referral does not authorize a later public notice. If the content, recipient, or channel changes, ask again before the new action. Consent can be withdrawn until the current communication owner accepts send; after that point, only the owner can decide whether correction or recall exists.

Do not persist a private medical detail in the quest record just to remember what the player was allowed to say. If an existing quest system stores only branch IDs, record the branch ID, not a duplicate copy of the private text. If no current owner can preserve the choice across save, do not promise that the disclosure history is durable.

### Field 02 supplement — information classification for scenes

| Scene information | Default treatment | Player action |
|---|---|---|
| Public room status | May be repeated with source/date | Verify current owner before update |
| Item count | Show only canonical inventory result | Recheck at dispatch |
| Named health detail | Private unless current recipient consent is explicit | Redact, ask, or cancel |
| Second-hand report | Label as unverified | Seek direct source or preserve uncertainty |
| Travel location | Use canonical place ID | Do not dispatch if unresolved |
| Historical document | Keep its original date/source | Cite as historic, not current |
| Owner refusal | Share only within the request’s agreed scope | Ask before public notice |
| Draft message | Not sent and not delivered | Review, cancel, or submit through owner |

This is content direction, not a new data classification engine. Current channel behavior controls what is public/private.

### Field 03 supplement — interruption cases

| Interruption | Correct state owner | UX recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Consent withdrawn before send | Quest/dialogue state | Cancel without command |
| Consent withdrawn after owner accepted send | CommunicationsSystem | Explain current recall options only |
| Recipient unavailable at arrival | Current travel/dialogue owner | Report no visit; do not infer refusal |
| Item count changed after preview | Inventory | Recheck before command |
| Route closed between preview and dispatch | Travel owner | Cancel and retain item |
| Duplicate delivery callback | Inventory/quest owner | Display once, no second reward |
| Save while a message is pending | Message/quest owner | Restore pending state without resend |
| Old content ID missing on load | Save/content owner | Approved migration or safe closure |
| Clinic room exists but staff does not | Room and staffing owners | Show two distinct facts |
| Health detail unavailable | Health owner | Say unconfirmed, not “stable” |
| Public channel lacks a private route | Communication owner | Ask permission for public send or cancel |
| Return travel unavailable | Travel owner | Tell the player before dispatch if possible |

### Field 04 supplement — trusted handoff sequence

The player’s handoff has four separately visible receipts: **request created**, **request accepted**, **item/message delivered**, and **medical owner response**. The sequence may stop at any point. A completed message is not a completed supply delivery; an arrived party is not proof of a medical examination. The UI avoids a single “care complete” badge unless the current medical owner itself reports that terminal result.

For an owner whose response arrives asynchronously, the panel subscribes only while relevant and releases the listener on close. A return callback can be read later through the existing quest/communication route. If the game has no stable callback route, the design says “response pending” and makes no silent change.

### Field 05 supplement — cost and reversibility review

Before commitment, identify whether an action consumes inventory, commits party time, sends public text, or changes a quest branch. If the current owner cannot return a cost preview, the UI may state that the operation has an unknown cost only if the owner’s actual command can still be safely issued; otherwise hold it for owner design. Do not charge medicine or travel time just because a story needs tension.

An accepted request may be reversible, irreversible, or cancelable only before dispatch. Each is specified by the owner, not inferred by content. The player can back out before confirmation. A request whose owner does not answer is not treated as a completed cost.

### Field 06 supplement — role-based story continuation

The player may meet a courier, requester, room steward, or record keeper, but the authoring role remains generic until a current survivor is assigned. Existing named survivors have prior quests and faction chronology; adding them requires checking the exact arc slot. A new name requires a roster/character integration path and cannot appear as a free-floating quest-only person if the game expects survivor identity.

Character callbacks refer to the owner result, not to a hidden medical condition. If the player delivered an item, the recipient may thank them for the parcel. If the health owner reports no outcome, dialogue cannot imply a cure. If consent was refused, no later scene reveals the detail “for dramatic effect.”

### Field 07 supplement — request fallback catalog

**No direct recipient:** ask the original requester for another supported contact or close. **No canonical place:** preserve the request and do not dispatch. **No item:** explain stock is unavailable and leave inventory unchanged. **No private channel:** request new consent for a public channel or cancel. **No owner response:** preserve pending only when its owner reports pending. **No staff result:** show room and staff facts separately. **No return route:** do not promise retrieval. **No patient ID:** keep the scene anonymous. **No profile provenance:** trigger a generic scene or omit it. **No save owner:** keep the branch transient or stop for a signed decision.

Every fallback has a complete end state and does not require the player to retry until it works.

### Field 08 supplement — screen-reader and focus QA

Disclosure preview reads recipient, channel, and full content in that order. The “cancel” action is next to the send action, not hidden at the bottom of a long list. A screen reader announces whether the text is private, public, or unknown. Focus does not jump when the owner returns a message. Refusal/unavailable labels have text and icon, not color alone. A user can review the result and then return to the original requester without reopening the whole medical panel.

### Field 09 supplement — save and replay checklist

Replay covers no-consent, consent then cancel, consent then send, repeated send, asynchronous delivery, save while pending, load after recipient disappearance, updated item count, route failure, and changed owner fact. The resulting branch IDs, transfer receipt, and sent/delivered states should match the same input sequence. There is no random recipient or diagnosis roll.

If the current owner changes a message or quest schema, its migration defines handling. The outreach plan adds no parallel migration. Private text is not written into log files, test output, or another system’s save section.

### Field 10 supplement — review disposition

Approve only cards whose actual owner and recipient route are proven. A useful narrative can remain as a design document when a route is missing; label it CONTENT-ONLY and name the exact dependency. A data-only card may ship only if its current loader consumes it and the player has a verified entry point. The expansion succeeds by giving the player careful, humane coordination choices while retaining current medical truth in one place.

## Pass 28 — First-hour care guidance and referral playbook

Outreach can teach the player how existing medical and logistics owners work without adding another tutorial system. The current onboarding surface and start flow remain authoritative. A small contextual guide can explain where to read a real health result, how to check an existing medical item, and how to avoid promising treatment before a clinic/ward owner confirms readiness. The guidance is optional, dismissible, and never substitutes for a functional action.

### Field 01 supplement — teach existing controls in sequence

The learning sequence is **read → verify → ask → dispatch → confirm → communicate**. In the first scene, the player reads a status from its current owner. The second asks for a room/stock check. The third previews a real communication or delivery command. The fourth shows an accepted, refused, or unknown owner result. The fifth lets the player choose whether to share that result. If an existing owner does not support a step, remove the step and its tutorial prompt.

This guide must fit into the existing onboarding/tutorial route. It does not create a medical tutorial panel, a help currency, a separate medical mode, or a forced early illness. It should not pause a live urgent event without an existing tutorial pause contract.

### Field 02 supplement — teachable facts and safe phrasing

| Concept | Plain-language guidance | Source the player can inspect | Phrase to avoid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Health fact | “This is the current result from the health panel.” | Existing health surface | “We know exactly how they feel.” |
| Room availability | “A room label does not confirm current staffing.” | Current room/staff owners | “The clinic is ready.” without evidence |
| Supplies | “Check current inventory before promising delivery.” | Canonical inventory | “We have enough.” based on a start profile |
| Travel | “A request is not a completed trip.” | Current travel/expedition owner | “The team is on site.” after dispatch only |
| Message | “A draft is not a sent message.” | Current channel result | “They have been told.” before delivery |
| Consent | “Only share what the recipient agreed to share.” | Current branch/dialogue state | “Consent carries over forever.” |
| Unknown | “No owner has confirmed this yet.” | Source receipt or missing response | “Probably fine.” |

Copy references only live interface labels and does not invent new terminology. It is reviewed against the current panel to prevent a tutorial describing a button that no longer exists.

### Field 03 supplement — optional learning branches

**Observe without dispatch:** the player opens the current health/room/inventory views and returns without spending or traveling. The guide recognizes only whether the views were opened if the existing tutorial owner records that fact. Otherwise it remains explanatory text rather than a completion condition.

**Request a referral:** the player selects a currently supported message/referral route. A preview explains its channel and recipient. The player can cancel and still continue the guide.

**Close with uncertainty:** the player receives no owner answer and chooses to preserve the report as unknown. The guide teaches that uncertainty is a valid operational result and does not punish the player with lower morale or lost progress.

No branch is a clinical diagnosis quiz. Correctness is about understanding what the system confirmed, not guessing hidden medicine rules.

### Field 04 supplement — referral and supply mini-scenarios

1. **A Request Without a Room:** ask a current room owner before telling a requester where to go.
2. **One Box for Two Stops:** inspect canonical inventory and choose one supported destination; do not split quantity locally.
3. **The Quiet Channel:** choose the minimum information needed for a referral.
4. **A Receipt With No Arrival:** distinguish accepted dispatch from confirmed arrival.
5. **The Change of Mind:** update consent before a second message.
6. **Outdated Clinic Hours:** request a current owner result or leave the time unconfirmed.
7. **Item Not Found:** communicate no stock without silently substituting a different item.
8. **No Return Route:** cancel before departure if current travel cannot promise return.
9. **Two Source Notes:** preserve source and date instead of averaging contradictory claims.
10. **The Appointment Was Never Booked:** explain that a request is not an appointment when the owner did not accept it.

Each scenario is one screen of instruction plus one real owner-backed interaction where possible. It does not spawn a patient or change disease state.

### Field 05 supplement — voice and humane pacing

Characters speak as people protecting time, privacy, and energy rather than as tutorial narrators. A clinician or caretaker explains one practical fact in their own voice, then leaves the decision to the player. New named roles remain unassigned until the current roster and narrative-continuity review finds an appropriate character.

Outreach is not presented as an endless emergency queue. The guide shows that a player can defer, decline, or ask for more information. Characters may return later if an existing event or quest owner supports that callback; otherwise the one-time scene closes without implying an appointment system.

### Field 06 supplement — integration with onboarding and current panels

The current TutorialPanel/onboarding owner determines when guidance appears, how the player dismisses it, and whether progress is saved. The medical screens retain all commands and data ownership. The guide only launches existing screens through their current route. If opening a UI panel has no stable tutorial event, the content remains optional reading; do not wire hidden button instrumentation solely for this guide without an owner decision.

The first displayed help text must be discoverable by keyboard/controller. Closing it returns focus to the original control. A player who dismisses all help must still receive accurate labels and ordinary in-context explanations. Tutorials can be revisited only through the current help route; no duplicate “medical manual” store is created.

### Field 07 supplement — volume and localization packet

Each concept has a one-line version, a short expanded version, a screen-reader label, and a no-audio equivalent. Strings avoid abbreviations that require prior knowledge. Use the existing localization pipeline if present; do not place new English literals in a panel. Content keys include source system and intended audience only if the current localization catalog supports that metadata.

A first tranche contains seven concept cards, five optional prompts, ten micro-scenarios, and a single completion summary. Each line is reviewed for ambiguous certainty words (“ready,” “sent,” “safe,” “treated”). Translation review focuses on the distinction between request, acceptance, and completion.

### Field 08 supplement — UX and accessibility checks

Help never covers the information it is explaining. Captions and text preserve any audio instructions. No concept depends on color or sound. A player can dismiss with the standard close/back action from keyboard and controller, and focus returns to the prior screen. The guide does not repeatedly reopen after dismissal. Long explanations can be skipped without losing the next real owner action.

The mini-scenario must explain the known cost before an irreversible transfer. Accessibility settings do not disable or invalidate outreach content. Error feedback says which owner did not answer if known, otherwise it says the fact could not be confirmed. It does not surface exception text or internal data paths.

### Field 09 supplement — performance and persistence

Guidance is loaded on demand and uses no medical-state polling. Progress is saved only through the current tutorial/onboarding owner. If that owner does not store optional help completion, repeated help can be dismissed per session without adding a new save field. Opening and closing guidance must not keep listeners on health, inventory, travel, or communications systems.

Verification covers fresh start, dismissed help, reopened help if supported, controller navigation, localization fallback, an owner refusal, and a panel that is unavailable. A guide may not claim to be complete because the player read it; at least one true owner interaction is needed for the “practice” label.

### Field 10 supplement — first-hour exit criteria

The player can explain the difference between a health fact, a room label, a request, a dispatched trip, and a confirmed result. They can find the current owner’s panel, cancel before commitment, and communicate an unknown response honestly. No new medical simulation is required for this learning outcome.

The implementer reports the existing tutorial route, panel entry points, current owner messages, help-dismissal persistence, and focus behavior. If adding a new tutorial event or save flag is needed, the current onboarding owner must accept it first. The content is released only with ordinary interface labels matching current code and with all questions of medical authority routed to the real owner.

## Pass 29 — Field-clinic referral contracts and care-circuit content

The current colony catalog now names `col_bldg_field_clinic`, while the disease lifecycle, survivor health, and ward-duty work already have their own owners. This makes a forward-care story plausible, but a catalog entry is not proof of a patient route, staffed clinic, treatment consumer, or reachable panel. This pass turns that distinction into the core design constraint: outreach may connect existing owners; it does not become a portable medical simulator.

### Field 01 supplement — Name the service being planned

“Mobile outreach” can mean a staffed vehicle, an expedition visit, a forward clinic, a courier carrying supplies, a remote referral, or simply a story about care beyond the shelter. These are different features. The first package should choose one actual service shape after source review. The existing `col_bldg_field_clinic` is a colony building definition, so it may serve as a destination only when a colony exists, the building is constructed, and a current owner can answer its availability. It does not imply that an on-foot mobile clinic or dispatch vehicle exists.

The plan separates four things on every screen: survivor health facts from the existing health owner; disease stage and treatment guidance from Plan 60; duty availability from the existing roster authority; and a proposed outreach request from any actual dispatch command. A player can read, prepare, or cancel a request without causing a diagnosis. A confirmed medical effect is shown only after the current treatment owner returns it.

No new patient ledger, symptom meter, clinic bed counter, triage algorithm, or treatment outcome store is proposed. A feature that needs any of those as mutable state goes back for an architecture decision and a named owner. In the absence of that decision, narrative visits can use existing facts and finish with a referral or an unresolved request.

### Field 02 supplement — Forward clinic availability contract

Before an episode can direct the player to a colony clinic, it should ask the colony owner for the colony ID, constructed building identity, and present availability facts exposed by that owner. If the owner only confirms construction and not medical capacity, UI copy should say “clinic building established,” not “doctor available.” Capacity, staffing, and treatment can be composed only where a current owner provides those facts.

Clinic availability has a clear truth table. No colony means no colony destination. Colony exists but building absent means planned location only. Building is constructed but no treatment route is bound means the building is a strategic asset without a playable appointment. Treatment owner available and destination accepted means a visit can proceed under that owner’s contract. A failed lookup remains unknown and must not be converted to “clinic closed” or “clinic open.”

If the route uses colony supply lines, item quantity changes still pass through the canonical inventory or delivery seam. Do not mirror the flow in an outreach schedule. The UI may preview an owner-supplied estimate if one exists; it cannot promise delivery from a travel calendar maintained by this plan. Refusals need to explain whether the destination, resource, route, or service was unavailable, but should not expose internal exception details.

### Field 03 supplement — Visit lifecycle without a parallel clock

The player-facing story lifecycle can be expressed as states of a request: considered, submitted, awaiting owner response, accepted, declined, completed, or unresolved. These labels describe the interaction, not clinical condition. They belong in the existing quest or host session only if its current save contract supports them. Otherwise the request stays transient and the player receives the live result in the same session.

Travel time remains with the existing expedition route if an expedition is truly dispatched. A “visit scheduled for tomorrow” requires an existing scheduler or campaign-day callback. Do not add a new outreach timer. If the current service only responds synchronously, present a synchronous outcome. If the owner exposes a persisted pending expedition, the outreach UI can read that status rather than duplicating it.

Cancellation is explicit before commitment. Once an owner accepts an action, the UI should distinguish “cancel request” from “recall active expedition”; they are not the same command. If cancellation is unsupported after dispatch, say so before confirmation. Save/load restores the owner’s pending action and result; it does not restore an invented copy of the same trip.

### Field 04 supplement — Referral and clinical fact boundaries

Plan 60 already covers the canonical disease catalog and derived lifecycle: 15 diseases across water, air, blood, and spore vectors, with diagnostic clues, timing guidance, and clinical staging. Outreach can carry a referral to those facts or surface a recommendation returned by the medical owner. It cannot author a new disease roster, recalculate lethality, infer an infection from dialogue, or introduce a hidden “care quality” percentage.

A referral message should separate observation, interpretation, and action. For example, “the patient reported thirst” is a witness observation; “the clinic requested a water-vector check” is an owner recommendation if actually returned; “treatment reduced lethality” is a result only if the treatment owner confirms it. If a field visit yields no clinical data, the episode can still resolve as a successful delivery or a request for later review.

Staff availability uses the duty roster’s current roles and rules. Plan 24 has a live staffing authority and ward-duty decisions; an outreach package must not create a second doctor assignment. If a field clinic needs an assignment the current roster does not support, that is a proposed extension for the Plan 24 owner to review, not an outreach-local worker field. The UI can explain “no assigned clinician was returned” without changing the roster.

### Field 05 supplement — Supply and equipment decisions

Medical cargo is canonical inventory. A dispatch manifest is a preview over item IDs and quantities, and final transfer goes through the current inventory owner. The plan should not define another stock room or silently reserve supplies at click time. A confirmation summary names the exact item, amount, source, destination owner, and whether the current transaction is reversible.

Do not promise that a vehicle cargo module provides sterile storage, refrigeration, oxygen support, or field surgery merely because those features are plausible. Adjacent preservation owners already exist: FoodTypeSystem covers perishable food; LyophilizationSystem owns specified medical batches with expiry and viability; CryoVaultSystem owns biological samples; and shelter load shedding identifies clinical refrigeration as a high-priority load. None of those facts proves that an outreach vehicle maintains a particular medical item or batch in range during transit, or that cargo links to those owners. The first outreach tranche leaves that mobile bridge unclaimed. Any extension must name the canonical medicine/batch owner, transport equipment and power result, duration semantics, interruption behavior, and deterministic restore path. It must not add an outreach-local spoilage timer. Existing medical items appear only when their current use is appropriate and wired.

Supply choices should be meaningful even without numeric care scoring. The player may choose between taking a smaller kit now, waiting for an owner-reported resupply, or sending a message requesting a specific item. A refusal preserves inventory and explains the authoritative shortfall. The narrative result can describe trust, gratitude, or disappointment, while mechanical morale or reputation changes remain behind existing owners and returned results.

### Field 06 supplement — Patient-led episodes and side stories

**The Return Address** follows a former shelter medic who no longer wants to be treated as the only person capable of care. Their story asks whether the player will send a request through an established referral route, assign a different available worker through the current roster, or leave the visit unstaffed and explain the delay. If no assignment API can perform the choice, the branch remains narrative and must not change duty state. The arc is about consent and workload, not a hidden expertise score.

**The Box With Two Seals** follows a courier carrying a medicine package whose paperwork names one colony while the route points to another. The player checks inventory identity, colony destination, and the message provenance before authorizing a transfer. The side quest can resolve through a verified correction, a safe refusal, or an honest unresolved record. It never destroys medicine as a surprise consequence and never manufactures a treatment effect from delivery alone.

**An Hour Before Dawn** concerns a survivor who wants a private consultation but lives in a crowded shelter. The story can present a conversation request and let the player choose whether to ask the current service owner for a private route, if such a route exists. If no owner supports privacy settings, the story stays as dialogue and does not claim the record was hidden. Its outcomes focus on the survivor’s expressed preference and the player’s explanation of limits.

These arcs use distinct care questions—professional identity, supply provenance, and consent—without duplicating existing disease or hospital story chains. Names and details must be checked against canonical factions, active quests, and current memorial state before data is authored.

### Field 07 supplement — High-volume encounter matrix

The first content pack can carry 12 encounter templates with data-authored substitutions: four supply requests, three destination checks, two declined referrals, two witness disagreements, and one follow-up note. Each template needs an owner-result slot, an uncertainty sentence, an optional side conversation, and a clean no-action ending. Variants should rotate people, time, and source material rather than reskinning the same disease case repeatedly.

Volume remains bounded by a shared vocabulary of action classes: read, request, confirm, transfer, dispatch, decline, and close. Each row maps only to existing commands. There should be no “treat” class unless the selected treatment owner accepts that precise command. Data validation checks source IDs, item IDs, destination IDs, text-key completeness, duplicate event identity, branch reachability, and the presence of at least one honest unresolved outcome.

The catalog should support a content coverage report grouped by owner and action class. That report identifies content with no consumer or a consumer that has since been retired. It is a development-time view, not a new in-game scheduler. Long-term additions can grow the stories without adding runtime polling or a fresh registry of patient state.

### Field 08 supplement — Interface and access needs

The request composer shows why outreach is being proposed, what is known, what remains unknown, the selected destination, current route result if available, any resource transfer, and the cancellation boundary. No vital sign or diagnosis is inferred from color. Patient names or private details appear only when the canonical data already exposes them and the player has a legitimate story reason to see them.

Keyboard/controller sequence is patient or case → source facts → destination/service → resources → review → confirm/cancel → owner result. Focus returns to the selected case after a modal closes. A disabled action explains the actual blocker. Text can be read at the player’s chosen pace; audio prompts are optional and use the current audio accessibility coordinator where wired. Dense clinical guidance is collapsible but never hidden behind an icon with no accessible label.

Low-bandwidth play is considered: the screen must render when a remote owner is absent, with the local case text and an “unable to verify current service” state. It must not spin indefinitely or imply a successful appointment after a timeout. Error copy identifies the failed fact in ordinary language and preserves the player’s draft when retry is safe.

### Field 09 supplement — Save, reload, and performance contract

Only the owner that accepts a persisted request may save its state. A transient form can preserve text and selected item in memory while open; it is not a new campaign save section. If the player confirms a trip, the existing expedition session remains the sole durable route state. If the player submits a quest objective, the existing quest save contract owns it. If neither contract can preserve the request, the action must be described as session-only before submission.

The interface reads health, colony, roster, and inventory on demand and never polls them each frame. It releases subscriptions on close and on campaign replacement. Detail panels load one case at a time and avoid materializing every patient biography in the campaign. Test-oriented acceptance includes repeated open/close, a large survivor roster, stale colony data, a missing owner, and reload at each owner-defined pending boundary.

Any future travel-time or treatment-resolution code must be deterministic and use current seeded RNG only if the owner already uses it. No outreach result depends on wall-clock time, machine locale, or roster iteration order. A failed or missing save migration must default to no fabricated treatment result.

### Field 10 supplement — Package gate and care-truth review

The package owner must identify the exact medical, colony, inventory, travel, roster, quest, and UI owners used by one playable episode. For each field, mark current API, current host route, persistence owner, and a gap. “The catalog includes a clinic” is evidence only for a definition; it does not satisfy the host, staffing, or treatment columns.

Before release, a reviewer follows one case from opening report through a declined referral, an accepted visit if currently possible, a resource refusal, a reload, and a final journal/archive view. The reviewer checks that no duplicate item transfer occurred, no staff role changed without confirmation, and no treatment is claimed before the medical owner reports it. A patient can decline, remain unresolved, or be referred without punishment authored by this feature.

Proceed with a story and interface that show true owner facts. Proceed with a mechanical field visit only when dispatch, care action, response, and restore are all reachable. Hold any mobile clinic treatment-capacity claim, vehicle-to-medical-storage/cold-chain bridge, remote triage, or independent scheduling proposal until a named owner and architecture decision exist. This gives the plan a strong playable first tranche without asking prose to impersonate an unbuilt medical system.

## Pass 30 — Distributed referral, colony reach, and communication privacy

ColonySystem, CommunicationsSystem, and the established medical authorities now make a wider care network possible. ColonySystem owns colony buildings and supply lines; CommunicationsSystem owns antenna range, interception, decoding, broadcast, jamming, and saved network state; medical owners retain disease, health, staffing, and treatment. This pass plans the handoff among those capabilities. It does not create a clinic-network manager or assume that a radio message is a medical record, an appointment, or a treatment result.

### Field 01 expansion — Three service modes with honest names

The content distinguishes **in-person referral**, **supply relay**, and **message relay**. In-person referral requires an accepted destination and an existing dispatch path. Supply relay requires an accepted shipment or colony supply-line result. Message relay requires a current communications command and a returned transmission result. A case may use one mode or combine them, but the UI identifies each transaction separately. “Care reached the outpost” is true only if the relevant owner returned a completed service result.

These modes create meaningful play even where no medical action is available. The player may successfully request a sealed package be forwarded while the clinic’s ability to treat remains unknown. A clinician can acknowledge a message without confirming a diagnosis. A colony can sustain a building through its supply line without recording that a patient was seen. The story may show a character valuing reliable contact while mechanically reporting the exact narrow result.

The minimum playable route is a request plus an honest completion card. A full medical visit is a richer route only after clinic availability, staffing, travel, and treatment callbacks are proven. The content pack cannot require that route to reach its chapter ending.

### Field 02 expansion — Clinic capability ladder

Clinic identity uses four evidence labels: **catalogued** (blueprint exists), **established** (colony owner says construction completed), **reachable** (a route or communications owner accepts a command), and **care-enabled** (a medical owner exposes a service response). These labels describe integration evidence rather than a new clinic-quality score. Each has distinct copy so a building definition is never presented as proof that a clinician or treatment is available.

The capability check resolves colony and building IDs, asks the colony owner for present state, then asks the route or communications owner for reachability only if the player chooses that method. Medical service details are queried last and only through a medical owner. A failure at one stage does not fabricate a negative result at another: an unknown radio route is not evidence that a clinic lacks supplies.

Availability is time-sensitive only if an owner exposes campaign-day data or a callback. No “clinic open hours” are created here. If the colony can receive daily supplies but has no staffed treatment route, it can still be a destination for a narrative parcel, labeled as such.

### Field 03 expansion — Referral packet and case-deck authoring

An outreach packet references a case ID, a canonical survivor reference, declared purpose, permitted recipient, selected channel, minimum context, and expected response. Health details are included only when the medical owner exposes them and the survivor’s authored consent allows sharing. The packet stores no copy of full disease state. A “message sent” fact is persisted only if an existing quest owner accepts that objective.

The first 18 templates divide by logistics: five destination-unavailable cases; four message-delayed cases; three shipments accepted but service unconfirmed; two patient-declined referrals; two duplicate-request recoveries; and two requests for details the player should not disclose. Each template has a no-action close, a safe retry if its owner contract permits one, and result wording keyed to the returned fact.

Variation comes from sender, recipient relationship, channel, missing source, and consequence of delay, not from changing invented symptoms. Validation checks recipient ID, channel availability, consent key, destination kind, localization, result vocabulary, and any sentence that asserts unowned clinical detail. The utilization report groups rows by channel and owner to reveal overuse of radio or a lack of non-digital alternatives.

### Field 04 expansion — Three network-care arcs

**One Line at a Time** follows a survivor who wants advice but does not want their whole history broadcast. CommunicationsSystem supplies actual transmission and interception results if a message is sent; the message contains only the minimum question. The player can send, wait for a private route if one exists, or decline to share. The story teaches that an antenna can deliver a message without guaranteeing confidentiality. It invents no encryption feature.

**A Clinic on the Ledger** begins with the `col_bldg_field_clinic` catalog row but no confirmed care callback. The player checks whether construction completed, whether a route is reachable, and whether a medical owner answers. The key decision is how to describe capability to a waiting family. “Building confirmed; clinician not confirmed” is a complete, truthful ending and does not depend on an unavailable treatment route.

**The Box That Took the Long Route** follows a care package placed into a colony supply line. The colony owner reports supply status; inventory reports what left the shelter; communications may carry a notification. None proves the other steps. The player resolves a mismatch between sender receipt and destination confirmation by asking for the missing source rather than spending a second package.

These arcs can interleave without sharing hidden mutable state. An archive or quest note is added only through the current owner’s route.

### Field 05 expansion — Consent and channel decision table

Before submission, the channel choice answers: does the intended recipient exist; is the channel supported now; who might intercept or overhear; what information does the survivor consent to share; and what confirmation can the owner return? The panel summarizes these facts. If interception is possible or unverified, it never labels the channel private.

Consent is specific to a packet. Agreement to receive care is not blanket permission to broadcast diagnosis or location. If the story has no current consent field, it can present a dialogue decision in the current quest branch; it cannot add a cross-campaign privacy database without an owner. With no consent fact, the safe behavior is to ask rather than presume agreement.

Declining transmission is a valid ending. It may leave the case awaiting another route or close with the survivor choosing to keep details local. This plan applies no morale or relationship penalty. Any supported survivor-relation consequence is explicit and separate from the communication result.

### Field 06 expansion — Transaction choreography by owner

For an in-person referral: read building state; select a real route; preview owner-reported travel and cost; confirm dispatch; transfer resources once through their owners; observe expedition result; and query the medical owner for a service result. The panel runs no shadow queue. If the route lacks a callback into treatment, an expedition may complete while the clinical case remains unresolved.

For a supply relay: choose canonical item IDs; verify inventory; ask the accepted shipment or supply owner; confirm the transfer; show its result; and optionally send a separate notification. A manifest is a preview. After timeout, first re-query the transaction owner if it supports identity lookup; otherwise report ambiguity and block a second transfer until resolution.

For a message: select recipient and current network; preview text and information scope; submit to CommunicationsSystem; display its transmission result; and wait for a response only if the owner has a response contract. Transmission does not prove reception. An intercepted message is shown as returned; this plan adds no security meter or patient penalty.

### Field 07 expansion — Case workspace and status projection

The workspace shows independent status lines for physical reach, material handoff, and clinical reply. A line is omitted if that route does not exist; it is not defaulted to “pending” in an invented scheduler. Every visible line names its source and last-updated campaign time. The message transcript is separate from the health view to reduce accidental disclosure while retaining a record of what was sent.

A route failure returns to the same case with recipient, channel, and unsent text preserved where safe. A completed transfer clears the pending manifest only after an authoritative result. Reopening queries that owner rather than trusting old button state. If no query contract exists, the UI labels the result unconfirmed and offers no duplicate command.

The contact list is contextual, not a global browser of all survivors and colonies. It includes only canonical destinations that have a story reason. Removed recipients render unavailable with a fallback label. Search is user-initiated and bounded to the known set.

### Field 08 expansion — Accessibility and interruption recovery

Text entry works with controller, keyboard, and screen reader. Recipient, channel, information scope, and confirmation are separate focus stops; confirmation names the recipient and summarizes the payload. Sensitive details are not announced in a public notification. The player can back out without submitting by activating a default control accidentally.

Radio status uses text and visual indicators, and captions remain available with audio disabled. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator supplies critical-cue behavior; a routine message arrival is not promoted to an emergency alarm. Coalescing avoids repeated notifications for one result, while reduced-stimulation settings preserve essential interception or failure information.

The design does not keep private text in a parallel global log. If the existing archive stores a transcript, the package follows that retention policy and names where the record appears. Without a retention contract, the UI clears ephemeral composition on campaign replacement and does not promise later recovery.

### Field 09 expansion — Polling, transcript size, and retry cost

The case panel requests a current network summary once on open and refreshes after a relevant owner event or explicit action. It does not recalculate range or enumerate every antenna each frame; CommunicationsSystem owns effective range. Colony state is read only for the selected destination. Medical state is not polled while the player reads a message.

Acceptance measures a large recipient list, heavily used communications history, multiple colonies, and signals arriving while the panel opens or closes. Transcript pages load on demand; the UI does not copy every intercepted message into a second list. Listener cleanup is checked after scene transitions and campaign load.

Retry is user-initiated and bounded. It is disabled while a known command is pending. If the owner has no safe retry contract, the control says “check result” or “close as unconfirmed,” not “send again.” This prevents request fan-out and duplicate item transfers.

### Field 10 expansion — Distributed-care release matrix

The vertical slice uses one colony destination, one communications route, one item shipment, and one medical reference. Cases cover catalog-only clinic, constructed but unreachable clinic, reachable but unstaffed clinic, successful transmission with no reply, interception, declined disclosure, accepted shipment, duplicate-submit attempt, missing recipient, supported pending-command reload, and unavailable archive route.

The implementation handoff marks each seam live, absent, or conditional and names Core owner, host route, panel surface, persistence owner, data IDs, and focused verification target. If the host cannot open a communications command from the case, the story stays authored and the route gap is reported separately; narrative code does not invoke an invisible API.

The release may claim “supply reached the colony,” “message was transmitted,” or “clinical advice was returned” only when the matching owner confirms it. Those are distinct results. The player can complete the arc with any one or choose an unresolved ending. This creates network-scale care stories while preserving medical truth, privacy, and one owner per mutable fact.

## Pass 31 — Specialized referral paths for maternity, ward triage, and dependency care

Recent integrations add three current medical authorities relevant to an outreach expansion: antenatal/maternal support extends the existing generational and caregiving owners; clinical ward triage extends the existing medical-ward and surgical-ward authorities; and dependency tapering extends the existing chemical-dependency and pharmaceutical authorities. Outreach content can connect a person to these owners and explain the handoff. It must not create a second pregnancy record, bed board, dependency ledger, or care-quality meter.

### Field 01 expansion — Outreach expands by referral type

The case list gains three specialized referral types, each with a distinct player promise. **Maternal support referral** means the player asks the established caregiving or antenatal owner for its current support result. It does not promise an appointment or a birth outcome. **Ward-priority referral** means a clinical owner returns a triage priority or a blocker; it does not promise admission. **Dependency-support referral** means the player requests the taper/care-policy guidance owned by the existing dependency system; it does not force a taper or treat withdrawal autonomously.

Each type can resolve through the same outreach lifecycle—review, consent, select an existing route, submit, inspect owner response, close—but its owner-specific facts are displayed in separate panels. A referral may be valuable because it clarifies the next safe step, even when the patient stays in place. This is an important expansion over a simplistic “visit equals treatment” loop: the player can coordinate a handoff, receive a refusal, or preserve a person’s preference without making a clinical decision the game has not assigned to them.

The story does not use demographic inference to place a survivor into one of these pathways. A case becomes eligible through an explicit current-owner fact or authored quest premise with a valid canonical identity. If that fact is absent, the story can discuss a general service or remain unavailable; it cannot infer pregnancy, triage acuity, or dependency from dialogue tone or inventory possession.

### Field 02 expansion — Clinical response envelope

ClinicalWardTriageEngine defines four triage categories and extends existing bed/procedure owners. Outreach may display the result it actually receives, together with the source, time, and next available owner action. It cannot recalculate category from symptoms, assign a bed, alter surgical readiness, or consume sterile supplies. If no current host adapter exposes the result, the plan remains content-ready while a package owner identifies the missing route.

The triage response envelope contains: patient reference; owner-returned priority; current accepted location or service if supplied; precondition or blocker; sterile-supply condition if returned; and the next command supported by the owner. It contains no copied symptom list. The player sees “priority returned by ward authority” rather than an unexplained red badge. A refusal is not written as neglect; it names the actual capacity or prerequisite returned.

Clinical urgency is not an outreach timer. No new countdown is introduced to make the decision feel dramatic. If the existing owner reports an immediate tier, the normal medical/ward route determines available action. If an interaction is delayed by travel, the expedition owner determines timing and the UI states only the returned estimate. Content can convey anxiety in dialogue without converting it into a fictional countdown that changes triage.

### Field 03 expansion — Maternal-support referral data

The antenatal authority models trimesters, nutrition reserve pressure, rest/fatigue effects, complication risk from existing factors, deterministic delivery resolution, and postpartum recovery. Outreach content may request information already exposed by that owner: current stage, supported need, supervision condition, or referral recommendation. It must not persist a parallel gestational week or derive a new risk score inside the field-case catalog.

A maternal case packet should carry only operational context: canonical survivor, consent to share, destination or caregiver reference, known owner-returned support need, and route choice. It should not include a general-purpose sensitive narrative field that can be broadcast over every channel. If the player chooses a message relay, the previous privacy rules apply: transmit the minimum, show channel limits, and distinguish successful send from response.

The catalog validator checks that any trimester word shown to the player comes from a current owner projection and that any outcome text corresponds to one of that owner’s supported results. New dialogue variants may represent emotion and family relationships, but cannot claim a specific complication, delivery status, or recovery rate unless the owning system reported it. A patient can decline to share details or choose a local caregiver where the current authority supports that option.

### Field 04 expansion — Dependency-support referral data

DependencyTaperWithdrawalEngine provides recommendations, withdrawal bands, medical escalation cues, peer support mitigation, and policy posture while extending the established dependency ledger. Outreach can surface a recommendation or referral to that authority. It cannot invent a daily taper schedule, consume a dose outside the pharmaceutical owner, or represent withdrawal severity using a local variable.

Case language is nonjudgmental. The player does not “catch” a survivor hiding a dependency; the case is opened by a request, an owner-returned care need, or a clearly authored story premise. “Decline now” remains a supported narrative outcome. A peer-support session appears only if the existing owner accepts it and reports a result. A resource shortage comes from canonical stock, not from a story-specific scarcity multiplier.

The player is never rewarded for abrupt forced withdrawal. A branch may compare permissive, supervised, and emergency policy recommendations only when those postures are returned by the owner. The story communicates that a recommendation is not a treatment command. If the medical escalation trigger is present, the interface routes to the supported medical owner and does not ask the player to override it as a dialogue challenge.

### Field 05 expansion — Four specialized storylines

**The Room Before the Road** follows a pregnant survivor who is weighing travel against rest. The current antenatal/caregiving owners provide any stage or support fact. The expedition owner supplies route availability and time if dispatch is requested. The player can request a remote consultation, prepare a locally supported care handoff, or accept the survivor’s decision not to travel. The ending cannot imply that the trip was safe or medically necessary unless the corresponding owners returned that advice.

**A Number on the Ward Slate** follows a runner who has heard that the ward is full. The player requests the real triage/bed response, then explains the outcome to a worried companion. If the ward owner returns a blocker, the player can seek an existing alternate route or close with the patient waiting. This story does not create a competing queue or silently reserve a bed.

**The Day Between Doses** follows a survivor who asks whether a taper can pause during a supply disruption. The current dependency owner supplies guidance; the pharmaceutical owner controls stock. A radio message may request clarification, but it cannot adjust the schedule. The arc allows the survivor to reject disclosure, and its positive outcome may be a supervised next step rather than a cure.

**A Familiar Voice at the Gate** pairs the case with a trusted peer who can support a conversation if the owner and roster indicate availability. The player asks whether the person wants company, an individual consultation, or no visit. Relationship, duty, and care state remain separate. The branch reinforces that peer support is chosen and bounded, not an outreach reward multiplier applied to every case.

### Field 06 expansion — Care-route cards and transition rules

The high-volume deck contains 20 specialized templates: six maternal-support requests, six ward-response questions, four dependency-support referrals, and four cross-category follow-ups. Each row identifies its primary owner, optional secondary owner, patient-consent requirement, current command, success response, refusal response, unknown response, and no-action ending. Rows are not interchangeable: a ward-priority response cannot satisfy a maternal referral, and delivery of supplies cannot complete dependency support.

State progression uses only the existing quest/request lifecycle. A case can move from considered to submitted when the owner accepts a command; from submitted to answered only when a response exists; and from answered to closed when the player acknowledges or declines the next step. Those labels are transient UI states unless a current save owner persists them. The plan cannot create a generic medical case database.

An interruption at any point preserves the current owner contract. Before confirmation, cancel changes nothing. After a medical command is accepted, closing the panel does not cancel treatment. On reload, the player queries the owner’s current state rather than restoring the panel’s previous guess. If there is no state-query API, the content package does not pretend that pending status was recovered.

### Field 07 expansion — Triage and referral interface

The case screen begins with the patient’s request in their own words, followed by owner-confirmed facts, optional medical guidance, destination/route, and action. This order avoids using a numerical priority as the sole introduction to a character. Triage labels are explained with accessible text. A returning result identifies which ward or medical authority supplied it and whether the next step is actually available.

Maternal panels separate a private care summary from travel and inventory. Dependency referrals avoid exposing details in list views or notification banners. A player must deliberately open the case to view sensitive text. If a transmitted message could be intercepted, its preview highlights which details leave the shelter. If a supported channel cannot send privately, the player may cancel without losing the unsent draft.

The panel gives a clear distinction between “referral sent,” “message received,” “priority returned,” “appointment confirmed,” “treatment started,” and “outcome recorded.” It does not combine these into a spinner called “care in progress.” A disabled action names the owner blocker and offers a useful read-only alternative where one exists.

### Field 08 expansion — Safety, consent, and accessible language

All three case types require person-centered copy. Triage priority describes an owner’s operational classification, not a person’s worth. Maternal-support options do not assume family structure. Dependency-related language avoids shame and treats relapse risk as a care need rather than a moral failure. Names, gestational details, and treatment information are not spoken by a global alert unless the player intentionally opens the case.

Keyboard and controller flow includes a clear skip/close action at every non-committed step. Screen-reader labels state case, source, freshness, and available action. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator can deliver an optional visual cue for a truly critical medical emergency, but opening a referral does not retrigger it. Text scaling supports long owner guidance without hiding cancel/confirm. Color is never the only signal for urgency, route status, or pending response.

The main story can close even when the player cannot or chooses not to act. An unresolved response is narrated as unresolved, not as failure. No optional objective is required for a survivor to receive ordinary system care. These safeguards keep the expansion about access and coordination rather than coercive medical roleplay.

### Field 09 expansion — Persistence and cost boundaries

The existing medical, caregiving, cohort, ward, surgical, dependency, pharmaceutical, inventory, communications, expedition, roster, and quest owners retain their state. The outreach UI stores no clinical snapshot. Any session-only draft is cleared safely on campaign replacement; an accepted command is rediscovered through its owner. A save review records the exact owners that are captured and restored before a field-route package may claim persistence.

Performance should be bounded by one selected case and the current owner projections. The list view must not query every survivor’s maternal, triage, and dependency state every frame. Sensitive data is fetched on selection if the owner supports it. Large history or message transcripts are paged. All listeners are released on close, campaign load, and survivor removal.

Deterministic outcomes remain in their current owners: seeded delivery resolution, existing triage calculations, and dependency recommendations follow their own current contracts. Outreach introduces no random care quality or hidden modifier. A paired replay verifies the existing outcome where the host wiring is changed; UI navigation alone is verified through focused route checks rather than broad simulation.

### Field 10 expansion — Specialized-care acceptance tranche

Stage A validates the 20 templates and consent text without adding runtime state. Stage B integrates one maternal-support referral through a real host route. Stage C integrates one ward-priority response and verifies that bed/procedure ownership remains unchanged. Stage D integrates one dependency-support request with canonical item/stock refusal. Only after each owner route is proved can the remaining content rows be promoted to playable status.

Review cases cover an unknown patient fact, declined consent, immediate triage response, delayed/refused referral, full or unavailable ward, no sterile supply, pregnancy-stage projection unavailable, accepted maternal support, dependency recommendation under scarcity, intercepted message, and save/load at each owner-supported boundary. Every case verifies no duplicate patient state, bed reservation, item charge, or treatment outcome.

The package handoff identifies the live command and read seam for each specialty, any host panel still missing, accepted data references, save owners, content-only fallback, and focused verification. Until that handoff proves a route, the plan describes the specialty as a connected referral concept rather than a working outreach service. This extends the plan into high-value care content while retaining the medical owners already integrated in the game.

## Pass 32 — Specialist-case ledger and continuity outcomes

Pass 31 established the specialty boundaries. This pass supplies a deeper content and acceptance ledger for maternal, ward-triage, and dependency owners. It treats their current outcomes as facts, not narrative decoration. The encounter cards are design candidates; a package owner must bind them to the current APIs and catalogs before marking them playable.

### Field 01 expansion — Case selection from current facts

A specialty case is eligible only when an existing owner returns the fact needed to open it or the story’s authored premise clearly establishes a request. The panel never scans dialogue for symptom phrases and infers triage. It never classifies a survivor as pregnant from relationship state or dependent from an item found in inventory. If no current, canonical case reference exists, the content offers general guidance or remains unavailable.

There are three supported ways to enter a case: the survivor asks through an existing personal request; a medical or ward owner emits a referral/status event; or a narrative arc introduces a fictional request that does not mutate clinical state until an owner accepts a command. This prevents authored text from silently enrolling a survivor into a medical system.

When multiple specialties apply, the interface asks which owner result the player wants to inspect. A maternal-support request and a ward-priority response may coexist, but each has a distinct next action and result. The player can leave the specialty view and use ordinary medical care without clearing the story case.

### Field 02 expansion — Referral decision record

The referral card records the human request, current owner fact, destination or channel, consent, resource preview when available, owner response, and follow-up. It does not convert all outcomes into a generic success/failure. A refusal names whether the blocker is destination, roster, stock, bed/procedure condition, or unsupported route only where the owner provides that reason.

For multi-step care, the story records references to each accepted operation rather than an aggregated treatment percentage. A message, trip, and medical visit are distinct. Completing one does not complete the others. If the current quest owner supports only one objective at a time, content uses a supported sequence or separate arcs instead of a hidden graph.

“No new operation” is a valid result. A patient can receive guidance and decline dispatch. The player can learn that no ward action is available and close the conversation. A current owner refusal is an observable fact; an unqueried status remains unknown.

### Field 03 expansion — Maternal and neonatal encounter cards

**Rest is the Request.** A patient asks to pause travel. The antenatal owner’s rest/fatigue projection is read if exposed; the travel owner decides whether a trip can be delayed or cancelled. No outreach timer is added.

**A Food Parcel Is Not a Care Plan.** A family offers food. The owner decides whether a nutrition reserve changes; inventory confirms only whether a canonical item moved. The story cannot claim that the parcel reduced complication risk.

**The Older Sister’s Notes.** A relative offers a list of support tasks. Caregiving and roster owners determine any accepted role. Without a live assignment command, the list is dialogue and the relative can decline further duty.

**At the Threshold.** A household asks whether to leave for another destination. Current owner facts and an actual route quote are presented; the scenario does not script a “safe to travel” answer. If access is unavailable, the choices concern communication and local support.

**The First Quiet Day.** Postpartum follow-up begins only after the antenatal owner returns a supported stage/result. The player asks whether the survivor wants another contact. No recovery clock is created; a missing projection remains a conversation.

### Field 04 expansion — Ward and sterile-supply encounter cards

**Minimal Priority, Real Concern.** The ward owner returns the lowest tier while a family remains worried. The UI displays the actual priority and explains that it does not dismiss the person’s concern. Follow-up is offered only through a supported route.

**The Delayed Bed.** A delayed priority is returned but no capacity is available. The player asks for the current next step, remains at the current site, or closes the referral. No hidden waitlist is created.

**The Sterile Tray.** A procedure is blocked by sterility. The clinical owner shows its actual requirement and inventory result. A courier may be offered only if a canonical consumable and transfer route exist; delivery alone does not book surgery.

**Two Names on the Slate.** Family members use different names for one patient. Canonical identity is resolved through the current survivor owner; the story creates no duplicate bed or triage record.

**After the Procedure.** A clinical owner reports completion. The story may ask whether a follow-up is wanted, but cannot mark rehabilitation, recovery, or discharge complete without those owners’ results.

### Field 05 expansion — Dependency-support encounter cards

**A Step Down, Not a Cliff.** A survivor asks to discuss tapering. DependencyTaperWithdrawalEngine supplies the current recommendation and symptom band. The player offers only owner-supported choices; abrupt cessation is not framed as heroic.

**The Last Bottle on the Shelf.** Pharmaceutical stock and taper guidance come from separate owners. Short stock does not authorize the UI to calculate a replacement schedule. If the recommended option is unavailable, the result is a referral or escalation, not a hidden workaround.

**Peer Support on Their Terms.** The patient requests a specific companion. The existing support route determines availability and result. The player may instead respect a request for privacy; neither choice grants a second morale effect.

**The Emergency Posture.** The care-policy owner returns an escalation cue. The ordinary emergency surface handles it. Dialogue cannot overrule required escalation through a made-up “wait” choice.

**A Name for the Meeting.** A survivor asks that a support conversation remain private. The story respects this in dialogue, but durable anonymity depends on an existing retention contract. The UI states which owner creates any saved record.

### Field 06 expansion — Mixed-specialty transfer cases

A patient with both maternal and ward needs uses the existing antenatal/caregiving and ward owners; outreach provides only the transport or information seam. A patient with dependency support and a sterile procedure uses the dependency and procedure owners; no local priority score is computed. A survivor who needs both a message and an expedition has two transactions, not a blended delivery flag.

Each mixed case states read order, any ordering constraint returned by an owner, and fallback when one source is unavailable. One owner’s severity is never derived from another owner’s state. If an owner changes a shared health fact, other owners read the canonical value on their next query; outreach does not write a copy.

The pre-implementation collision list includes duplicate charge, duplicate patient identity, appointment promise without a bed, shipment without acceptance, private details sent on a public channel, and a branch that becomes unreachable after refusal. Every risk receives a disposition before code work begins.

### Field 07 expansion — Result language

Use exact status phrases: “request prepared”; “sent through communications”; “recipient acknowledged”; “referral accepted”; “priority returned”; “destination reachable”; “item transfer accepted”; “procedure authorized”; “care action recorded”; and “outcome unknown.” A button can submit a request; only the owner confirms acceptance.

Refusal text names its source and, where possible, a valid next step. “Ward owner reported no eligible sterile stock” is clearer than “the hospital is closed.” “No current route result” is clearer than “too dangerous to travel.” Missing owner response is a technical unknown, not a medical judgment.

The result screen offers return to the patient conversation, inspect the owning panel, or close without another transaction. It never drives a repeated retry loop. Consent is reviewed before every new recipient or channel rather than carried forward automatically.

### Field 08 expansion — Content warnings and accessible control

The campaign summary names pregnancy, clinical urgency, dependency, and withdrawal themes in neutral language before launch. Sensitive dialogue is not required for a mechanical reward. The player can skip a scene, close an optional referral, or allow a private conversation without losing an item or ending access.

Visual and audio cues follow AudioAccessibilityCoordinator. Only a critical owner event becomes a high-priority notification; opening a referral does not replay one. Screen readers receive the status, source, and person’s chosen words in order. Patient names and dependency details stay out of public toasts. Color is not the only marker for immediate, delayed, or expectant priority.

Localization uses canonical medical terms and consistent family names/pronouns. Copy does not imply a particular relative must provide care or that the player can force a survivor to become a clinician.

### Field 09 expansion — Load and save boundaries

The specialty list fetches only the owner projections needed for visible rows and requests detail after selection. It does not recompute triage or taper recommendations per frame. Message history is paged through its owner. Closed cases are reconstructed from existing medical, journal, archive, or quest sources; no local case archive is added.

Save review occurs at accepted referral, dispatch, item transfer, triage result, support session, and underlying medical-state change. The selected tab is not a reason for a new save section. After reload, the UI queries the owning system. If no query exists, it states that completion cannot be verified and does not automatically repeat the command.

The load profile uses a large survivor population and several simultaneous specialties. It checks listener cleanup when a patient leaves the roster and when the campaign reloads. A stale case object must not retain health data after owner replacement.

### Field 10 expansion — Focused release tranche

Acceptance follows one maternal request, one triage response with sterile-supply blocker, one dependency-support referral, and one mixed case. It verifies identity, owner source, refusal explanation, no duplicate charge, exact result phrase, ability to close, and no unauthorized state change. Reload is tested only at boundaries the owner claims to persist.

Catalog checks require canonical subject, specialty type, owner reference, supported action, consent rule, result phrases, localization, and a no-action path. Coverage includes accepted, declined, refused, delayed, unknown, and unsupported states.
