Existing focused owner tests are reused by the eventual integrator; this draft adds no tests and authorizes no broad run.

The handoff separates owner-bound cases, narrative-only conversations, and held cases missing a host/read seam. Only reachable content is marked playable. This lets outreach cover specialized care at scale without duplicating maternal, ward, dependency, pharmaceutical, inventory, communications, roster, or save authority.

## Pass 33 — Referral follow-through through survivor-owned personal arcs

This pass adds continuity after an outreach encounter by connecting a player-visible choice to the current survivor personal-quest owner where a real quest already exists. Outreach does not create an auxiliary care journal and does not turn every patient into a quest giver. Its contribution is to let the player discover that care, identity, and a survivor’s own unfinished concern may meet in one authored story, then hand control to the existing personal-quest route. A personal quest’s morale and item rewards remain with `PersonalQuestSystem` and its current delegate bridges; the medical owners continue to decide treatment.

### Field 01 expansion — Continuity is a handoff, not a second case state

The player-facing specialist case can point to a survivor ID and one optional existing personal-quest ID. It cannot clone the quest stage, choices, morale delta, inventory reward, or survivor traits into outreach data. Opening the case may ask `PersonalQuestSystem` whether a known quest is eligible for that survivor only if the live host exposes that query and selection route. If no query exists, authored content may still mention that the survivor has a personal concern, but the route remains narrative-only and cannot promise a quest unlock.

The choice sequence protects the distinction between medical follow-up and character agency. A patient may accept care, decline a visit, ask for a message, or simply end the conversation. None of these choices automatically advances a personal quest. A later, explicit interaction opens the quest and invokes one of its supported options. If the quest owner rejects the choice or the survivor is no longer eligible, outreach displays that owner result without retrying, repairing, or locally advancing the quest.

### Field 02 expansion — Eligible arc selection from canonical content

The integrated catalog currently contains ten personal quest identities: `pq_buried_cache`, `pq_last_confession`, `pq_radio_echoes`, `pq_lost_journal`, `pq_oath_of_iron`, `pq_spores_of_mercy`, `pq_broken_locket`, `pq_debt_of_blood`, `pq_silent_choir`, and `pq_watchers_remorse`. These are a validation inventory, not a claim that all are clinic- or care-related. The outreach authoring pass reviews each quest’s survivor binding, traits, existing stage, required items, consequence language, and voice before choosing any cross-link. A candidate without a plausible, consent-safe connection is explicitly marked `NO_LINK`.

Compatibility records carry `quest_id`, `outreach_specialty`, `eligible_survivor_rule`, `consent_prompt`, `owner_query`, `handoff_action`, and `fallback`. They never carry an alternate list of stages or quest choices. A quest needing a specific item asks the quest owner to validate the supported objective; outreach cannot reserve that item, mark the stage satisfied, or use a medical supply transfer as an unrelated quest reward.

### Field 03 expansion — Storyline: Pages for the person who returned

The arc begins when a survivor finishes a difficult outreach conversation and mentions an unfinished personal matter. The player asks whether the survivor wants to revisit it now, later, or not at all. A “later” response leaves the current medical follow-up with its actual care owner and does not start a hidden timer. If the personal-quest route is available, the survivor’s next interaction opens the existing quest. If it is absent, the episode ends honestly with the request recorded only as dialogue and a clear status that no tracked follow-up was created.

The middle chapter places care and personal agency side by side without making one a reward for the other. A clinician may recommend a supported next step while the survivor pursues a separate personal objective. The player cannot withhold care to force quest completion or promise care in exchange for quest participation. The closing chapter may show the personal quest’s returned outcome and a separate medical owner result. It names each source and leaves any disagreement visible—for example, a resolved personal concern does not mean the survivor has recovered medically.

### Field 04 expansion — Referral-to-arc case cards

**The Locket Stays Closed.** A survivor receiving support asks not to discuss a personal keepsake. The care case closes according to its owner; the existing locket quest remains unopened. The player can respect the boundary without losing medical service.

**Pages of the Lost.** A survivor requests help finding a journal. If `pq_lost_journal` is already available to that survivor, the player may open the canonical quest after confirming consent. If it is not available, outreach can ask for a location clue but cannot spawn or complete the journal quest.

**Signals from Sector 4.** The player passes a request for a quiet follow-up to the existing radio-related personal arc only through its own supported interaction. A successful broadcast, if chosen, proves transmission; it does not prove the survivor received an answer.

**The Lichen Tincture.** The medical owner answers whether a treatment or supply action is available. `pq_spores_of_mercy` may appear as a separate quest option only if its canonical item/objective and personal-quest state accept it. A quest ingredient cannot substitute for an actual treatment.

**The Last Confession.** A patient declines group disclosure but may choose a private conversation. The outreach record remains privacy-minimal, and the existing quest owner determines whether an option is recorded.

### Field 05 expansion — Consent, refusal, and autonomy table

Before an outreach-to-quest link is shown, consent is scoped to that action: open the personal story, disclose a specific fact, or use a supported communication channel. Consent to medical triage does not authorize a broadcast. Consent to share a route address does not authorize opening a private quest. A “no” removes the cross-link from the current interaction but does not delete the quest, penalize treatment access, or reduce morale through a local rule.

Refusal states remain separate: the survivor declined; the quest owner says the quest is unavailable; the route cannot identify a canonical survivor; the current host lacks an open-quest command; or the player closed the panel. Each gets a distinct phrase and next step. A refusal never masquerades as an accepted referral. The player can continue ordinary, supported medical actions even when a story link is blocked.

### Field 06 expansion — Handoff transaction and reward boundaries

The safe handoff is: verify the canonical survivor; query the outreach owner facts; present the care option and any privacy notice; obtain a deliberate choice; invoke the current care/referral command; report its receipt; then, only through a separate player action, query/open a canonical personal quest. If an existing quest choice returns a morale or item effect, the current delegate bridge applies it once through the survivor or shelter inventory owner. Outreach listens to the result but never repeats the reward. A page refresh or panel reopen is not a new command.

Duplicate protection follows the actual quest and care owners. If either owner lacks an idempotent command key, the host must disable resubmission while the result is pending and recover its state from the owner before enabling the action again. No “care completed” flag is inferred from a quest option, and no “quest completed” flag is inferred from a successful treatment referral. If the integration seam cannot keep those results independent, the cross-link is held from release.

### Field 07 expansion — Patient workspace and transition clarity

The specialist workspace shows two clearly separated cards: current care, with owner-returned status and next supported operation; and personal story, with the existing quest’s own stage summary if the route supports it. A connecting label such as “You may also ask about this, if you want” invites an optional transition without suggesting that the quest is care. Returning from the quest restores the previous case projection by re-querying owners, not by reviving a stale copy.

Keyboard/controller focus order visits the medical summary, current action, private-story invitation, then close/back. Sensitive quest text is not included in a public triage banner or route summary. The player can complete one supported care action and close without opening the story. Screen-reader copy identifies which system supplied each status and announces whether a command was sent, accepted, refused, or merely viewed.

### Field 08 expansion — Voice, accessibility, and non-coercion review

The text must never imply that a survivor owes the shelter a personal disclosure because it supplied medicine, a bed, transportation, or a visit. Conditions such as addiction, pregnancy, grief, and disability are not used as plot keys that remove agency. A quest can contain pain or regret, but its outreach framing must not label a survivor by diagnosis. Names and medical details stay out of generic map markers, achievement notifications, and public messages unless the player invokes a supported disclosure with informed consent.

Localization review checks pronoun consistency, the difference between “declined” and “unavailable,” low-reading-level action summaries, and clear focus/close behavior. Text-only routes remain completable when a portrait, audio cue, or optional archive link is absent. No action is conveyed only by color. Narrative closure can validate the player’s respectful choice without awarding an invented morale bonus.

### Field 09 expansion — Save ownership and reload continuity

The personal-quest owner persists quest state and applies its own choice effects; the relevant care owner persists referral, medical, bed, inventory, or travel outcomes; the existing campaign/quest host persists only the supported story link. If those systems do not expose a stable cross-reference, the UI can show both current projections but must not save a guessed association. A reload queries each owner and reconstitutes the two cards independently. Missing or retired quest IDs degrade to a readable unavailable link rather than a fabricated quest stage.

At scale, the case list reads a compact set of current survivor identifiers and does not call `GetQuestsForTrait` across the entire colony every frame. Eligibility is resolved after selection and cached only for the lifetime of the view. The panel disposes subscriptions on close, patient removal, and campaign replacement. Quest completion history is paged or read only through the canonical quest/archive API; this plan creates no second case journal.

### Field 10 expansion — Promotion checklist and focused sample

The first end-to-end sample uses one survivor whose personal quest and care route are both currently reachable. It proves consent, separate owner queries, a care refusal path, a personal-quest refusal path, a successful quest option if supported, exact-once morale/item effects, and reload at the owners’ declared persistence boundaries. A second sample verifies that another survivor with no matching personal quest still receives normal care. The catalog’s remaining candidate IDs are reviewed for `LINK`, `NO_LINK`, or `HELD`, not bulk-promoted because the system exists.

Promotion requires exact host route, owner APIs, catalog IDs, event wiring, save ownership, focused tests, and accessibility evidence. A core-only personal-quest integration does not prove outreach host reachability. Until a real cross-link is demonstrated, these cards remain authoring candidates. The expansion offers richer longitudinal survivor stories while retaining independent care, quest, reward, privacy, inventory, and persistence authority.

## Pass 34 — Time-capsule continuity and bereavement-aware follow-up

This pass uses the integrated time-capsule content as an optional source of legacy comfort after an outreach visit. The feature is not a new counseling system, memory library, or promise that opening a capsule treats grief. `TimeCapsuleSystem` owns its four canonical capsule records, opening condition, sentimental contents, morale calculation, and bereavement-comfort calculation; survivor and memorial owners retain their respective facts. Outreach can offer a consent-led route to an existing capsule or a legacy message only if its current host path allows the owner to resolve and open it.

### Field 01 expansion — Four existing sources, four different contexts

The current capsule IDs are `capsule_founders_cache_1984`, `capsule_prewar_geologists`, `capsule_bunker_echo_memorial`, and `capsule_childhood_memories`. They cover a day-based founders’ vault, a manually opened geologist core box, an event-based watchman footlocker, and a survivor-based nursery time box. Their open conditions are meaningful gameplay gates. The medical outreach expansion may read a capsule only when its owner says that capsule is openable/opened under the current rule; it does not add another opening command or turn a clinical state into a capsule trigger.

Each story card names why a particular source might matter to the survivor and what the player is actually asking permission to do. A discovered legacy message is not a medical record. A time capsule containing a nursery drawing is not a diagnosis. A memorial source remains under memorial/archive visibility rules. A capsule that is unavailable is not replaced with a generic, fabricated “comfort message.”

### Field 02 expansion — Bereavement support as optional conversation

An outreach conversation may ask whether the survivor wants a quiet moment with a known legacy object, a memorial, or an existing message from a deceased person. The player can offer the choice, respect a refusal, or return to the primary care request. Bereavement comfort is reported only if the corresponding owner returns a supported calculation/result for the named survivor and deceased person. The view must not invoke `CalculateBereavementComfort` repeatedly during rendering, and a computed comfort value must not be re-described as therapy, risk reduction, or resolved grief.

The optional interaction never blocks urgent triage or replaces professional care. If the medical owner returns an immediate priority, that action takes precedence according to its real workflow. The capsule interaction remains available later if the survivor consents and its own open condition is satisfied. This rule keeps story pacing from turning a sentimental item into a gameplay gate for care.

### Field 03 expansion — Storyline: The Voice in the Nursery Box

An adult survivor asks why the nursery keeps a sealed box with their name. The existing survivor-based capsule targets `surv_firstborn_adult`; the player first asks whether the intended recipient is actually the current survivor and whether the capsule owner permits opening it. If so, the player can offer to read the message privately, leave the box closed, or invite a chosen support person if the survivor agrees. The opening action, recipient, and resulting morale/comfort are returned by the capsule and survivor owners.

The next chapter follows a different survivor who has lost a relative and hears that an old message might exist. The player can check the current capsule/archive sources with consent, explain that no matching message is available, or offer an ordinary conversation. The lack of an artifact does not become a failure state. The final scene is not “grief solved”; it records whether the survivor wants further contact, whether any message was actually shared, and what care/referral status remains.

### Field 04 expansion — High-volume encounter set

1. **The Founders’ Note:** a patient asks who wrote the shelter covenant; the player offers an archive search, not a clinical diagnosis.
2. **Core Samples:** a geologist in recovery wants to see the old aquifer drawing; the capsule must be openable and the recipient agrees.
3. **The Watchman’s Photograph:** a bereaved recruit requests a private viewing; memorial privacy and the current deceased-survivor link are checked first.
4. **The Yellow Sun:** the nursery recipient decides whether to open the childhood box; no birth or development fact is inferred from the drawing.
5. **No Message Found:** the owner returns no matching capsule; the player offers a normal follow-up and closes without inventing one.
6. **Not Today:** the survivor refuses to open an artifact; care continues, and no morale penalty is added.
7. **Read It Yourself:** a survivor wishes to open the source alone; the player ends the interaction and avoids replaying private contents in a public summary.
8. **A Message for Someone Else:** a capsule’s target does not match the selected survivor; the route refuses the association and preserves the capsule’s owner-defined recipient.

The bank scales through the four real capsule identities and varied consent/result conditions, not copies of their prose or dozens of near-identical grief vignettes. Any new authored capsule is a separate data-authority change and needs its own schema validation, owner registration, unlock contract, and content review.

### Field 05 expansion — Privacy, dignity, and recipient validation

Before showing capsule text, validate that the capsule owner allows access and that the selected recipient is permitted to see it. If an item was written for one survivor, another survivor cannot inherit the private message merely because they share a diagnosis or household. Public case lists display only a neutral status such as “legacy source available”; message text appears after deliberate selection. The player can exit without revealing the contents to the rest of the group.

The UI must avoid notifications that name a deceased person or sensitive relationship on a public dashboard. If the owner returns an identity mismatch, stale target, or unavailable content, the screen explains the limitation without exposing another survivor’s private text. No “comfort score” is included in a colony morale panel; the owner’s actual morale result is reported through its normal interface.

### Field 06 expansion — Cross-owner order and cancellation behavior

The operation sequence is: resolve the active survivor; check the capsule’s current visibility/open condition; request a private preview if supported; ask the survivor’s consent through the existing conversation choice; perform the owner’s open/read action; apply the returned morale/comfort exactly once through its owner; then refresh the medical case separately. Cancelling before the owner action produces no capsule state change. Closing after an accepted owner action cannot reopen or replay its reward. If the capsule has already been opened, the current owner’s repeat behavior governs the result.

An owner response can be `NOT_OPENABLE`, `TARGET_MISMATCH`, `ALREADY_OPENED`, `CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE`, `REFUSED_BY_SURVIVOR`, `OPENED`, or `NO_SUPPORTED_ROUTE` only where those distinctions match real returned state. The adapter must not invent hidden mutations to force these labels. Where the owner exposes only a boolean result, UI text stays within that contract and the unobservable distinctions remain prose-only.

### Field 07 expansion — Quiet-room interaction and optional audio

The interaction provides text-first presentation and never requires an audio recording to understand a legacy message. If a recording exists and audio accessibility settings permit it, playback is user initiated, uses current audio routing, and stops on close or scene change. Captions and a transcript respect the capsule’s privacy and consent state. A failed or missing audio cue falls back to text without repeating the owner action or blocking the conversation.

The visual focus is on the survivor’s decision, not on a collectible animation. The player can leave the source sealed, read its summary, or open the full content where the owner permits. Focus returns to the originating care card when the quiet-room view closes. The UI does not add an “open all capsules” convenience command, because bulk reveal would bypass survivor-specific consent.

### Field 08 expansion — Memorial language and clinical boundary

Copy separates sentimental value, bereavement comfort, morale change, and medical status. A high sentimental value is a property of capsule content and does not predict how a particular survivor will feel. A comfort calculation may be useful as one small owner result, but it is never described as a cure or as proof that a clinician’s work is unnecessary. The character can feel comfort and continue to grieve; the story can close with uncertainty.

The content review checks for coercive memorial participation, assumptions about family relationships, overgeneralized trauma responses, and public exposure of deceased survivors. An episode can end with “the message was not opened” and still be a complete, respectful player choice. The route avoids assigning blame for bereavement and never links acceptance of medical supplies to opening an intimate artifact.

### Field 09 expansion — Data access, repeated-open behavior, and storage

Capsule content is loaded only after the selected interaction asks for it. The outreach list stores the capsule ID and a transient display projection, not the message, item contents, target survivor, or sentimental score. The capsule owner retains opening condition and opened state. Survivor morale and bereavement effects remain in their existing state owner. After reload, outreach reconstructs its view from those sources and handles a retired/missing capsule ID with a neutral fallback.

The performance profile contains a long archive, repeated panel open/close, several patients, and audio playback interruption. It checks for one owner request per explicit selection, no per-frame comfort calculation, bounded transcript length, and released audio/event subscriptions. It does not pre-load every capsule while the player is reviewing triage priority.

### Field 10 expansion — Release evidence and quality gate

The first release candidate includes the nursery capsule only after the owner route proves target matching, open eligibility, private viewing, repeat behavior, save/restore, and exact-once morale/comfort outcome. The other three capsules remain `REVIEWED` or `HELD` until their own access and recipient rules are demonstrated. Acceptance includes refusal, mismatch, unopened, already-opened, source missing, current medical urgency, audio unavailable, close/reopen, and save/reload. The report lists which outcome belongs to which owner and includes no claims about mental-health treatment.

This pass extends outreach beyond a transactional visit into optional, humane continuity. It uses legacy content already present in the game and gives it a carefully bounded care context while preserving time-capsule, survivor, memorial, archive, medical, audio, and persistence authority.

## Pass 35 — Regional outreach stops at canonical settlements

This pass uses the newly integrated settlement catalog to give mobile outreach a regional itinerary and a concrete set of potential service contacts. It does not convert settlements into clinics or assume they have trained staff, beds, sterile supplies, maternal capacity, or disease containment. A destination is a place with current catalog facts. Medical capability must still come from a medical owner, a real staffed facility, and a reachable host route. The added feature is a site-by-site outreach schedule whose decisions include whether to travel, communicate remotely, ask permission, or close the request as unsupported.

### Field 01 expansion — Destination and capability are separate

Each stop references a canonical settlement and `location_id`, then asks the current travel owner to resolve a route. Settlement archetype, attitude, faction relation, and trade needs provide context only. They do not imply that the site has a clinic. A “mobile visit” means the player can reach and interact through an existing action; it is not a portable hospital object. `col_bldg_field_clinic` remains a colony building definition until a separate consumer proves staffing, care services, and player accessibility at a settlement.

Before scheduling, the board resolves service type and capability: general conversation, medical screening if supported, ward escalation if supported, maternal referral if supported, dependency support if supported, or no clinical action. A settlement with no qualified owner response can still host a consented request interview, but the UI must not call it treatment.

### Field 02 expansion — Twelve candidate outreach stops

| Stop | Canonical anchor | Outreach question, pending current owner evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Brine-Pan Hollow | `settlement_brine_pans` / `loc_settlement_brine_pans` | Can a resident request water/food guidance without conflating salt production with medical supply? |
| Iron Siding | `settlement_iron_siding` / `loc_settlement_iron_siding` | Is there a reachable private space for a consultation, or only a public rail-car meeting? |
| Cape Beacon Commune | `settlement_cape_beacon` / `loc_settlement_cape_beacon` | Can a message relay be used for follow-up if the physical route is unavailable? |
| Slate Hollow | `settlement_slate_hollow` / `loc_settlement_slate_hollow` | Does a quarry worker have a canonical survivor/roster record and consent? |
| Pilgrim Hearth | `settlement_pilgrim_hearth` / `loc_settlement_pilgrim_hearth` | Who may request a private referral without assuming one leader speaks for all? |
| Tinkers’ Notch | `settlement_tinkers_notch` / `loc_settlement_tinkers_notch` | Can a trader be asked to carry a sealed care message through an existing channel? |
| Ferry Crossing | `settlement_ferry_crossing` / `loc_settlement_ferry_crossing` | Does the travel owner expose a safe arrival/return path for a follow-up visit? |
| Nine Rails | `settlement_nine_rails` / `loc_settlement_nine_rails` | Can an interview be scheduled without exposing sensitive details in a freight notice? |
| Fort Karkov | `settlement_fort_karkov` / `loc_settlement_fort_karkov` | Is an entry/standing response compatible with an independent clinical conversation? |
| Lock Seven | `settlement_lock_seven` / `loc_settlement_lock_seven` | Are current territory conditions compatible with a return visit? |
| Silo Burrow | `settlement_silo_burrow` / `loc_settlement_silo_burrow` | Can a resident accept a private aid referral without public identification? |
| St. Nicholas | `settlement_st_nicholas` / `loc_settlement_st_nicholas` | Can a participant decline group care and request an individual follow-up? |

These are authoring questions, not existing services. Each row remains `CONTACT-CANDIDATE` until a canonical survivor, supported route, consent interaction, medical owner query, and result surface are verified. A missing survivor ID or clinical service leaves the row as an untracked conversation or makes it unavailable; it never creates a synthetic patient.

### Field 03 expansion — Itinerary records without a new scheduler

The itinerary projection contains stop ID, canonical settlement/location reference, current route quote if one exists, service topic, owner capability result, consent rule, optional communication route, visit status from a current quest/dispatch owner, and next supported action. It does not store a separate appointment date, travel duration, service capacity, staffing roster, or clinic resource count. If the current game has no scheduler command, the itinerary is ordered content shown to the player, not an automatic queue that dispatches visits.

The player can re-order stops only through an existing expedition/quest command. A refusal, missed route, delayed travel, or failed message updates only the corresponding owner. The outreach view refreshes its own projection and keeps unrelated stops available. Closing the panel never consumes supplies or advances the day.

### Field 04 expansion — Story arc: Twelve Doors, One Medical Kit

A traveling clinician carries a limited kit, but the game must not imply that carrying it grants a new treatment ability. At each stop, residents ask for different things: a private question, a route to an existing ward, a follow-up message, or no visit at all. The player first checks what the current medical owner can do and what the inventory owner actually contains. When the kit cannot satisfy a request, the clinician explains the limitation and offers a route or referral if one exists.

At the midpoint, a route is delayed by current territory/weather conditions and two stops compete for the remaining travel window. The player can postpone one visit, send a supported message, or return to the shelter; the game does not create an urgency timer or assign moral blame. At the finale, the clinician reports actual arrivals, declined visits, accepted referrals, and unserved requests separately. A single day can end with a partial circuit and still be a successful, truthful service story.

### Field 05 expansion — Three site-linked side arcs

**A Seat Behind the Rail Car** asks whether Iron Siding can provide a private interview area. It only succeeds if a current location/interaction owner exposes one; otherwise the player offers a message route or closes the request. **The Beacon Has No Clinic** follows a misleading sign that implies a lighthouse is a care site. The player corrects the description and routes residents to a real owner-backed medical option. **The Quiet Queue at Silo Burrow** lets a resident request help without being named publicly. The case panel stores only the minimum identifying reference supported by the care owner and does not broadcast it in the regional notice.

Other candidate stories use the same authored dimensions: private or group contact, available or unavailable route, referral accepted or declined, current owner result or unknown, and follow-up requested or refused. They are not copied scenes with swapped settlement names; each must use a canonical local detail and a distinct operational outcome.

### Field 06 expansion — Territory and travel handoff

Before every physical stop, the host asks the current map/travel and territory systems for the route/access result. Territory safety, contested status, trade tax, settlement attitude, and standing gates remain separate fields. None is a clinical risk score. If access is refused, the board gives the player a supported choice to defer, use an existing communication channel, or end the itinerary. It cannot assume that a medical team receives diplomatic immunity.

For remote contact, CommunicationsSystem owns transmission, interception, reply, and persistence. The payload preview states which details leave the shelter, and the player can cancel before sending. A successful send is not a consultation. A consultation is not a diagnosis. A reply is not proof that medicine was delivered.

### Field 07 expansion — Regional care board and patient privacy

The board shows settlement, visit state, service capability, last confirmed route/source, and one next action. It does not show public names, pregnancy stage, dependency status, triage priority, or memorial data on the regional map. Sensitive detail is fetched only after a player deliberately opens the selected case and the owner confirms access. The location list can be browsed without querying every survivor at every settlement.

When the player returns from a stop, a receipt summarizes what actually happened: arrival, conversation, referral request, transfer, or refusal. No combined green checkmark masks an incomplete care chain. Focus returns to the selected stop; an inaccessible route does not trap keyboard/controller users in a modal. The player can close the itinerary at any time and keep the original case status.

### Field 08 expansion — Content differences by community without stereotypes

Settlement archetypes are not medical capability labels. A monastery is not assumed to have a hospital; a stronghold is not assumed to have a surgeon; a refugee camp is not a single helpless patient; a trade post is not a secure privacy environment. Each named patient needs current canonical identity evidence and a voice/chronology check. Where none exists, dialogue uses a role placeholder or remains unbound content.

Consent has a separate scope for being visited, being examined, receiving an item, sharing details, being named in a public report, and receiving future contact. A patient may accept one and refuse another. Refusal does not penalize a settlement, lower reputation, or remove unrelated services. Language review treats maternal, dependency, grief, and triage cases with the same privacy and noncoercion rules used in the specialist passes.

### Field 09 expansion — Visit-volume performance and continuity

The itinerary page reads twelve static settlement anchors cheaply, but it does not eagerly load twelve territory histories, every faction quest, all survivor records, or all stock. Route/service data is queried after stop selection. The case detail fetches one survivor and only the required specialty owner projection. Transcript/history content is paged. On close, campaign change, patient removal, or route failure, the view releases all listeners.

Save review confirms that the true visit route and referral owner persist their actions. If no durable stop-order owner exists, the chosen itinerary order is transient and is not presented as an appointment schedule after reload. A campaign reload reconstructs actual completed actions from their owners and marks unresolved requests as needing review rather than replaying medical commands.

### Field 10 expansion — A reachable launch set, not twelve false clinics

The first tranche validates all twelve anchors and promotes only sites with a real route. One pilot should demonstrate one physical outreach visit; another should demonstrate a remote communication when travel is blocked. At least one specialty referral must complete end-to-end through its current medical host route before that specialty is called available in the itinerary. Remaining sites can still contribute to the regional story as requests, interviews, or unavailable destinations.

Acceptance includes accessible and blocked route, territorial/standing refusal, site with no patient, no supported clinic, inventory shortage, private-room claim unverified, consent declined, message intercepted, message sent without reply, patient unreachable, one completed care referral, one refused referral, and reload after accepted visit. The release report names reachable sites, supported specialties, owner results, and withheld rows. This expansion creates a broad, place-specific outreach programme while keeping clinical capacity and settlement state with their actual systems.

## Pass 36 — Patient autonomy, care choice, and community mediation

This pass adapts the integrated survivor autonomy and ideological-friction systems to mobile care without converting social behavior into clinical consent. `SurvivorAutonomySystem` can produce help, refusal, initiation, expression, or personal pursuit; `IdeologicalFrictionEvents` can produce confrontation, conversion, shelter-wide split, or mediation. Outreach can expose those current actions and route accepted nonclinical tasks through their real owners. It cannot override a patient’s refusal of treatment, disclosure, referral, capsule access, or personal-quest participation. The owner’s work-override mechanic applies only to its supported work action and consequences.

### Field 01 expansion — Separate autonomy facts from clinical consent

Every patient interaction scopes what the survivor agreed to: being visited, being examined, receiving a specific item, contacting a clinician, sharing a detail, or receiving future contact. An autonomy event is a separate fact. `refuse_exhaustion_duty` is not consent to care; `help_comfort_grieving` is not a clinical referral; `pursue_trauma_recovery` is not permission to reveal private history; and `help_share_rations` does not create treatment.

If the autonomy owner exposes a refusal, the interface explains its actual category and supported next step. A patient who refuses an examination keeps access to other accepted care options. No override control may invoke `OnWorkRefusalOverriddenSeam` for clinical consent. An urgent triage classification can inform the offer and its wording, but it does not erase the patient’s decision through outreach content.

### Field 02 expansion — Twenty autonomy templates as content references

The integrated catalog includes `help_comfort_grieving`, `help_mentor_skills`, `help_share_rations`, `help_relieve_workload`; `refuse_resentment_work`, `refuse_exhaustion_duty`, `refuse_trauma_danger`, `refuse_low_morale_drill`; `initiate_practice_session`, `initiate_hobby_craft`, `initiate_social_gathering`, `initiate_fortify_perimeter`; `express_praise_shelter`, `express_complain_rationing`, `express_duty_preference`, `express_faction_distrust`; and `pursue_mastery_project`, `pursue_reconciliation`, `pursue_trauma_recovery`, `pursue_memorial_tribute`.

Outreach neither copies these actions into a private catalog nor changes their deterministic triggers. It displays a related action only when the autonomy owner emits it for the canonical survivor. The content matrix records `action_id`, `patient_id`, `specialty_context`, `consent_scope`, `allowed_response`, `forbidden_interpretation`, and `owner_result`. A missing source fact means no event; authored prose cannot force one.

### Field 03 expansion — Autonomy-to-outreach response matrix

| Autonomy event | Permitted outreach response | Disallowed interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `help_comfort_grieving` | Offer private support or an existing memorial route | Clinical recovery or group-disclosure consent |
| `help_mentor_skills` | Ask whether mentoring can support a nonclinical role | Qualification to provide care without certification |
| `help_share_rations` | Confirm a wanted transfer and inventory availability | Nutrition treatment or referral completion |
| `help_relieve_workload` | Query the roster owner for a real duty change | Discharge from care or permanent staffing |
| `refuse_resentment_work` | Revisit a duty request through its owner | Refusal of medical examination |
| `refuse_exhaustion_duty` | Offer rest and query the schedule owner | Treatment refusal or failure state |
| `refuse_trauma_danger` | Respect refusal and offer another supported route | Permission to override through a work seam |
| `refuse_low_morale_drill` | Remove or defer the drill through its owner | Refusal of a clinic visit |
| `initiate_practice_session` | Offer scheduling if the hobby/training owner supports it | A clinical appointment |
| `initiate_hobby_craft` | Offer an optional hobby entry | Medical recommendation |
| `initiate_social_gathering` | Offer a voluntary group event after privacy review | Public patient disclosure |
| `initiate_fortify_perimeter` | Route a build request through its owner | A care task or new medical facility |
| `express_praise_shelter` | Record only through a supported source event | Automatic morale/reputation change |
| `express_complain_rationing` | Check real ration facts if requested | Proof medicine was missed |
| `express_duty_preference` | Query roster options with consent | Medical capacity or diagnosis |
| `express_faction_distrust` | Offer private contact choices | Faction change or refusal of all clinicians |
| `pursue_mastery_project` | Keep the goal separate from case closure | Discharge or treatment completion |
| `pursue_reconciliation` | Open the existing relationship route if requested | Mandatory family participation |
| `pursue_trauma_recovery` | Offer an existing referral if desired | Permission to reveal or diagnose progress |
| `pursue_memorial_tribute` | Offer the current memorial owner route | Bereavement resolved or capsule authorized |

The matrix is an authoring guard. The autonomy system supplies event occurrence; patient and medical owners supply consent/care results; none of the listed actions is a diagnostic result.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: A Visit With No Assignment

A mobile clinician arrives after a survivor declines a scheduled duty and requests rest. The player sees the actual refusal and asks whether the survivor wants a private check-in. The survivor may decline the visit but accept food; another person offers to help carry supplies; a third asks to join a group hobby after the clinical conversation. The player routes each choice separately: rest through the roster owner, food through inventory/needs, a group activity through `HobbySystem`, and care through the current medical owner. No single “visit complete” flag represents all four.

On the return trip, two survivors trigger an ideological confrontation over whether medical resources should be reserved for the shelter or shared with visitors. The player uses the event owner’s supported mediation choice. Affinity and morale change only through that owner; triage, stock, and settlement allegiance remain separate. The patient chooses whether to continue care, request an appointment, or close contact. The social dispute can remain unresolved without affecting the referral receipt.

### Field 05 expansion — Ideological cases without clinical discrimination

The current catalog includes `event_theological_dispute`, `event_martial_orders_clash`, `event_ration_hoarding_quarrel`, `event_superstition_science_schism`, `event_quiet_evangelism`, `event_pacifist_persuasion`, `event_bunker_faction_schism`, and `event_formal_mediation_quest`. Their affinity thresholds and effects stay with `IdeologicalFrictionEvents`. Outreach intersects them only when the current event target and context genuinely overlap a care scene.

An ideology label never selects care priority. The ward owner continues triage independently while a policy dispute is mediated. A conversion attempt does not change consent; a shelter split does not cancel a referral. If a patient asks that their condition remain private, the privacy rule blocks it even when an ideological event is active.

### Field 06 expansion — Side-quest paths with patient-controlled exits

**The Unassigned Chair** follows a work refusal, checks an actual rest/roster option, and returns to the care case without assigning a diagnosis. **Carry Only What Was Asked For** follows a help offer and a separate inventory transfer. **A Message Without a Name** uses an existing communication route only if it can represent the minimum payload. **The Quiet Mediator** follows an emitted ideology event and reaches its supported mediation quest. **Practice Tomorrow** offers a hobby session through its owner, not a therapy proxy. **The Door Stays Shut** lets a patient refuse a private legacy or memorial interaction while the care episode continues.

Each quest names its actual completion source. The player can stop a conversation without deleting a referral. A referral can finish while ideological conflict continues. Mediation can close without changing the patient’s mind or treatment plan.

### Field 07 expansion — Owner events and notification design

The outreach host listens to autonomy/ideology event seams only while the relevant view is active. It identifies the canonical survivor, event kind, supported options, and source fact, then routes the chosen action through the existing system. It never triggers an autonomy evaluation from panel open, refresh, or medical day tick. Notifications stay concise and keep diagnosis/private text off shared dashboards. A notice can announce an available conversation without broadcasting its contents.

Medical facts are queried separately before a care action appears. If a patient becomes unavailable, the social event remains with its owner and the referral keeps its state. Removing a survivor closes stale private details and re-resolves any remaining state. A binding failure in one system cannot erase another owner’s event.

### Field 08 expansion — Refusal-safe UX and accessibility

Decline, defer, and close are visible actions. The player can refuse a group event, keep a medical visit private, and honor autonomy without losing unrelated functionality. A work override requires an explicit consequence summary and remains unavailable for treatment, privacy, memorial access, or personal-quest consent. The interface identifies work and care owners so a disabled action cannot be mistaken for a clinical judgment.

Screen readers announce a patient name only after the case opens; public notifications use neutral text. Color and affinity graphs are supplementary. Keyboard/controller navigation preserves focus through concurrent updates. Alerts follow the current accessibility coordinator and coalescing behavior rather than introducing a parallel notification system.

### Field 09 expansion — Save and deterministic lifecycle

Autonomy probability, trait/affinity scaling, cooldown, goals, and actions remain saved by `SurvivorAutonomySystem`. Ideological affinity, conversion, mediation, and split state stay with `IdeologicalFrictionEvents`. Treatment and referrals persist through current medical owners. Outreach saves no local duplicate consent, patient condition, or ideology choice unless the campaign owner already supports an explicit reference.

Reload queries each owner, verifies that pending events are not applied twice, and ensures a care receipt does not reapply morale. A closed case does not reopen merely because a personal autonomy goal remains active. Long-run profiling covers many survivors and simultaneous cases without a per-frame colony scan; disposed views release subscriptions.

### Field 10 expansion — Narrow end-to-end pilot

The pilot proves one emitted autonomy event and one emitted ideology event in a reachable outreach route. It includes a patient declining care, one supported nonclinical help action, a medical option remaining available after refusal, one mediation result, and save/reload. A separate acceptance case confirms the work-override seam cannot be called from a care-consent control. Authored dialogue-only cards are counted separately from reachable stories.

Acceptance covers all autonomy kinds; each refusal; event thresholds; consent combinations; patient removal; no-op and accepted paths; duplicate event; medical-triage independence; private-text exposure; accessible alert behavior; same-seed replay; and owner restore. Promotion requires exact current APIs, host routes, and focused tests under the eventual package owner. This pass puts survivor agency into medical outreach without turning care into a coercive event tree.

## Pass 37 — Research-backed care capabilities across the referral network

The integrated `ResearchUnlockBridge` maps completed research to canonical item, recipe, shelter, medical, combat, and expedition capabilities. This pass makes outreach aware of clinical protocols without adding its own technology tree or claiming that research itself provides treatment. The initial medical targets include `unlock_field_trauma_surgery` → `medical_procedure_field_trauma`, `unlock_pathogen_isolation` → `medical_procedure_quarantine_isolation`, and `unlock_chelation_infusion` → `medical_procedure_chelation_infusion`. Existing ward, surgical, antenatal, dependency, disease, pharmaceutical, and inventory owners remain responsible for capability, patient eligibility, action, supplies, and outcome.

### Field 01 expansion — Unlock, capability, and treatment are separate

An outreach case can ask whether a protocol is researched, whether the clinical owner currently recognizes it, whether the selected provider/facility can perform it, whether required supplies are present, and whether the patient consents. These are independent facts. `unlock_field_trauma_surgery` does not create a mobile operating room; `unlock_pathogen_isolation` does not guarantee a negative-pressure bed; `unlock_chelation_infusion` does not diagnose contamination or stock an infusion. If the current owner lacks a player-facing capability query, the case remains a referral question rather than a button.

The referral screen reports only the highest confirmed step. It may say “protocol unlocked” but cannot say “care available” unless the current medical owner accepts that procedure for the patient and location. A successful procedure command, if supported, returns an owner receipt. The outreach module does not consume research unlocks or apply treatment effects itself.

### Field 02 expansion — Protocol handoff table

| Research unlock | Target procedure | Referral story use | Required owner answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unlock_field_trauma_surgery` | `medical_procedure_field_trauma` | A field injury needs a ward-level follow-up | Eligibility, facility, clinician, sterile supplies, accepted action |
| `unlock_pathogen_isolation` | `medical_procedure_quarantine_isolation` | A possible transmission chain needs separation guidance | Disease/triage owner status, bed/isolation capacity, consent, result |
| `unlock_chelation_infusion` | `medical_procedure_chelation_infusion` | A survivor asks whether exposure care is available | Exposure source, diagnosis owner, ward, protocol, supplies, result |

The content cannot create its own symptoms, exposure, diagnosis, or procedural eligibility from a settlement visit. A patient may ask a question and receive “we cannot determine that here” as a valid result. A referral to the appropriate existing ward is distinct from dispatch, arrival, triage, and treatment.

### Field 03 expansion — Research-aware referral journey

When a case opens, the host checks the current research bridge only for the target procedure that the patient’s owner-backed case calls for. If the protocol is not unlocked, the clinician explains that limitation and queries the ordinary supported care path. If it is unlocked, the host asks the medical owner to validate actual capability. It then checks supply availability, patient consent, and reachable destination. The player confirms dispatch only after receiving those facts. Each step can refuse independently.

This does not create a multi-step clinic scheduler. If the current dispatch owner supports one referral at a time, the content queues only through that route or creates separate accepted requests. The plan cannot maintain a parallel waitlist to simulate clinical capacity. The player can close the case and return later to a current owner query.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: The Procedure in the Ledger

A traveling clinician finds a field injury and remembers that the shelter researched advanced trauma surgery. The player sees the unlock, but the nearest outreach stop lacks a verified surgical facility. The survivor can accept a route to the current ward, decline travel, or ask for nonclinical assistance that is supported. If the ward owner accepts the referral and the sterile-supply gate passes, the player may dispatch. The resulting outcome comes from the surgical owner; no story text guarantees success.

In a second chapter, an infection concern raises the possibility of isolation. The research unlock exists, but the disease owner and ward report no current capacity. The player may ask the person’s consent for a remote message, wait, or use a currently available alternative. Another survivor refuses a public isolation label; the interface hides the sensitive status while still showing operational capability to the player with appropriate access. At close, the case distinguishes protocol researched, capacity unavailable, consent choice, and any actual referral result.

### Field 05 expansion — Specialized side-quest matrix

**The Bed Is Not a Protocol** asks the player to compare a research unlock with actual ward readiness and ends when the owner provides a capability response. **Two Filters and a Missing Receipt** follows a suspected exposure but verifies supplies through inventory and a clinical owner, not prose. **Leave the Name Off the Board** lets a patient request privacy while the player checks an isolation route. **The Long Road to the Ward** follows an accepted dispatch through current travel conditions and returns the actual arrival result. **A Protocol for Someone Else** handles a patient who is not eligible for the unlocked procedure, showing the refusal reason. **Research Finished Yesterday** begins after a successful unlock event but does not retroactively treat a previous case.

Each side quest’s `success_fact` points to one owner: research bridge, medical owner, inventory, communications, or travel. A chain can close as “referral offered and declined” or “destination unavailable” without faking a procedure. Rewards are not invented; if the research/procedure owner returns a result with a morale/item effect, it is applied exactly once through its owning delegate seam.

### Field 06 expansion — Existing pathways remain first-class

Research-gated capability cannot hide ordinary care. If a specialized protocol is locked or unavailable, the medical owner may still offer general care, triage, safe observation, or a referral. Outreach must not make the new unlock a mandatory gate on the existing antenatal, ward, dependency, disease, or pharmaceutical paths. A scenario can teach the player that research improves options, but it cannot tell them that a patient is untreated merely because a specific advanced procedure is absent.

If a specialist route is already integrated, this pass adds a capability check only when that route actually consumes the research bridge. It must not duplicate clinical triage or route around the current ward’s supply checks. Existing closeout chains and clinic destinations remain collision exclusions; the settlement itinerary supplies context, not a new care facility.

### Field 07 expansion — Capability comparison and patient-facing language

The case view groups information into `Research`, `Facility`, `Supplies`, `Patient Choice`, and `Referral Result`. A small progress indicator may show which checks have returned, but it is not a clinical-risk bar. If the user selects an unavailable procedure, text quotes the owner reason and offers a real alternative. The screen differentiates “not researched,” “researched but facility unavailable,” “facility exists but supplies missing,” “patient declined,” and “procedure accepted” only when the host can prove each status.

No public colony notice names the procedure or patient unless the patient consents to that disclosure and a communications owner can send the message. The player can return to the prior outreach site; focus and selected case remain stable. Keyboard/controller controls do not send a referral when merely expanding the protocol details.

### Field 08 expansion — Clinical ethics and accessibility

An unlock is a capability, not a value judgment about a person. Copy does not call a patient “unworthy” or “too difficult” because they do not meet protocol conditions. Research availability is not presented as the clinician’s competence. A patient’s refusal is not overridden through the work refusal seam. Information about pathogen isolation or contamination is hidden from public list panels and is shared only through authorized owner routes.

The user can review plain-language procedure descriptions, content warnings, side effects only when the medical owner provides them, and the exact recipient of a message. Audio is optional and captions remain available. Disabled options carry written explanations. A no-action path preserves dignity and prevents a player from feeling forced to invent care through an unsupported interaction.

### Field 09 expansion — Deterministic unlock and save behavior

Research completion/unlock state stays with the bridge; medical readiness and procedure outcomes stay with their clinical owners; referral/dispatch stays with the current quest or travel owner; supplies remain in inventory. The campaign stores stable references only if its existing owner supports them. A reload re-queries current capability and does not rerun an unlock event or procedure. A past case uses its archived result rather than reevaluating current research as if it had existed at the time.

The performance profile uses many survivor cases, all three target protocols, many incomplete research nodes, and a full clinical ward. Opening the regional itinerary loads no medical details. Selecting one case triggers bounded unlock and clinical queries. Listener cleanup is tested on patient removal and campaign replacement. Determinism checks ensure that reading a capability does not advance research, RNG, day, or treatment progression.

### Field 10 expansion — Two-route release pilot

Pilot one demonstrates an unlocked trauma protocol that is either accepted by a real ward route or truthfully refused with a supported referral alternative. Pilot two demonstrates an unavailable isolation protocol despite research unlock, with privacy preserved and ordinary care still available. A chelation case remains held until the current exposure/diagnosis owner can prove what initiates it. The package lists exact host call sites and does not claim all research-backed medicine is reachable from mobile outreach.

Acceptance covers protocol locked/unlocked; wrong target; no facility; full ward; no sterile supply; patient ineligible; consent declined; travel closed; dispatch accepted/refused; procedure accepted/completed; reload after each supported boundary; public/private notice; stale unlock ID; research completed during an open case; and current-care fallback. Focused tests belong to the eventual integration package. This pass increases care options through the game’s actual research contract while keeping clinical decision-making and outcomes with medical owners.
## Pass 38 — Clinical logistics for a mobile-care deployment

This pass develops the outreach vehicle as a logistics and access platform, not as a second clinic system. VehicleCustomizationSystem owns modules, slot limits, cargo projections, living capability, base-camp deploy/pack operations, survivor rest capacity, and its save path. ExpeditionSystem owns destinations, route acceptance, travel, and expedition outcomes. Clinical owners decide what care can be offered, which patient is eligible, what supplies are required, whether the patient consents, and what result follows. Inventory remains the item authority. The outreach plan coordinates these facts into one readable dispatch decision without copying any of them.

No verified current contract establishes that a vehicle cargo module provides sterile storage, a refrigerated medicine compartment, treatment capacity, or a clinic-room effect. Existing shelter/batch preservation owners remain authoritative for the item classes and processing paths they already cover; the gap here is the mobile transport bridge and its receiving clinical route. Until those owners supply a usable transport result, the plan does not claim that an outreach trip altered medicine viability or safe storage.

### Field 01 expansion — Separate transport capacity from clinical capability

The visit review asks two different questions. First, can the vehicle reach and stage at this destination under current expedition and vehicle rules? Second, can a current medical owner accept the requested service at that place, for this patient, with the available canonical supplies and valid consent? A yes to the first question does not imply a yes to the second. A vehicle with cargo capacity is not an operating room, isolation ward, pharmacy, or maternity unit.

The player may still conduct supported nonclinical activity at a reachable stop: listening, referral intake, public-health information from an existing source, follow-up conversation, or returning a patient request. The route is marked clinical only when a medical action owner accepts a treatment command and produces a receipt. The UI never converts a transport module into a clinical facility by description alone.

### Field 02 expansion — Deployment compatibility matrix

| Owner result | Outreach use | Required second answer | No unsupported claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expedition accepts canonical stop | Add stop to current route review | Vehicle route projection and destination still valid | No clinic operation automatically exists |
| Vehicle reports cargo capacity | Check requested canonical item list | Inventory availability and expedition load acceptance | No item was consumed or preserved by capacity alone |
| Vehicle is mobile-base-capable | Offer camp deployment where route permits | Vehicle deployment receipt and pack path | No sterile, private, or climate-controlled room |
| Vehicle bunk rest accepts survivor | Offer a rest action within bunk cap | Survivor eligibility and vehicle action result | No treatment, cure, or consent |
| Research unlock indicates a medical procedure | Display protocol readiness | Medical owner facility, provider, patient, item, consent checks | No field treatment solely from the unlock |

The matrix is a view contract. It does not add a mobile-clinic counter or attempt to predict medical outcomes in the outreach panel.

### Field 03 expansion — Pre-departure checklist and staged receipt

The player selects a real settlement/stop, a visit purpose, and one or more patients only when a patient-facing owner exposes that selection. The review lists target, route, vehicle profile, cargo request, intended conversation or referral, medical preconditions, and the consent state returned by its owner. Each line has a source. The player may remove an optional request, change to a nonclinical visit, or postpone.

The dispatch is staged in phases. Expedition acceptance resolves travel; vehicle deployment confirms camp state if requested; inventory/expedition owners confirm cargo; the medical owner accepts eligible commands at the destination; and the visit journal captures returned outcomes. A refusal or unavailable item at any stage stops only the dependent action. It does not invalidate unrelated conversations or erase an accepted route. No composite “clinic ready” rating hides the reason.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: The Cool Box With No Circuit

A mobile team receives three requests in different settlements. A patient asks for a trauma follow-up, a parent asks whether medicine will survive the trip, and a local worker wants to speak privately. The vehicle reaches the first location and has room for the canonical supplies accepted by the expedition owner. The medical owner returns that a ward-level procedure cannot run at this camp. The parent’s medicine is present, but the game returns no cold-chain status. The worker agrees to a private conversation through the supported social route.

The player can refer the trauma case to a clinic, record the medicine-storage question without promising safety, and complete the consented conversation. A later stop has a valid facility handoff and the patient accepts the appointment. The episode closes on accurate limits rather than failed heroics: the mobile team brought people into contact with care, but did not pretend the vehicle replaced the ward or clinical owner. The unresolved cold-chain question becomes a clearly written architecture gap, not an invisible timer in the story.

### Field 05 expansion — Visit and logistics record bank

**The Ward Is Two Roads Away** validates the route and referral owner separately. **Enough Room for Gauze** checks item identity, quantity, cargo capacity, and load receipt without consuming stock on preview. **The Tent Is Not a Theatre** presents a procedure unlock while the facility owner refuses a field operation. **A Patient’s Own Schedule** lets a consenting patient choose an eligible follow-up window only if a current owner exposes one. **The Seat Home** uses vehicle bunk and rest capacity; it does not change triage priority.

**A Box, No Temperature** records an unanswered storage question and blocks spoilage claims. **The Driver Needs a Break** exposes only supported rest options for the driver and crew. **An Empty Medical Shelf** follows a canonical inventory query to a resupply/crafting route. **A Private Word at the Gate** uses the social/consent route without publishing the patient’s diagnosis. **Road Closed, Referral Open** lets the team communicate an existing referral even when travel is refused, if a supported comms route exists. **No Patient Selected** keeps a public information stop playable without inventing a patient. **Return the Kit** confirms only the inventory owner’s receipt if items were actually consumed or transferred.

These story cards create distinct logistical outcomes: care action accepted, referral made, conversation held, supply missing, route blocked, patient declines, or a technical capability remains unknown. They do not use a single success flag to grade patient cooperation.

### Field 06 expansion — Consent, transfer, and clinical order of operations

Medical consent is recorded by the clinical owner and is never inferred from autonomy help offers, vehicle occupancy, expedition assignment, family relationship, or a prior visit. A patient can refuse a procedure and still accept information or a future referral. A guardian/next-of-kin proxy is used only when the current clinical system permits it. If the patient cannot be selected through a valid owner route, the story remains generalized and non-identifying.

Transport can be accepted before clinical action, and clinical care may require a separate location/facility. The itinerary cannot execute a transfer by moving a survivor ID between lists. The responsible medical or roster owner must provide the handoff. The dispatch board shows waiting, accepted, refused, and unavailable as separate owner results. Urgent triage remains with the existing clinical/needs owner; a narrative urgency tag cannot leapfrog that logic.

### Field 07 expansion — Supply custody and mobile preservation bridge

This plan does not add an outreach inventory. It requests item IDs and quantities from the canonical inventory and cargo owners, receives their accept/refuse receipts, and records an action receipt only after an existing medical or logistics consumer changes state. A preview cannot consume an item, craft a substitute, or reserve stock. If the game has no reservation contract, competing requests are resolved by the item owner when each real operation is submitted.

The vehicle-to-medical-storage bridge is a separate candidate feature with an explicit prerequisite decision. Its owner would need to identify which existing item or batch IDs are covered by FoodTypeSystem, LyophilizationSystem, CryoVaultSystem, the clinical refrigeration load, or another canonical medical owner; which actual vehicle equipment and power receipt applies; what duration is already tracked; and how transit interruption is represented by that owner. If an existing batch already has an expiry/viability result, the outreach panel reads it instead of starting a second clock. Any new transport effect must enter canonical inventory/medical state through its owner and preserve that owner’s deterministic save path. Until a verified route answers, dialogue says “mobile storage condition not verified” rather than asserting spoilage or safety.

### Field 08 expansion — Visit board and accessible feedback

The UI stages route, travel, vehicle, supply, consent, and clinical status in that order. Only one primary action is highlighted at a time; a patient-sensitive action requires an explicit private confirmation and states its consequence. The route detail does not expose a public diagnosis. Focus returns to the patient or stop just completed, and keyboard/controller back exits review without submitting an operation.

Rows identify whether the result came from route, vehicle, inventory, medical, consent, or story owner. A tooltip is not the sole place for a blocker; screen readers announce the reason inline. Clinic-required and referral-only states use words and symbols as well as color. Long itineraries load compact stop summaries, with patient detail resolved on demand after privacy authorization. Audio cues respect accessibility settings and avoid sounding like an emergency alarm for ordinary deferral.

### Field 09 expansion — Persistence, event ordering, and load

Existing route, vehicle, inventory, patient, and clinical save owners restore their own state. The outreach campaign stores only a stable stop or action reference in the current quest/journal authority. It cannot keep medicine expiration, patient treatment, occupied beds, cargo totals, or clinic inventory in a parallel save section. On reload, completed procedures are not resent; a missing action receipt produces a “verify with owner” state rather than a duplicate procedure.

The schedule is command-driven and deterministic. Opening the dispatch panel cannot advance days, expire medicine, use seeded RNG, change a route, or apply healing. Stop lists are fetched for the chosen expedition and filtered in memory only for display. A performance profile covers a long route, many patient request summaries, full cargo, multiple referrals, and panel disposal/reopen. Any owner event subscriptions must be removed when the route panel closes.

### Field 10 expansion — Two-stop pilot and acceptance gates

The pilot uses two canonical stops: one where only a referral/conversation is available and one where a current clinical owner accepts a specific procedure after its own eligibility, supply, facility, and consent checks. One vehicle with a living module can deploy and pack camp; a second vehicle without mobile-base capability proves the itinerary still handles a nondeployment stop. Cargo capacity is tested with an absent and present item, while preview remains side-effect-free.

Acceptance covers unreachable settlement, invalid route, no compatible vehicle, camp refusal, insufficient cargo, absent item, item available but procedure unsupported at field site, protocol unlocked but facility absent, patient refusal, private discussion, transfer not accepted, repeat dispatch after reload, missing owner receipt, capacity boundary, and unknown cold-chain data. Reviewers trace every clinical effect to its owner, every route to ExpeditionSystem, every module/cargo fact to VehicleCustomizationSystem, and every item count to canonical inventory. The pilot is promoted only when a host route can produce those receipts end to end. This adds operational depth to outreach while leaving treatment, consent, inventory, and any future storage mechanic with the systems that own them.
