## Pass 38 supplemental story continuity rules

An outreach episode is not graded by how many procedures the player completes. It can succeed by listening, honoring a refusal, reaching an accepting provider, clarifying a missing capability, or accurately recording an unresolved supply issue. The debrief uses distinct wording for “visit delivered,” “referral accepted,” “patient declined,” “route unavailable,” and “owner result pending.” It avoids “treated” unless the clinical owner returned a treatment receipt.

Patient names and diagnoses appear only in an authorized private surface. Public settlement updates summarize service availability and route status without identifying individuals. If later episodes refer to an earlier case, they query the campaign/medical journal for an allowed stable reference; they do not store a shadow health history in scenario state.
## Pass 38 worked sequence — Two stops, one referral, no false clinic

This playthrough exercises a mobile care route and demonstrates how transport, supply, consent, and treatment remain separate owner decisions.

1. The player opens a route containing two canonical settlement stops and one unresolved request. The unresolved request remains a map/communications task until a real destination and route reference exist.
2. The expedition owner returns a valid route to stop A and a conditional route to stop B. The player sees route conditions and chooses a plan without creating a local travel clock.
3. VehicleCustomizationSystem reports cargo projection and mobile-base capability for the chosen vehicle. The outreach UI does not call the vehicle a clinic.
4. Inventory returns the requested kit items and one absent item. The player may remove the absent item from the dispatch preview or use a real resupply route. Nothing is consumed while reviewing.
5. A survivor refuses to ride on the trip. The route owner decides whether the remaining crew is eligible; the social refusal is honored and the roster is not rewritten by narrative code.
6. At stop A, a patient requests a trauma follow-up. The medical owner reports that the research protocol exists but the current stop lacks an accepted treatment facility.
7. The patient chooses whether to accept a referral. Their consent is checked by the clinical owner; the autonomy system’s unrelated help events are not used as medical consent.
8. The referral owner accepts a handoff to a canonical clinic. The outreach journal stores the returned referral reference, not a duplicate diagnosis or treatment schedule.
9. The patient’s relative asks what was found. The private record route refuses disclosure without authorization. The player can share a general service update that contains no private diagnosis.
10. At stop B, the vehicle owner accepts a camp deployment. The team holds a private conversation only if the current scene/consent route can provide that state; camp deployment itself does not guarantee privacy.
11. Another resident asks whether a medicine remained cool. Existing medical batch or shelter preservation owners may report their own expiry/viability state, but no vehicle-transit result has been verified for this route. The team records the mobile condition as unverified and avoids either spoilage or safety claims.
12. The player submits a supported clinical action for a different consenting patient. The medical owner accepts it and returns a treatment receipt; only then does the journal use the word “treated.”
13. The vehicle rests one eligible crew member within its bunk cap. This action has its own receipt and does not alter treatment or patient triage.
14. The player packs camp and follows the accepted return route. The system prevents a second submission of a completed procedure after route refresh or save/reload.
15. The debrief separates referral accepted, conversation held, treatment returned, storage unknown, and route completed. The episode can conclude with useful follow-up even though a requested mobile surgery did not occur.

Failure rehearsal covers a route closing before stop B, the referral destination disappearing, the patient declining, a required item being unavailable, the medical owner returning pending, the camp action being refused, and the old save lacking a referral reference. Each branch blocks only dependent actions and avoids inventing medical or transportation state.
## Pass 39 — Outpost care relays, radio referral, and continuity of treatment

This pass expands outreach through ColonySystem, CommunicationsSystem, DiseaseSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, AudioAccessibilityCoordinator, and the existing research bridge. A colony field-clinic building definition, a communications relay, a received message, and an actual clinical action remain separate facts. The outreach plan creates a distributed referral route only when each owner returns a valid result. It does not create a second patient registry, clinic inventory, disease ledger, or radio network.

### Field 01 expansion — Colony destination eligibility

ColonySystem owns canonical colony types, building construction, capacity, garrison, supply lines, daily consumption, condition, and save/restore. Its current catalog includes col_bldg_field_clinic and col_bldg_comm_relay. The outreach browser may show these as infrastructure facts when ColonySystem returns them for a canonical outpost or settlement. A building definition alone does not prove staffing, treatment availability, privacy, or an accepted patient route.

The stop card therefore separates COLONY_EXISTS, BUILDING_PRESENT, CLINICAL_ROUTE_VERIFIED, and REFERRAL_ACCEPTED. Only the last two can support clinical wording. If the host has no clinical consumer for the field-clinic building, the card remains a destination/infrastructure story and offers a referral or conversation route instead of a treatment button.

### Field 02 expansion — Communications relay and message custody

CommunicationsSystem determines whether a comm relay, antenna, frequency, condition, range, jam state, and decoding workflow support an outgoing referral or incoming patient message. The outreach panel submits a message only through the communications owner and records its returned transmission receipt. A broadcast reaching the relay does not prove that a clinician read it, a bed exists, or a patient consented.

Messages are classified as SENT, RECEIVED, DECODED, ACKNOWLEDGED, or CLINICAL_ACTION_ACCEPTED. The panel never promotes RECEIVED to TREATED. A missing acknowledgment can still support a patient-facing “we sent the request” outcome. A decoded message with unknown source is not used to identify a patient or reveal a private record.

### Field 03 expansion — Disease and referral triage

DiseaseSystem remains the authority for canonical disease definitions, vector, clinical stage, diagnostic tells, treatment effects, protocol maintenance, and expiry. Outreach can display a diagnostic clue or refer a case only when the medical owner provides an allowed projection. It cannot diagnose from prose, assign a disease from a radio message, or use urgency text to bypass triage.

The referral card displays severity source when available, distinguishing dose-derived severity from illness-derived severity. A patient may receive education, a test request, isolation guidance, or a clinical referral as separate actions. Isolation capacity belongs to the disease/medical owner and a field-clinic building does not create negative-pressure capability unless the owner returns it.

### Field 04 expansion — Supply-line and kit continuity

Colony supply lines may report delivery status and colony supplies; they do not automatically transfer a medical kit into a patient action. Inventory remains canonical. The outreach board can ask whether a requested item is at the outpost, whether a supply-line receipt exists, and whether the medical owner accepts that item for the selected action.

An interrupted supply line creates a logistics case, not an invented shortage number in outreach. A delivered crate is not consumed until a medical/crafting owner accepts its use. The plan supports three player choices: wait for the current route, send an accepted replacement request, or downgrade to education/referral. No action changes colony consumption or supply-line condition outside its owner.

### Field 05 expansion — Storyline: The Relay at North Watch

The team receives a message from North Watch, a canonical outpost with a communications relay and a field-clinic building. ColonySystem confirms the buildings, CommunicationsSystem confirms the message, and the medical owner reports that no current clinical route is bound to that outpost. The player can answer with first-aid information, send a referral request to the nearest verified clinic, or travel if ExpeditionSystem accepts the route.

On the second day, the outpost supply line returns a delayed receipt. A field nurse asks for a specific item, but inventory reports the item is absent at the main shelter. The player sends a communications request and opens a supported crafting/resupply route. A later acknowledgment confirms the request was read. The patient’s treatment remains pending until a medical owner accepts it. The chapter closes with a documented relay, an honest supply delay, and a human connection that never pretended a building was a staffed hospital.

### Field 06 expansion — Privacy across radio and colony boundaries

Patient identity, diagnosis, consent, and treatment outcome remain private owner facts. The communications message contains the minimum allowed referral fields, not a full medical record. Colony public boards show service availability and route status, while private clinical surfaces show patient detail only after authorization. A relay operator cannot reveal a patient’s condition merely because they received a transmission.

When a message is intercepted or decoded by an unauthorized party, CommunicationsSystem reports the event. Outreach can create a trust or privacy follow-up through existing social/quest owners, but it cannot rewrite the medical record or invent a breach consequence. If no current communications privacy response exists, the episode records the uncertainty and avoids naming a culprit.

### Field 07 expansion — Audio, visual, and notification lifecycle

A medical emergency uses the existing cue_medical_emergency; a radio referral uses cue_radio_incoming_signal; an expedition return uses cue_expedition_returned. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator supplies visual labels, coalescing, ducking, and reduced-stimulation behavior. The outreach route does not add duplicate alert banners or a second sound manager.

Notifications are scoped to the active player surface and remain readable in a quiet mode. A critical medical cue is not suppressed merely because a radio message occurred within the same frame; the coordinator owns category and timing behavior. Closing the panel unregisters listeners. Reopening it queries current owner state rather than replaying all past alerts.

### Field 08 expansion — Archive and continuity

ShelterArchiveSystem can record a referral decision, a medical milestone, a communication receipt, or a memorial event under its canonical categories. Outreach requests archival entries only through the archive owner. It does not keep a duplicate chronology or paste private diagnoses into the institutional timeline. The player can search for a public milestone such as “North Watch referral accepted” if the source permits it.

An archived message is historical. Current colony, supply, disease, and clinical state may differ. The UI presents historical receipt and current projection in separate sections. If the archive lacks a source or privacy flag, the detail is withheld. A repeated archive request must be idempotent or rejected by the owner.

### Field 09 expansion — Save, deterministic routing, and scale

Colony, communications, disease, inventory, expedition, archive, and audio owners persist and restore their own state. Outreach stores only stable action/quest references. Reload must not resend a message, re-consume a supply, retrigger a disease treatment, repeat a notification, or duplicate an archive entry.

A route list with many colonies loads metadata first and resolves patient detail for the selected stop. Message histories are paged. Daily colony and disease ticks remain owner work; opening outreach is read-only. Same-seed tests compare message decoding, supply-line result, referral order, and archive IDs for equal state. Missing old-save references render as unavailable rather than being rebound to a similarly named colony.

### Field 10 expansion — Two-outpost launch gates

The launch slice uses North Watch and Relay Tower, one comm relay, one field-clinic building definition, one verified distant clinic, one delayed supply line, one consenting patient, and one patient who declines. It proves infrastructure visibility, message send/receive, referral acceptance, privacy filtering, supply status, and archival receipt. It also includes a build-present but clinical-route-unverified branch.

Promotion requires exact owner receipts for every clinical word, no duplicate message or supply transfer, accessible notification behavior, deterministic reload, and a clear fallback when a colony route cannot provide care. A missing patient route does not block all outreach play; it narrows the episode to communication, education, or referral. The plan remains compatible with current colony and disease authorities.

## Pass 40 — Patient education, leisure, and seasonal care continuity

This pass expands outreach beyond transport by composing SurvivorEducationSystem, HobbySystem, SeasonalCelebrationSystem, NuclearWinterProgressionSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and Archive owners with the existing medical route. Education can explain care; hobbies can support patient-led connection; celebrations can mark recovery; weather can change access timing. None of these systems diagnoses, treats, or stores a second patient record.

### Field 01 expansion — Education as information, not treatment

SurvivorEducationSystem owns curriculum, age stage, teacher/student assignment, prerequisites, study, graduation, knowledge pool, and persistence. Outreach may ask the education owner for a health-literacy or first-aid lesson if a canonical subject exists. The lesson can improve knowledge only through the education owner. It cannot provide immunity, reduce disease stage, or substitute for a clinical action.

Patient-facing text distinguishes information offered, lesson accepted, lesson completed, and treatment accepted. A patient can refuse a lesson while accepting a referral. A caregiver can attend a class without being authorized to see a patient’s private record.

### Field 02 expansion — Hobby and social recovery

HobbySystem owns leisure sessions, facility requirements, group participation, mastery, affinity, morale, and save. Outreach may offer music, craft, writing, map-making, or social sessions as a voluntary recovery-adjacent activity. A hobby cannot heal or alter a clinical stage. If the owner returns a morale effect, it remains a hobby result.

The content avoids treating leisure as compulsory therapy. The patient chooses whether to attend where the owner allows; a refusal is preserved without lowering medical eligibility. A group session may occur at a shelter, colony, or outpost only when facility and participant queries succeed.

### Field 03 expansion — Seasonal access and appointment timing

NuclearWinterProgressionSystem and WeatherCascadeSystem provide phase, season, temperature, daylight, hazard, delay, and closure facts. Outreach uses them to display appointment timing, route closure, and supply pressure. It does not create a seasonal disease or infer that cold weather changed a patient’s diagnosis.

SeasonalCelebrationSystem can supply a community gathering where general health education occurs. The event’s resources, participants, streak, and skip penalty remain with the celebration owner. A celebration is not a clinic, and a holiday invitation is not consent to a medical action.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: The Winter Lesson

An outpost asks for a care visit during deep winter. The route owner reports a delay, the communications owner confirms the message was received, and the medical owner says the clinical appointment cannot occur at the outpost. The player offers a general hygiene and referral lesson through SurvivorEducationSystem, which a caregiver accepts while the patient declines.

During a later harvest observance, the community holds a voluntary hobby session. HobbySystem reports participation and a morale result. WeatherCascadeSystem then opens a route window, and ExpeditionSystem accepts travel to a verified clinic. The patient consents to a clinical assessment; only the medical owner returns treatment. The story honors all three forms of agency: information, leisure, and care.

### Field 05 expansion — Curriculum and privacy

Education content uses public-safe curriculum descriptions. A class can teach vector prevention, medication labels, or how to request isolation without naming a patient. DiseaseSystem supplies any actual clinical guidance or diagnostic facts. A teacher cannot browse the sick list merely because they lead a class.

Private questions route to the medical/consent owner. The outreach panel shows “education available” or “private clinical answer required,” not a guessed diagnosis. Archive entries from the class contain public milestones only unless an authorized owner permits more detail.

### Field 06 expansion — Supply literacy and medication handling

The class can teach how to read a canonical item label, request a resupply, or report a missing kit. Inventory, PharmaLab, LyophilizationSystem, CryoVaultSystem, and clinical owners remain authoritative for item creation, batch viability, storage, and use. Outreach does not create an expiry clock or claim a vehicle preserved a batch.

A patient can learn that a medicine is unavailable, pending, or requires a clinical prescription. A delivered kit still needs a medical action receipt. If a batch owner returns expiry or viability, the panel displays it; otherwise it says storage or validity is unverified.

### Field 07 expansion — Audio and calm-care presentation

Medical, radio, expedition, and low-power notifications use AudioAccessibilityCoordinator’s existing cue catalog, visual labels, coalescing, ducking, and reduced-stimulation presets. A care class does not add a therapeutic sound layer. Quiet-mode players still receive text and icon feedback for appointment delay, referral acknowledgment, and treatment receipt.

Focus order keeps patient consent, education choice, hobby invitation, and route action separate. Closing the panel removes listeners. A repeated visit does not replay every notification; it queries current owner state.

### Field 08 expansion — Archive and survivor continuity

An accepted class, referral, or public celebration milestone can enter ShelterArchiveSystem through its owner. The archive does not become a clinical chart. A future outreach episode can search a public education milestone and ask whether current medical status has changed, but it cannot copy old treatment text into current state.

If the patient dies or retires, Memorial and campaign owners decide what remains public. Bereavement content can offer a memorial or letter without implying that a hobby or lesson caused a clinical outcome. The archive record distinguishes patient choice, caregiver participation, and actual clinical result.

### Field 09 expansion — Persistence and deterministic scheduling

Education, hobby, season, weather, communication, medical, archive, and expedition owners persist independently. Outreach stores only a visit or lesson reference. Save/reload cannot repeat a class, celebration cost, hobby session, message, or treatment. Time advances only through the current campaign/day owner.

The schedule view resolves one selected patient/stop at a time. Many classes and group sessions are summarized. Same-seed replay checks study outcome, hobby mastery, seasonal eligibility, message acknowledgment, and clinical receipt under equal state.

### Field 10 expansion — Care-continuity tranche

The tranche promotes after one public lesson, one patient-led refusal, one hobby invitation, one winter delay, one celebration context, one communications acknowledgment, one archive milestone, and one verified clinical action. The clinical action remains a separate owner receipt. Missing curriculum, facility, teacher, route, or patient consent must produce a coherent fallback.

This creates a rich outreach loop that gives patients information, community, and time while keeping medicine honest. It is especially useful in the long campaign because not every visit must end in a procedure.

## Pass 41 — Mobile triage network, patient journeys, and high-volume referral records

This pass specifies the outreach command surface for many simultaneous requests. It composes current disease, clinical, colony, communications, inventory, expedition, vehicle, consent, archive, and audio owners. It does not create a master patient queue that overrides triage or a new appointment scheduler. It makes referrals legible, private, and performant.

### Field 01 expansion — Request identity and privacy class

Each request row has a stable case reference from the current medical/quest owner, a public/private classification, source settlement, request age, owner status, and allowed actions. Outreach cannot create a patient ID when the medical owner has not supplied one. A public information request and a private diagnosis request use different row treatments.

The list displays minimum necessary data. Private details load after authorization and are never copied into a public colony notice, communications history, archive search, or scenario manifest. An unidentified request can remain a general referral without inventing a person.

### Field 02 expansion — Triage projection without triage authority

DiseaseSystem and clinical owners supply stage, severity source, vector, protocol, urgency, and action eligibility where exposed. The outreach board uses those facts as labels. It does not rank patients by a local score, alter dose, or change a treatment deadline. If no triage result exists, the row says clinical priority unavailable.

Urgent visual notification uses the existing medical cue. The panel does not turn urgency text into a forced dispatch. A player can choose a communication/referral action if the owner permits it, while the medical owner remains responsible for treatment order.

### Field 03 expansion — Patient journey states

The journey is represented as owner receipts: REQUESTED, CONTACTED, CONSENT_PENDING, ROUTE_ACCEPTED, REFERRAL_ACCEPTED, CLINICAL_ACTION_ACCEPTED, RESULT_RETURNED, DECLINED, UNAVAILABLE, and ARCHIVED. These are projections of existing owners, not a new care state machine.

A patient can move from contacted to declined without penalty, or from referral accepted to result pending. Reopening the panel never advances a state. If two owners disagree, the UI names the unresolved seam rather than choosing one.

### Field 04 expansion — Outpost and colony volume

A route may include many canonical colonies and outposts. ColonySystem supplies building/supply/capacity facts; CommunicationsSystem supplies message reach; ExpeditionSystem supplies travel. The outreach list loads destination metadata first and patient requests on selection. A field clinic is not a clinical route until the medical owner confirms it.

The player can filter by current route, communication-only, verified clinical destination, supply pending, or consent pending. Filtering does not mutate colony supply or patient state. Outpost starvation/overrun remains a colony/outpost result.

### Field 05 expansion — Inventory and batch evidence

Inventory, PharmaLab, LyophilizationSystem, CryoVaultSystem, food preservation, and clinical owners provide item/batch facts within their scopes. Outreach displays an item present, batch expired, batch viable, or storage unverified only when that owner returns the result. It never adds a mobile expiry clock.

A requested item can be removed from a dispatch preview without changing stock. Actual consumption or transfer requires the canonical transaction. A batch’s viability cannot be inferred from a vehicle module or a narrative cool box.

### Field 06 expansion — Communication volume and acknowledgement

CommunicationsSystem supplies sent, received, decoded, acknowledged, intercepted, jammed, and range results. A referral row links to a message receipt when the owner exposes a stable reference. It never turns a sent message into an appointment or a received message into treatment.

High-volume message histories are paged and privacy-filtered. An intercepted message can generate a separate privacy quest but cannot reveal a diagnosis in the patient board. Duplicate sends use owner response or remain visibly pending.

### Field 07 expansion — Audio/accessibility for urgent care

The existing medical, radio, and expedition cues provide visual labels and reduced-stimulation behavior. A high-volume board coalesces repeated noncritical notices while preserving distinct critical patient events. Quiet mode retains text, focus, and icon state.

Focus order is patient-safe: public summary, private authorization, owner status, supported action, consequence, and back. No irreversible clinical command is adjacent to a generic dismiss control without an explicit label. Closing the board disposes listeners.

### Field 08 expansion — Archive and continuity limits

ShelterArchiveSystem can record a public referral milestone, a clinical milestone allowed by its source, or a memorial. Outreach never archives a full diagnosis by default. A future visit queries current status rather than treating an old archive entry as current care.

When a patient dies, retires, or leaves the roster, medical/memorial/campaign owners decide continuity. A letter or remembrance scene can be offered without changing a clinical outcome. Historical text is labeled and access-controlled.

### Field 09 expansion — Save/reload and failure paths

All owner systems retain their own state. Outreach stores stable references and view preferences only where authorized. Reload cannot resend a message, duplicate a referral, consume a kit twice, repeat a treatment, or archive a duplicate milestone.

Failure paths remain actionable: no route, no clinic, patient declined, message jammed, supply delayed, batch validity unknown, owner result pending, privacy denied, or destination missing. Each state has a fallback or an explicit foreman gap.

### Field 10 expansion — Load and acceptance gate

The performance slice includes 200 request summaries, 24 destinations, 60 message receipts, 30 item/batch rows, 12 active patients, 8 clinical actions, and 10 audio notifications. It measures open, filter, detail authorization, message send, route submit, save/reload, and close.

Promotion requires no diagnosis leak, no local triage, no duplicate treatment, exact-once transfer, deterministic owner state, and legible fallback. A full list is useful only if a patient can understand what is known, what is private, and what action is actually available.

### Pass 41 supplemental worked journey

The board opens with 200 requests and filters to route-accepted cases. One patient is private, one public, one unidentified. The private row requires authorization; the public row opens an education referral; the unidentified row remains a general request. ## Pass 42 — Outreach performance, privacy lifecycle, and regression scaffolding

This pass defines the operational quality bar for large referral volumes. It covers patient-detail authorization, route-panel disposal, message coalescing, batch projections, save migration, deterministic replay, and accessible urgent-care feedback. No medical authority is changed.

### Field 01 expansion — Patient-detail lazy loading

The outreach list renders public metadata first. Private patient detail is fetched only after the current authorization route succeeds. Closing or changing the row clears private detail from the view model. The list never preloads every diagnosis or message body.

### Field 02 expansion — Consent lifecycle

Consent prompts are bound to the selected medical owner and carry an action ID. Cancel, decline, timeout, and accepted states remain distinct. Reopen does not repeat a prompt or convert an earlier decline into consent. A stale prompt fails safely if the patient/owner state changes.

### Field 03 expansion — Message subscription lifecycle

Communication and medical notification listeners attach once on panel open and detach on close. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator owns coalescing and visual fallback. An acknowledged message is not replayed as a new alert on reopen.

### Field 04 expansion — Batch/item projection

Inventory, LyophilizationSystem, CryoVaultSystem, PharmaLab, and clinical projections are queried only for selected actions. The outreach panel does not calculate viability, spoilage, or dosage. It displays source owner and timestamp when available.

### Field 05 expansion — Route and colony pagination

Colony/outpost metadata is paged. Patient requests, supply receipts, and message bodies are resolved on selection. A route refresh invalidates only affected stops. A large world cannot make the patient board scan every colony every frame.

### Field 06 expansion — Determinism and privacy replay

Paired runs compare referral order, message results, disease projection, consent outcome, archive IDs, and visual notification count. Private fields are compared through hashes or redacted labels in diagnostics, never printed into logs. UI opens remain side-effect-free.

### Field 07 expansion — Save/migration behavior

Old saves with missing case IDs render historical unavailable. New optional privacy labels default to most restrictive display. A saved accepted treatment is not resent. A saved pending referral remains pending until the medical/communications owner reports a result.

### Field 08 expansion — Accessibility cases

Cases cover a medical emergency with muted audio, reduced stimulation, screen-reader focus, high contrast, private detail authorization, long messages, and a declined action. A critical consequence is visible before submit.

### Field 09 expansion — Error and audit output

Errors include owner, case reference, action, reason, and privacy-safe context. The panel never logs a full patient note or diagnosis to debug a route. Missing clinical consumers remain explicit design gaps.

### Field 10 expansion — Focused gate

The gate package includes one accepted referral, one refusal, one pending message, one expired/unknown batch, one unreachable colony, one save/reload, one duplicate-submit, and one accessibility snapshot. Promotion requires exact owner effects and no shadow patient state.

The high-volume board is successful when it helps the player make fewer false assumptions. It should be faster to understand what is pending, private, declined, or treated, while remaining impossible for a panel refresh to change the patient’s medical state.
## Pass 43 — High-volume patient journeys and referral prose deck

This pass supplies a large authoring deck for repeated outreach stops. It covers education, referral, supply, privacy, consent, route, colony, communications, archive, and grief without making any one visit a compulsory treatment scene.

### Field 01 expansion — Journey cards

Each card includes request source, public/private classification, patient choice, owner action, medical boundary, logistics dependency, accessible copy, follow-up, and closure. A card never invents a diagnosis or treatment result.

### Field 02 expansion — Multiple valid endings

A journey may end in education delivered, referral sent, referral accepted, patient declined, route delayed, supply pending, clinical action accepted, result pending, result returned, or memorial follow-up. These outcomes are not ranked on a hidden care score.

### Field 03 expansion — Consent-first writing

Prose asks before it acts. A patient can accept information and decline examination, accept a message and decline transfer, or ask for privacy while a caregiver attends a public lesson. Each difference is visible.

### Field 04 expansion — Logistics detail

Cards refer to canonical item IDs, colony supply receipts, vehicle cargo, batch/expiry results, and route status only when owners provide them. “The kit is in the truck” is not a mechanical fact until inventory/expedition accepts the load.

### Field 05 expansion — Clinical wording

Use “symptom,” “request,” “referral,” “protocol,” and “treatment result” with care. “Recovered” is reserved for an owner outcome. A character’s hope is not an outcome.

### Field 06 expansion — Privacy writing

Public notices avoid names and diagnoses. Private scenes require authorization. Intercepted messages produce a communications/privacy event, not a freely visible medical record.

### Field 07 expansion — Community and family voices

Family, caregivers, teachers, nurses, and patients receive distinct roles when current survivor/relationship owners support them. No relationship automatically grants medical access or consent.

### Field 08 expansion — High-volume data

The 48 records below are authored candidates. Twelve can enter the first playable slice; the remainder stay validated preview content until their owner routes are verified.

### Field 09 expansion — Accessibility and localization

Every card has a concise public line, a private detail line, a refusal line, a pending line, and a screen-reader action description. The exact clinical terms remain consistent across translations.

### Field 10 expansion — Acceptance

Promotion requires one journey for each major ending, one privacy case, one route delay, one supply failure, one save/reload, one duplicate guard, and one memorial boundary.

## Pass 44 — Cross-plan patient handoff and implementation order

This pass makes the outreach plan’s dependencies reviewable before content volume grows.

### Field 01 expansion — Patient identity

Medical/quest owners supply stable case references. Outreach never invents them.

### Field 02 expansion — Route identity

Expedition and colony owners supply destination/route facts. Outreach never creates clinics.

### Field 03 expansion — Message identity

Communications owns send/receive/decode/acknowledgment. Outreach only links receipts.

### Field 04 expansion — Item identity

Inventory and medical batch owners supply item/viability facts. Outreach never tracks stock.

### Field 05 expansion — Consent identity

Clinical/consent owners decide patient permission. Autonomy is not medical consent.

### Field 06 expansion — Care identity

Medical owners return eligibility, action, and outcome. Education/hobby remain supportive.

### Field 07 expansion — Memory identity

Archive and memorial owners decide public history. Outreach stores references.

### Field 08 expansion — Alert identity

AudioAccessibilityCoordinator owns critical cues and quiet modes.

### Field 09 expansion — Save identity

Each clinical/logistics owner restores its own state. The outreach journal does not replay actions.

### Field 10 expansion — Handoff order

Verify destination, message, consent, supply, care, archive, accessibility, and reload in that order.

## Pass 45 — Remote triage, consent, and continuity without a second clinic

This pass extends outreach into low-connectivity care while preserving the existing clinical, disease, inventory, vehicle, expedition, communications, and consent authorities. Outreach can request a triage exchange and present its consequences; it cannot diagnose, own a medicine counter, or create a remote clinic ledger.

### Field 01 expansion — Triage question sets

Each referral begins with a small question set: immediate danger, ability to travel, available caregiver, known condition, and preferred communication. The clinical owner decides which questions are valid for the case. Outreach presents the answers with timestamps and confidence labels. Missing answers create a safe follow-up rather than an invented severity score.

### Field 02 expansion — Urgency bands

The care owner returns an urgency band such as routine, soon, urgent, or emergency. Outreach maps the band to a communication and routing action: queue a visit, request a relay, hold a vehicle slot, or escalate to an existing emergency path. The panel explains that the band is an owner result. It never derives urgency from dramatic prose or player intuition.

### Field 03 expansion — Consent at a distance

A patient can accept, limit, defer, or refuse a remote exchange. A caregiver can relay only the permissions granted by the consent owner. Private details are hidden from public notices and archive projections. If the patient cannot answer, the existing clinical rule supplies the allowed surrogate path; outreach records that a surrogate rule was used without creating a new legal model.

### Field 04 expansion — Message compression

Poor signal can reduce a referral to a compact packet containing stable case ID, urgency, destination, requested question, and callback window. Communications owns encoding, range, jamming, acknowledgment, and retry. Outreach shows packet state and stale time. It does not assume that a sent packet was read or that a reply contains the requested care.

### Field 05 expansion — Caregiver support

Some cases need a prepared caregiver rather than a vehicle. SurvivorEducation, autonomy, relationship, and hobby owners can provide teaching, refusal, or comfort facts. Outreach creates a caregiver task request and waits for an owner response. A successful lesson yields a knowledge receipt; it does not grant an unbounded medical skill.

### Field 06 expansion — Symptom journal projection

A patient journal can display reported changes, treatment receipts, questions, and next review. The disease and clinical owners decide the actual condition. Outreach stores references and source timestamps. Contradictory reports stay visible as a comparison rather than being silently merged.

### Field 07 expansion — Medication and supply handoff

When a care owner requests an item, outreach asks inventory for identity, quantity, condition, and route. A batch owner may reject an expired or damaged item. The patient card displays the rejection and a safe substitute request. There is no outreach-local expiry clock; all viability remains with the item or batch owner.

### Field 08 expansion — Waiting-room dignity

A waiting state contains a plain explanation, estimated next owner event, a quiet option, and an alternative activity. It does not spin forever or imply that a delay is player failure. The AudioAccessibilityCoordinator provides critical medical cues and visual equivalents. A player can leave the panel and return without losing the referral.

### Field 09 expansion — Family and community boundaries

A family member can ask for an update, but the consent owner determines what can be shared. Community notices use aggregate language such as “care team requested supplies” rather than naming a condition. Archive and memorial owners receive only public facts. The story can explore worry and trust without making privacy a hidden punishment.

### Field 10 expansion — Triage closure

A triage thread closes when an owner returns a care decision, the patient or surrogate acknowledges it, and the next action is scheduled, completed, or declined. A stale thread can reopen when the patient reports a change, a route opens, or a clinician requests new evidence. Reopening links to the original case and does not duplicate its supplies or reward.

## Pass 46 — Outreach seasons, rehabilitation, and patient-led recovery

This pass gives long-running cases an arc of agency. It joins seasonal weather, education, hobbies, shelter, colony, and relationship facts to patient-led goals while leaving clinical outcomes with the medical owner.

### Field 01 expansion — Recovery goals

A patient may choose a goal such as walking to the noticeboard, teaching a child, returning to a workshop, tending a planter, or recording a testimony. The goal is a narrative request whose feasibility is checked by needs, health, route, and activity owners. It can be postponed, adapted, or declined without treating the patient as a failed quest.

### Field 02 expansion — Seasonal care plans

The outreach panel can suggest different follow-up timing in deep winter, pale spring, ash summer, and black autumn. NuclearWinterProgression and weather provide the context. Clinical owners decide whether timing is safe. A seasonal suggestion is never a hidden modifier to health; it is a transparent scheduling option with a reason.

### Field 03 expansion — Rehabilitation spaces

A shelter may have a bench, quiet room, garden, or workshop supplied by existing building definitions. Outreach can request a session there and show its accessibility or safety facts. Colony and construction owners decide whether the space exists and whether it is available. A story beat can celebrate a repaired room without declaring that rehabilitation succeeded automatically.

### Field 04 expansion — Pain and fatigue language

Patient-facing prose distinguishes pain, tiredness, fear, frustration, and relief. The clinical and needs owners provide actual state where available. Writers avoid turning every symptom into a numerical meter. The UI offers “ask for help,” “rest,” “continue with support,” and “stop” as explicit actions routed through the relevant owner.

### Field 05 expansion — Peer support

A survivor with a compatible hobby, education subject, or relationship may offer companionship. Autonomy can accept, refuse, or defer. The relationship owner handles affinity. Outreach records that the support was offered and whether the patient chose it. Peer support cannot replace a clinical action or be used to unlock a medical recipe.

### Field 06 expansion — Progress evidence

Progress uses concrete receipts: attended review, completed exercise request, returned item, answered question, or chosen rest. The plan displays a sequence of evidence instead of a single “recovered” bar. Clinical owners can state that symptoms remain even when agency improves. This keeps the story honest and protects players from confusing narrative optimism with medical certainty.

### Field 07 expansion — Setbacks

A weather closure, pain flare, supply delay, refusal, or failed message can interrupt a goal. The player receives a recovery option: reschedule, change location, ask a different caregiver, or archive the attempt. Setbacks do not erase prior receipts. A later scene can refer to the earlier attempt, making patience part of the playable arc.

### Field 08 expansion — Care team handover

When a clinician, caregiver, or shelter changes, the case has a handover checklist: stable case ID, current consent, recent owner receipts, open questions, and next review. Each item is acknowledged by the receiving owner. Outreach can show missing acknowledgments and prevent a false “complete” label.

### Field 09 expansion — Memory and memorial boundaries

A completed case may become an archive entry, a private family note, a memorial, or no public record. Archive and memorial owners make the decision. Outreach can propose the record with patient wording and source links. It cannot use recovery success as automatic evidence for a community legend.

### Field 10 expansion — Patient-led closure

A patient-led thread closes when the patient or permitted surrogate chooses a next chapter: continue care, maintain routine, teach someone, document experience, or rest from outreach. The clinical owner may still keep a follow-up open. The player sees the difference between narrative closure and clinical closure, preserving continuity without forcing one dramatic ending.

## Pass 47 — Outreach release gates, safety review, and repeatable content production

This pass defines how high-volume patient stories can be authored without turning outreach into a hidden medical simulator.

### Field 01 expansion — Minimal clinical slice

The first slice contains one patient case, one consent decision, one relay message, one inventory request, one route query, one review, and one reload. It proves that a player can receive a case, protect privacy, request care, and understand the next step.

### Field 02 expansion — Clinical truth gate

Every medical statement in content is tagged reported, owner-confirmed, or unresolved. Writers cannot use an unresolved statement to promise treatment. The content checker requires a source owner and an outcome path for every care verb.

### Field 03 expansion — Deterministic referral gate

A same-seed replay yields the same case order, message packet, and owner acknowledgments. Variation may change which peer offers support or which descriptive line appears, but not whether a medicine exists or a route is open. Randomness stays behind the existing seeded contract.

### Field 04 expansion — Privacy gate

A fixture tests patient consent, caregiver request, public notice, archive proposal, and reload. Private details remain private after save/load. A rejected disclosure produces a clear explanation and does not penalize the patient’s care priority.

### Field 05 expansion — Supply truth gate

The referral asks inventory for an actual item or batch. The test covers absent, damaged, expired, reserved, and delivered states. Outreach shows the returned state and offers a safe next action. No local stock count is permitted.

### Field 06 expansion — Lifecycle gate

Hidden, closed, and disposed panels release subscriptions and focus state. A delayed message arriving after the panel closes updates the owner journal and produces one reopen notification. Reopening the panel does not replay the same alert.

### Field 07 expansion — Accessibility gate

Critical medical alerts use the audio accessibility seam with visual and text fallback. Every care action has a focus label, disabled reason, and controller route. Quiet mode suppresses duplicates while preserving emergency visibility.

### Field 08 expansion — Performance gate

The case list uses indexed metadata and selected-case detail. A fixture with 200 referrals does not request full clinical records for every row. Message history is paged, and inactive cases are not polled every frame.

### Field 09 expansion — Content rollback gate

If a story package is disabled, open referrals show a migration note and retain their clinical state. The player can continue through the existing owner path or archive the narrative thread. No patient data is deleted to hide a content dependency.

### Field 10 expansion — Definition of done

An outreach slice is complete when a case can be received, consented, routed, supplied, reviewed, interrupted, reloaded, and closed with an auditable owner chain. A large patient prose bank is additive only after that chain is proven.

## Pass 48 — Outreach operations runbook, patient safety, and post-release care

This pass makes the outreach expansion supportable after launch. It describes daily referral review, privacy correction, old-save behavior, and care continuity while keeping clinical, consent, inventory, route, communications, and accessibility authority in their existing owners.

### Field 01 expansion — Referral change sweep

A scheduled sweep checks only open referrals for owner changes: urgency, route, message acknowledgment, batch viability, consent, clinician assignment, and patient request. It emits a bounded change list. It does not poll every survivor or derive a new disease state. The patient panel explains which owner changed and what action is now available.

### Field 02 expansion — Safety-first operator triage

Diagnostics group issues by stale clinical result, consent mismatch, duplicate delivery, missing acknowledgment, inaccessible alert, save mismatch, or unsupported treatment wording. Each issue contains case ID, owner, package version, and a remediation link. Sensitive symptoms and private notes are redacted from aggregate diagnostics.

### Field 03 expansion — Correction and apology path

If a referral displayed the wrong destination, stale supply, or incorrect privacy label, the patient journal receives a correction entry. The entry says what changed, whether the patient’s prior choice remains valid, and which owner now controls the next step. Outreach never silently rewrites the patient’s account or manufactures compensation.

### Field 04 expansion — Old-save care continuity

A pre-expansion save may contain a case reference, item reference, route request, or archive proposal unknown to the new package. Migration preserves the stable case ID, maps recognized owner references, and marks the rest as legacy. The player receives a plain explanation and can continue through the base care path while the optional story package is unavailable.

### Field 05 expansion — Privacy review cadence

Open referrals periodically recheck consent only when the consent owner reports a change or the player opens a disclosure decision. Routine refresh does not expose details to a wider audience. Public notices and archive proposals carry the latest permitted scope and a source timestamp.

### Field 06 expansion — Remote care staffing

When a clinician or caregiver is unavailable, outreach queries the current roster, colony, communications, and route owners. Responses are available, delayed, unreachable, or refused. A remote helper is not displayed as active until the owner returns an acceptance and the communication route is acknowledged.

### Field 07 expansion — Quiet medical presentation

Routine appointment, supply, and education updates can be coalesced. Emergency medical alerts remain in the critical cue set and appear visually and in text. The patient panel remembers the last acknowledged alert without replaying it after every reopen. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator owns ducking, presets, and visual notification seams.

### Field 08 expansion — Record retention and deletion requests

A patient can request a private record, a public record, or no record. Archive and consent owners decide retention. Closing the outreach thread does not delete clinical state. A temporary message can leave the active queue while remaining in the owner journal when policy requires it.

### Field 09 expansion — Content batch cadence

New patient journeys arrive in batches by care seam: relay, supply, caregiver, rehabilitation, archive, or seasonal follow-up. Each batch includes privacy fixtures, owner response fixtures, accessibility strings, and rollback notes. Draft prose can remain staged until the clinical and consent contracts are proven.

### Field 10 expansion — Patient-centered review

Reviewers ask whether the patient understands the next step, can decline safely, can recover after interruption, sees the difference between reported and confirmed facts, and retains dignity during delay. A journey that has beautiful prose but no safe refusal, reload, or owner receipt remains incomplete.

### Pass 48 operational acceptance sequence

1. Open one referral and record case ID, consent scope, owner list, current urgency, and next action.
2. Change one premise through an owner fixture, such as a route closure or narrower consent, and confirm one understandable update.
3. Interrupt before the patient chooses, reload, and verify that privacy, case ID, and pending action are unchanged.
4. Request a real inventory item, exercise, or message acknowledgment and verify that the owner receipt appears exactly once.
5. Test refused care, delayed care, and missing information; each must offer a safe next step without shaming language.
6. Toggle quiet mode and controller navigation, then confirm that emergency cues remain visible and focus returns correctly.
7. Disable the story package in a fixture save and confirm that clinical and consent state remain intact behind a migration note.
8. Re-enable the same package and confirm stable reconnection without duplicate treatment or disclosure.
9. Replay the same seed twice and compare case order, owner results, and closure records.
10. Sign the batch only when clinical truth, privacy, save behavior, accessibility, rollback, and patient-centered wording are evidenced.

## Pass 49 — Regional care relay, interpretation, and humane outage handling

This pass expands outreach for patients whose care crosses shelter, region, language, or signal boundaries. Existing clinical, consent, communications, education, route, inventory, archive, and accessibility owners remain the only authorities.

### Field 01 expansion — Regional referral

A case can request a neighboring clinician, caregiver, or shelter when the local route returns unavailable. Medical and expedition owners provide destination and travel facts. Outreach shows the relay status and does not invent a second patient queue.

### Field 02 expansion — Interpretation request

A patient can request an interpreter, teacher, visual explanation, or written exchange. Education and communications owners return availability. The consent owner decides which information can be translated or shared. The case remains open while interpretation is pending.

### Field 03 expansion — Compact medical packet

Poor signal reduces a referral to stable case ID, urgency, question, destination, consent scope, and callback window. Communications owns encoding and acknowledgment. Outreach marks missing fields rather than filling them with assumptions.

### Field 04 expansion — Mobility accommodation

A patient may choose a home visit, assisted route, caregiver relay, or delayed appointment. Needs, vehicle, expedition, and clinical owners decide feasibility. The UI presents the choices as respectful alternatives and records the selected path.

### Field 05 expansion — Equity review

Care review checks whether delay, distance, signal, literacy, disability, or caregiver availability changed access to the same owner path. The plan does not create an equity score; it surfaces the owner facts and opens a correction request when access was blocked.

### Field 06 expansion — Outage queue

A medical outage card shows last acknowledgment, safe interim instruction from the clinical owner, retry window, and emergency route. It does not poll continuously or provide treatment advice from prose. A player can leave the panel without losing the case.

### Field 07 expansion — Handoff acknowledgement

A receiving care team acknowledges case identity, current consent, latest evidence, and next review. Missing acknowledgments stay visible. Outreach closes the local referral only after owner receipt or patient withdrawal.

### Field 08 expansion — Family communication boundary

A family member can receive the scope allowed by consent and no more. The panel distinguishes “not yet received,” “not permitted,” and “not known.” That distinction remains after reload and in public notice previews.

### Field 09 expansion — Conflicting care reports

Reports from two relays remain separate with source and time. Clinical owners can request clarification or select a current result. Outreach never merges a contradiction merely to make the story advance.

### Field 10 expansion — Relay closure

A regional care relay closes on acknowledgment, completed handoff, respectful refusal, or explicit withdrawal. The closure links both case records and can reopen when the patient reports a change or a clinician requests evidence.

### Pass 49 relay acceptance sequence

1. Open a case and request a regional relay with the current consent scope.
2. Run available, delayed, unreachable, and refused fixtures.
3. Confirm compact packet, interpretation option, mobility option, and safe waiting copy.
4. Interrupt during outage and reload without duplicating a message, supply, or disclosure.
5. Complete the receiving acknowledgment and verify linked case records.
6. Test a family request, conflicting report, and patient withdrawal.
7. Repeat with quiet mode, controller focus, and the same deterministic seed.
8. Sign only when privacy, access, clinical truth, and archive boundaries remain intact.

## Pass 50 — Patient follow-up checklist and care handoff cards

This closeout packet turns the outreach expansion into small reviewable patient journeys.

### Field 01 — Case identity
Each journey begins with a stable case ID and current owner source. Outreach never creates a duplicate patient record.

### Field 02 — Consent scope
The case displays what can be shared, with whom, and until when. A narrowed scope takes effect on the next disclosure without deleting clinical history.

### Field 03 — Clinical truth
Urgency, condition, and treatment statements come from clinical or disease owners. Unresolved reports remain labeled as reports.

### Field 04 — Supply truth
Items and batches come from inventory and medical owners with quantity, viability, and route. Outreach does not track stock locally.

### Field 05 — Route truth
Visits, relays, and home care use expedition, vehicle, weather, and colony facts. Delays explain themselves and remain safe.

### Field 06 — Human choice
Accept, refuse, defer, privacy, and caregiver choices are explicit and routed through consent/autonomy owners.

### Field 07 — Accessible care
Critical alerts have visual and text equivalents, clear focus, quiet-mode behavior, and an understandable disabled reason.

### Field 08 — Save continuity
Case, consent, pending message, owner receipt, and next review survive interruption without duplicate treatment or disclosure.

### Field 09 — Replay key
Same seed and fixture responses reproduce case order and closures. Seed variation cannot change clinical authority.

### Field 10 — Handoff note
The final card lists clinical, privacy, supply, route, accessibility, migration, and rollback evidence.

## Pass 57 — Care pathway states and referral continuity

This pass defines a bounded pathway for outreach cases. It composes existing clinical, disease, consent, communications, inventory, vehicle, expedition, colony, education, archive, and autonomy owners. The pathway is not a new diagnosis engine or local clinic ledger.

### Field 01 expansion — Reported case

A case enters through a patient, caregiver, clinician, archive, or communications owner. It carries stable case ID, source, timestamp, consent scope, and preferred response channel. Reported symptoms remain reports until clinical or disease owners return a result.

### Field 02 expansion — Clarification state

The outreach panel asks only questions authorized by the clinical owner: immediate danger, ability to travel, caregiver availability, known treatment, and requested support. Missing answers remain missing. A clarification request has a timeout, privacy scope, and safe waiting message.

### Field 03 expansion — Routed state

The owner returns a destination, urgency band, message route, or home-care option. Outreach shows the result and requests acknowledgment. It does not create a destination or infer a clinic from a building definition.

### Field 04 expansion — Prepared state

A prepared case lists consent, route, clinician/caregiver, requested item, and return or check-in condition. Inventory, vehicle, expedition, and roster owners decide readiness. A player can change a reversible choice before the owner action.

### Field 05 expansion — Active care state

An active care state exists only after the care owner accepts the action. Outreach displays progress receipts and open questions. If a route closes or the patient withdraws, the care owner returns the interruption and outreach offers reschedule, stop, or safe follow-up.

### Field 06 expansion — Review state

After a visit, message, lesson, or supply delivery, the player sees what happened, what was not answered, and what the next review is. Clinical outcomes come from clinical owners; narrative satisfaction cannot substitute for them.

### Field 07 expansion — Supported recovery state

A patient-led goal can create a support request for education, hobby, shelter, relationship, or caregiver help. Supporting systems return acceptance, refusal, and capacity. Outreach records the receipt without turning support into a medical modifier.

### Field 08 expansion — Waiting state

Waiting includes last acknowledgment, retry window, emergency route, and a quiet option. A case can remain open while the player works elsewhere. Reopening the panel does not replay the same alert.

### Field 09 expansion — Reopened state

A case reopens on new symptom report, changed consent, changed route, new clinician request, or player follow-up. The delta links to the previous closure and never duplicates a medicine, visit, or reward.

### Field 10 expansion — Patient-led closure

A patient or permitted surrogate can close the outreach story as continue care, maintain routine, teach, document, rest, or withdraw. Clinical follow-up can remain open. The journal distinguishes narrative closure from clinical closure.

## Pass 58 — Outreach data contract, privacy schema, and migration policy

This pass defines the proposed content fields for high-volume patient journeys. It does not grant outreach permission to own clinical or consent state.

### Field 01 expansion — Case key

The case key is stable, snake_case, package-scoped, and independent of a patient’s display name. Aliases support migration and never recycle an old key.

### Field 02 expansion — Clinical references

A case names clinical query kind, disease reference when permitted, urgency source, review owner, and unresolved questions. It cannot encode a diagnosis in prose as a replacement for a clinical result.

### Field 03 expansion — Consent references

The row declares who can view, relay, archive, or publish each field. Consent narrowing is a runtime owner event. Content cannot widen visibility because a branch was selected.

### Field 04 expansion — Communication references

A message block names packet type, destination, acknowledgment, retry, expiration, and fallback. It distinguishes sent, received, decoded, read, and acted upon.

### Field 05 expansion — Supply references

The supply block names item or batch ID, quantity request, validity owner, reservation, delivery route, and rejection copy. Outreach never stores a local expiry clock.

### Field 06 expansion — Route references

A route block names canonical location, expedition query, vehicle need, weather window, and patient mobility accommodation. It contains no invented clinic capacity.

### Field 07 expansion — Support references

Education, hobby, relationship, shelter, and colony support are optional owner references. Their result becomes a support receipt and cannot be interpreted as a treatment result.

### Field 08 expansion — Narrative envelope

Copy is split into patient voice, caregiver voice, clinical explanation, uncertainty, refusal, delay, closure, and accessibility labels. Translation context and maximum length are mandatory.

### Field 09 expansion — Save envelope

The row lists open case references, owner receipts, consent scope, pending packet, and next review to restore. It points to current save owners and cannot add an outreach-local save section.

### Field 10 expansion — Determinism and migration

Seeded variation lists stream purpose and allowed choices. Migration lists old/new keys, preserved receipts, privacy behavior, package version, and rollback note.

## Pass 59 — Outreach desk UI, privacy presentation, and patient comprehension

This pass specifies a calm patient-facing desk over the existing owner routes.

### Field 01 expansion — Case queue

Rows show case ID, urgency source, consent state, route status, last acknowledgment, and next review. The queue does not expose private detail in summary view.

### Field 02 expansion — Consent panel

Consent scope is displayed before any share or archive command. Each field has a private, permitted, and unknown label. A narrowed scope immediately changes the preview.

### Field 03 expansion — Clinical explanation

The clinical result is separated from reported symptoms and player-authored notes. The panel states which owner returned the result and when it can be reviewed again.

### Field 04 expansion — Supply panel

Supply rows show item, batch, quantity, reservation, delivery, and rejection reason. The action opens inventory or expedition context rather than duplicating a transaction button.

### Field 05 expansion — Route panel

The route panel shows destination, mobility option, weather window, vehicle need, and safe return. It does not infer capacity from a building icon.

### Field 06 expansion — Waiting panel

Waiting shows last acknowledgment, retry, emergency path, quiet option, and alternative activity. Leaving the panel preserves state.

### Field 07 expansion — Support panel

Education, hobby, peer, and shelter support display as optional requests with owner response and boundary. No support card claims clinical improvement without evidence.

### Field 08 expansion — Alert presentation

Medical emergencies use critical cues and visual text fallback. Routine updates coalesce. Acknowledged alerts are not replayed on reopen.

### Field 09 expansion — Archive view

The archive view shows private/public choice, source, correction, retention, and patient wording. It is lazy-loaded and closed independently.

### Field 10 expansion — Error recovery

Errors state whether the owner is unavailable, consent blocks sharing, the route is closed, the package is disabled, or the case is unknown. Focus returns to the failed action.

## Pass 60 — Outreach performance envelope, privacy lifecycle, and stress fixtures

This pass makes high-volume referral content supportable.

### Field 01 expansion — Indexed queue

The queue indexes status, urgency, destination, consent, age, and owner. Full clinical detail loads only for the selected case.

### Field 02 expansion — Privacy-safe caching

Caches hold stable IDs and permitted summaries. Restricted notes are fetched only when the consent owner allows them and are released when the panel closes.

### Field 03 expansion — Message paging

Message histories use stable cursors and summary-first loading. A 200-case queue does not decode every packet at startup.

### Field 04 expansion — Owner subscriptions

Visible case detail subscribes to relevant owner events. Hidden cases are updated through bounded adapters rather than one subscription per case.

### Field 05 expansion — Alert coalescing

Routine appointment and supply updates coalesce by case and event type. Emergency alerts bypass routine grouping and retain visual fallback.

### Field 06 expansion — Save workload

Save captures case references, owner receipts, consent scope, and pending packet keys. It does not serialize clinical catalogs or duplicate inventory.

### Field 07 expansion — Focus lifecycle

Closing a panel releases message and note objects while retaining the selected key and focus target.

### Field 08 expansion — Failure isolation

A malformed optional journey fails that journey or package and leaves base care routes available. The patient journal keeps a migration note.

### Field 09 expansion — Deterministic order

Queue ordering, retry order, and seeded peer selection use stable IDs and explicit streams.

### Field 10 expansion — Stress evidence

Fixtures record case count, detail requests, subscriptions, message pages, save/restore duration, and alert count. A threshold breach creates one bounded repair task.

## Pass 61 — Outreach implementation milestones, safety gates, and package handoff

This pass orders implementation work without claiming that the entire medical system is unfinished or duplicated.

### Field 01 expansion — Premise audit

Reconfirm clinical, disease, consent, communications, inventory, route, save, and UI APIs against current source before touching the adapter.

### Field 02 expansion — Minimal case fixture

Add one case with report, consent, urgency, message, supply query, route result, refusal, and closure. Keep it isolated and focused.

### Field 03 expansion — Adapter slice

Translate panel commands to owner requests and display facts. Do not put triage or treatment decisions in callbacks.

### Field 04 expansion — Privacy save slice

Round-trip an open case with private scope, pending packet, and one receipt before adding public notices.

### Field 05 expansion — Accessible slice

Complete keyboard, controller, visual, text, and quiet behavior for one full care path.

### Field 06 expansion — Determinism slice

Replay case order, retry order, peer selection, and closure with paired seeds.

### Field 07 expansion — Content batch

Add 12–24 journeys across routine, soon, urgent, and emergency owner responses, including refusal and unknown paths.

### Field 08 expansion — Stress batch

Run 100- and 200-case fixtures and capture detail, message, subscription, and save evidence.

### Field 09 expansion — Rollback rehearsal

Disable the optional journey package in a save with open cases, verify base care route, then re-enable by stable key.

### Field 10 expansion — Safety handoff

Hand off owner map, privacy proof, focused results, limitations, and untouched shared seams. Do not claim clinical integration from content presence.

## Pass 62 — Outreach governance, patient trust, and long-horizon journey health

This pass defines post-release review for large patient-journey libraries.

### Field 01 expansion — Consent freshness

Open cases state when consent was last confirmed and which event can narrow it. A refresh does not widen scope.

### Field 02 expansion — Clinical uncertainty

Reported symptoms, owner-confirmed results, and unresolved questions remain separate in the journal and exportable review.

### Field 03 expansion — Respectful refusal

Decline, delay, and withdrawal have equal-quality copy and safe next steps. They are never used as automatic failure or moral scoring.

### Field 04 expansion — Access equity

Review samples check distance, signal, literacy, mobility, translation, and caregiver access through owner facts.

### Field 05 expansion — Privacy retention

Public, regional, household, and private records retain source and consent scope. Closing a story does not erase clinical state.

### Field 06 expansion — Seasonal care review

When winter phase or weather changes, only relevant appointments and routes are re-evaluated, with a visible reason.

### Field 07 expansion — Package retirement

Retired journey packages leave legacy notes and preserve owner receipts. Base care remains playable.

### Field 08 expansion — Writer diagnostics

Diagnostics identify repeated fallback, inaccessible wording, stale clinical copy, duplicate case IDs, and unacknowledged handoffs.

### Field 09 expansion — Release claims

Store and onboarding copy comes from verified manifest evidence, not from an authored promise of treatment or clinic capacity.

### Field 10 expansion — Sampling

A long-horizon review samples open, waiting, refused, transferred, completed, legacy, private, and reopened cases.

## Pass 63 — Triage network, urgency evidence, and safe referral branching

This pass gives high-volume outreach cases a clear triage network while leaving urgency and treatment decisions with clinical and disease owners.

### Field 01 — Intake source
A case identifies patient, caregiver, clinician, relay, or archive source with timestamp and consent scope.

### Field 02 — Question set
Clinical owners define immediate danger, mobility, caregiver, known treatment, and requested support questions.

### Field 03 — Urgency result
The owner returns routine, soon, urgent, or emergency. Outreach maps the result to communication and route options.

### Field 04 — Referral destination
Medical and expedition owners return destination and path. Outreach does not infer clinic capacity.

### Field 05 — Message branch
Communications returns send, receive, decode, read, act, retry, jam, or courier results.

### Field 06 — Supply branch
Inventory and batch owners return requested, reserved, rejected, delayed, delivered, or substituted results.

### Field 07 — Consent branch
Consent returns permitted, limited, deferred, refused, or withdrawn. Each branch has patient-safe language.

### Field 08 — Care branch
Clinical owners return accepted, delayed, completed, changed, or stopped care.

### Field 09 — Support branch
Education, hobby, relationship, shelter, and colony owners provide optional support receipts.

### Field 10 — Closure branch
The case closes with owner outcome, patient choice, next review, and record scope.

## Pass 64 — Patient logistics, supply custody, and home-care continuity

This pass expands the practical logistics of reaching a patient without creating a local medical inventory.

### Field 01 — Case packing
Inventory returns item, batch, quantity, reservation, and condition. Outreach displays missing and substituted items.

### Field 02 — Vehicle request
Vehicle and expedition return cargo, route, rest, and return facts. The panel cannot claim a delivery from a request alone.

### Field 03 — Custody handoff
A supply packet names sender, receiver, item, batch, time, and owner acknowledgment. Duplicate receipts collapse by stable key.

### Field 04 — Home visit
A home visit uses canonical site, mobility accommodation, weather window, caregiver, and safe-return condition.

### Field 05 — Cold or dry storage
Food, lyophilization, cryo-vault, and clinical-load owners supply preservation facts. Outreach only links their receipts.

### Field 06 — Delivery failure
The player sees absent, damaged, delayed, rejected, or misrouted supply and receives a safe alternative.

### Field 07 — Patient pacing
Needs and clinical owners can require rest, shorter route, caregiver, or reschedule.

### Field 08 — Caregiver teaching
Education returns lesson availability and receipt. A lesson is not treatment authority.

### Field 09 — Return reconciliation
Vehicle and inventory confirm delivered, returned, reserved, or unresolved items.

### Field 10 — Logistics closure
The case records delivery and care outcomes separately so a shipment is never mistaken for clinical success.
