## Pass 103 — Fields 11–20 after the 100k gate

The outreach packet has reached the second field layer. These fields deepen care continuity with provenance, consent, accessibility, operational tooling, and long-tail follow-up. They remain scaffolds until the current health, inventory, travel, relationship, save, and UI owners confirm the seam. No field creates an independent patient ledger or a hidden clinical decision path.

### Field 11 — Care fact provenance

Every symptom, referral, dose, and follow-up promise needs a provenance label that identifies observation, patient report, clinician assessment, settlement notice, or authored history. The label helps the player judge confidence and helps QA trace a surprising outcome. It is metadata on an existing fact, not a replacement for the health authority. The record stores source kind, source ID, deterministic time, confidence, and whether the source was reviewed. A save round trip preserves reviewed provenance and removes temporary observations when their owner expires them. Same-seed replay must produce the same ordering and labels.

### Field 12 — Consent and privacy cards

Consent cards explain what information may be shared, with whom, for what purpose, and until which condition. A card can cover a referral, a transport request, a household notification, or an anonymous public lesson. The player sees a plain-language summary and a detailed view, while the runtime checks the authored scope through the current relationship or journal owner. Withdrawal changes future sharing without rewriting the historical fact that consent was once granted. Tests cover missing consent, expired consent, withdrawn consent, and a save restored immediately before a scheduled expiry.

### Field 13 — Case conference tooling

A case conference is a short review action that gathers already-known facts into one decision surface. It does not diagnose through UI code. The conference view lists current symptoms, recent care, inventory availability, travel constraints, consent scope, and unresolved questions, each linked to its owner. Participants can recommend a next step, defer, or request another visit. The command route validates the decision in Core and emits a fact for the journal or care plan. A fixture proves that opening the conference has no mutation and that cancelling it leaves all patient state unchanged.

### Field 14 — Triage queue fairness

When several patients need the same scarce route or medicine, the queue needs visible ordering rules. Authored policy may consider urgency, travel time, prior promise, vulnerability, and consent, but the final ordering must be deterministic and inspectable. The panel shows why a case is ahead of another without exposing private details to the wrong audience. Queue state belongs to the existing outreach or settlement service owner. Tests seed tied cases, restore a save, and verify that stable tie-breaking never depends on dictionary order or host locale.

### Field 15 — Interpreter and caregiver support

Care can fail when a patient cannot understand a procedure or a caregiver cannot reach the clinic. This field adds authored support roles, preferred communication methods, availability windows, and a fallback request. It does not model real-world medical advice; it models fictional communication logistics. The UI makes the support need visible, offers an accessible alternate route, and records whether the player accepted, declined, or postponed help. Localization fixtures exercise long translated labels and right-to-left placeholders if those are supported by the current UI stack.

### Field 16 — Cold-chain route evidence

Some medicines require a stable transport condition. The route evidence record stores the item reference, required condition, departure and arrival facts, interruption reason, and final custody owner. Inventory remains authoritative for quantities and transfers; this field only explains whether a transfer met its authored handling rule. A degraded route produces a clear consequence and a repair or replacement path. Save tests cover a vehicle stop, a shelter handoff, a cancelled trip, and a reload at each boundary without duplicating the item stack.

### Field 17 — Rehabilitation goal ladder

Recovery after injury or exhaustion should offer goals that are observable and achievable over several visits. A goal record contains a baseline, a next milestone, a permitted support action, an interruption state, and a reflection prompt. Progress is derived from existing health, needs, activity, or relationship facts according to an authored rule. The player can pause a goal without losing context, and the record explains whether a setback changes the target or only the schedule. A deterministic fixture checks identical progress across two runs with the same activity sequence.

### Field 18 — Clinic staffing and fatigue

Mobile teams need staffing choices that create tradeoffs without becoming a second needs simulation. The staffing packet references existing character availability, travel, and fatigue facts, then exposes a bounded assignment command. The owner decides whether a route can depart and emits a reason when staffing is insufficient. The UI shows the next rest or handoff opportunity and never hides an unsafe shortage behind a disabled button. Performance checks cover a full settlement roster, event fan-out, and a clinic panel opened repeatedly during a long session.

### Field 19 — Follow-up promise ledger

A promise to return is a relationship and schedule fact that should remain meaningful after the immediate visit. The ledger stores who promised, the target case, the due condition, an allowed substitute, and the result of fulfilment or breach. It is routed through the current journal or campaign save owner and deduplicated by a stable promise ID. A reminder can appear in the travel or journal view, while the health panel only displays a linked status. Acceptance covers fulfilled, missed, transferred, and cancelled promises with clear text for each outcome.

### Field 20 — Outreach handoff matrix

The final field is a handoff matrix that links every outreach addition to its health, inventory, travel, relationship, consent, data, event, save, UI, test, and rollback seam. Empty cells mark design-only work or a blocker requiring a signed decision. The matrix is updated after each implementation slice and includes a patient-safety review note. It gives integrators a compact receipt that can be checked against current source instead of trusting plan volume. Closure requires an observable host route, a focused test, and evidence that no duplicate care authority was introduced.

The review receipt records owner evidence, data and runtime observations, focused verification, accessibility checks, and the follow-up outside this package.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Trace the player-visible question through data, runtime, save, UI, and narrative seams. Records use snake_case IDs, explicit versions, bounded values, resolvable references, and diagnostic failures. For **portable privacy archive**, the state ladder field must map pending, active, paused, complete, failed, expired, and replay transitions deterministically. Replay policy distinguishes resettable content from one-time history with retained completion evidence. Start with a current-source premise receipt and a bounded implementation claim. #### Field 6 — Accessibility

Frame the topic as a playable expansion whose facts remain with existing owners. Contrast, focus, scaling, remapping, reduced motion, and non-timed alternatives are acceptance requirements. Invalid input keeps context, explains correction, and preserves reviewed information. ## Wave 35 integration closeout receipt — Plan 2: Mobile Medical Outreach

**Closeout status:** documentation-only; READY FOR PREMISE AUDIT. This receipt does not claim implementation.

**Program role:** health, disease, medical ward, inventory, vehicle, expedition, consent, relationships, journal, and roster

**Primary owners:** health and disease, ward duty, inventory, vehicle, expedition, consent, relationship, journal, and roster owners

**Required delta:** a consent-aware outreach dispatch projection over an existing care result, with clear limits between transport, referral, supply handoff, and clinical treatment

**First safe slice:** one mobile referral packet that reads a current patient or settlement fact and routes an acknowledged, deferred, refused, or unresolved handoff

**Evidence anchors:** a folded triage card, a sealed medicine tin, a vehicle cot strap, and a message receipt marked by hand

**Observable signals:** triage freshness, consent age, medicine custody, travel delay, symptom uncertainty, and follow-up route

### Closeout boundary

The plan closes at the design boundary where one current owner can publish a fact, one consumer can display or consume it, one command can be issued through the owner, and one recovery path can return the player to a known state. The plan does not create a second ledger, registry, cache authority, save store, event bus, or presentation-owned counter. A row remains design-only until a current source search proves its consumer.

### Integration contract

The first receipt must identify the owner, public API, data file, save section or stateless proof, host route, focused tests, and rollback. It must exercise source age, stale input, duplicate delivery, interruption, correction, keyboard/controller parity, empty and error states, and one delayed content callback. The same seed and ordered inputs must reproduce the result across save, reload, host reopen, and duplicate event delivery.

### Content and failure gate

The first content slice uses clinic visits, supply escorts, family messages, missed appointments, privacy choices, and return-to-care callbacks. It includes discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, choice, quiet success, costly success, refusal, unresolved outcome, delayed callback, repeat policy, and retirement rule. It must stop safely for duplicated patient state, implied treatment, privacy leakage, medication double-spend, and unreachable referral branches. Prose can describe evidence and uncertainty but cannot create a gameplay fact.

### Handoff

**MUST PRESERVE:** existing authority, engine-free Core, JSON data authority, deterministic ordering, current save ownership, truthful UI, and active path claims.

**MUST ADD:** one premise receipt, one owner-bound slice, one validator-backed sample, one replay or stateless proof, one accessible route, one focused verification result, and one rollback note.

**MUST NOT DO:** duplicate state, revive retired architecture, claim runtime integration from document volume, or widen the catalog before reachability.

**NEXT ACTION:** run the bounded premise audit for the first safe slice and return the evidence to the integrator.
